in-progress, and planning stages.  He spoke about the completed projects,

Complex Entry Monument Sign: Ready to construct after receiving

addressing future needs and includes a strategic plan for the next 5-20

PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT SERVICES: 
 
a. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution
Number 01-2025, approving/denying an update to the Navajo County
Comprehensive Plan:
Cody Cooper provided clarification on the Navajo County Comprehensive
Plan update, explaining that the plan is not a regulatory document but
rather a guiding one. He indicated that it serves as a foundation for future
amendments and the adoption of regulatory documents, including those
related to renewable energy ordinances. He emphasized that while the
plan provides a pathway for these changes, it does not directly implement
regulations.
A presentation was shown. Terry Hogan, Consultant from Logan Simpson
Design, shared her appreciation for the collaboration with the county’s
planning and development team. She indicated that the team consisted of
experts in transportation, water resources, and economics, essential for
addressing various planning areas. She reviewed the purpose of the
comprehensive plan, which is required by state law for every Arizona
county, noting that the plan provides a blueprint for growth and
development, guiding coordinated, efficient, and sustainable growth while
conserving natural resources and promoting public welfare. She stated that
the plan is forward-looking, with the goal of aligning future development
with the community’s vision.  She outlined how the comprehensive plan
serves as the foundation for other planning tools like zoning codes and
subdivision regulations. She stated that the team worked on the entire
county, knowing that two-thirds of the county is in sovereign nations but
that there’s connectivity with roadways for open spaces, and coordinated
with tribal governments and incorporated cities to ensure compatibility with
their plans. She indicated that the process, lasting over 12 months,
involved six phases, including public engagement and feedback.  She
indicated that that the draft was reviewed during a 60-day public period,
and that the Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval.
She stated that if adopted, the plan would become effective immediately,
serving as the governing land use document for Navajo County.  She
reviewed the Public Participation Plan , indicating that it is a statutory
requirement and was presented to the board in March of last year. She
stated that it aligns with state regulations and the county’s existing public
participation efforts.  She spoke about the process and Strategy, noting
that the goal was to maximize exposure and gather public input, which
included setting up a project website that has had over 9,100 views and 74
  
                                                                    6 of 12 
DRAFT

<!-- page 11 -->
direct communication sign-ups. She indicated that a Comprehensive Plan
Committee (CPC) of experts was established to guide the process at key
milestones.  She spoke about community outreach, indicating that multiple
methods were employed to engage the community, including a community
questionnaire, in-person and virtual interviews, and eight in-person events
with over 900 participants. She stated that social media and press
releases helped publicize the process and encourage participation.  She
spoke about the public review, indicating that a 60-day public review period
was held, during which the plan was posted online, advertised through
various media, and open house meetings were held. She stated that
feedback was collected and reviewed, with most comments being
positive.  She reviewed the content of the plan, indicating that it addresses
nine key topics, including land use, transportation, economic growth,
housing, water, and energy with guiding principles and goals for each. She
stated that a future land use map and policies for future growth were
developed.  She spoke about implementation, indicating that while not
required by statute, an implementation plan has been included to help
guide the execution of the plan. She stated that it includes 87 action items
covering short-term, mid-term, and long-term goals.  She stated that the
project team recommends approval of the Navajo County 2050
Comprehensive Plan.
Supervisor Benally expressed dissatisfaction with the Comprehensive
Plan, specifically highlighting the exclusion of input from the Navajo Nation
and Hopi Tribe, which cover two-thirds of the county. She spoke about the
plan primarily focusing on wealth and development for towns and
municipalities while neglecting the rest of the county, leaving out vast areas
with Indigenous populations. She questioned the rush to push the plan
forward without involving these groups, raising concerns about the fairness
and inclusivity of the plan.
Cody Cooper acknowledged the concerns raised, explaining that the
comprehensive plan is limited by statutory authority, which excludes
sovereign nations from the process. He spoke about efforts to engage with
the Navajo Nation, conducting outreach to various chapters and community
representatives, noting that despite reaching out to 40-50 entities,
feedback was limited. He indicated that they had done their best within the
legal constraints of their planning authority.
Chairman Whiting inquired if the plan only applies to areas within the
county's statutory authority, excluding cities or incorporated areas, as they
cannot plan for those regions.
Mr. Cooper confirmed that the plan only governs unincorporated,
non-reservation areas of the county, as towns are required to create their
own plans. He indicated that there is ongoing collaboration with towns,
cities, and neighboring counties to ensure consistency and compliance
with legal requirements. He spoke about Winslow doing their General
Plan, noting that they reached out to the County for the a 60-day review
period, which allowed the county to provide feedback and address any
potential conflicts between their plans. He stated that the county continues
to collaborate with all agencies within its authority but cannot regulate
anything outside the unincorporated areas.
Supervisor Benally expressed frustration that the Navajo Nation was not
properly involved in the planning process, despite the claim of reaching out
                                                                    7 of 12 
DRAFT

<!-- page 12 -->
to all jurisdictions. She criticized the exclusion of the two-thirds of Navajo
County covered by sovereign nations, stating that the county's plans seem
to prioritize certain areas while neglecting others. She spoke of a
constituent's perception of prejudice in the area and felt the county was not
being inclusive in its approach, despite claiming the plan was
comprehensive.
Supervisor Peshlakai expressed his appreciation for the comprehensive
plan and the efforts behind it, acknowledging the differences between
county and tribal planning processes. He explained that the county's plan
focuses on land use, infrastructure, and economic growth within county
boundaries, while tribal nations prioritize cultural preservation,
self-determination, and economic development within their sovereign
lands. He clarified that tribal nations are not bound by state regulations in
the same way as counties, which operate under state authority. He noted
that tribal nations receive federal funding for community planning, unlike
counties, which rely on local taxes.
 
10:26 a.m. Supervisor Peshlakai stepped out of the meeting.
 
Supervisor Seymore expressed gratitude for staff's hard work in
developing the comprehensive plan, emphasizing its importance for future
community growth, zoning, and economic sustainability. He spoke about
the plan's potential to guide the county's development over the next 20-30
years, addressing challenges like population decline and shifts in the
economy. He commended the plan as a necessary update, noting the
county's last comprehensive plan was in 2004, and it was only recently
revised to remain compliant. He acknowledged that while the plan isn't
perfect, it provides a strong foundation for growth and will be refined over
time through regulations and ordinances.
 
10:30 a.m. Supervisor Peshlakai returned to the meeting.
Chairman Whiting opened the Public Hearing. There being no comments,
the Public Hearing was closed. 
 
Vice-Chair Whitesinger asked for clarification on the approval process
and inquired about the procedure for making amendments or modifications
to the plan if needed in the future, specifically in the context of the
recommendation to review the plan every 10 years.
Mr. Cooper explained that, by state law, the comprehensive plan must be
updated or readopted every 10 years, but that the plan is a "living
document," meaning it can be amended or modified earlier if significant
trends or shifts are identified. He indicated that any changes would follow
a process similar to the one already completed, allowing for updates as
needed at the local level.
Vice-Chair Whitesinger expressed appreciation for the effort and
professionalism in developing the comprehensive plan, highlighting its
importance in meeting state requirements and its impact on local
communities. She commended the outreach efforts to educate the public
about the plan's significance and its potential effects on property, land, and
future projects. She acknowledged the importance of considering

Chairman Whiting thanked staff for the efforts made to connect with

PUBLIC WORKS:
 
a. Presentation of Navajo County's Waste Tire Program and notification of
the receipt of the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ)
Voluntary Environmental Stewardship Program (VESP) Bronze Award :
A presentation was shown.  Madhav Mundle stated that Navajo County
received the VESP Bronze Award from ADEQ for maintaining sustained
compliance with environmental laws for three consecutive years,
recognizing the county's waste tire program. He stated that the program,
managed by Navajo County Public Works in collaboration with ADEQ,
involves two tire collection sites in Holbrook and Show Low. He indicated
that the county also organizes community cleanups and works with a
contractor to haul and dispose of tires, noting that in fiscal year 2024, over
54,000 tires were collected. He stated that the program is funded by the
state, with annual funding varying but typically exceeding $210,000. He
indicated that the county's outreach includes informational materials
available on their website.
A presentation was shown.  Manny Bowler, Community Liaison for Navajo,
Apache, and Gila counties, spoke about Navajo County's waste tire
program, which received the VESP Bronze Award for sustained
compliance with environmental laws. She stated that this recognition is
part of the Voluntary Environmental Stewardship Program (VESP), created
by the Arizona State Legislature. She indicated that the program
encourages organizations to improve their environmental practices, with
recognition levels ranging from Copper to Platinum, noting that Navajo
County's tire program caught up on six years of overdue reporting and has
maintained compliance. She praised the county's efforts, noting that the
program has become a model for other areas, including Apache County,
where tire disposal options are limited. She thanked the county for its
continued support of waste tire disposal events. 
 
  
b. Consideration of an Intergovernmental Agreement with the State of   
                                                                    9 of 12

b. Consideration of an Intergovernmental Agreement with the State of
Arizona, Department of Transportation for the Silver Creek Drive and Silver
Lake Boulevard Crossing :
Madhav Mundle stated that Navajo County received funding through AZ
Smart Funds for the design of a bridge replacement project in District 3,
specifically in the White Mountain Lakes Community. He indicated that the
project would involve designing a new bridge over Rocky Arroyo and
creating a new storm drain crossing at Silver Lake Boulevard. He stated
that Public Works applied for and secured $890,000 for the design phase,
which will be administered by ADOT. He indicated that the project aims to
improve access and infrastructure in the area. He noted that they would
apply for separate funding to do the construction work.  He stated that staff
requests approval of the IGA.
 
Chairman Whiting inquired about the plan for managing traffic disruptions
during construction, emphasizing the importance of minimizing the impact
on the public and ensuring smooth traffic flow during the project.
Mr. Mundle confirmed that managing traffic disruptions will be a key
consideration during the project, assuring that access to the community
will not be cut off and that detour routes will be planned. He indicated that
the goal is to avoid impacting both routes simultaneously, ensuring the
community's access is maintained during construction, which will be
addressed as part of the design and development phase, focusing on
traffic maintenance.
Chairman Whiting encouraged them to communicate effectively with the
public about the upcoming construction, including timelines and alternative
routes.
 
Vice-Chair Whitesinger made a motion to approve an Intergovernmental
Agreement with the State of Arizona, Department of Transportation for the
Silver Creek Drive and Silver Lake Boulevard Crossing, motion seconded
by Supervisor Peshlakai.  Vote unanimous approving the motion.

COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney
and Board members :
Supervisor Seymore thanked Chairman Whiting and Vice-Chairman Benally 
for their leadership in the past year. He spoke about the tragic loss of life in
California and reflected on the continuing risks and challenges faced in the White
Mountains region. He shared an inspirational story from a friend who overcame
adversity after being released from prison, emphasizing the importance of
freedom, faith, and rebuilding in times of loss. He encouraged setting goals for
personal growth and resilience in the new year.
Supervisor Benally spoke about her attendance at the local Veterans'
organization and Chapter meetings.  She indicated that she attended the
inauguration of officials in the Western and Chinle Agencies, noting that she has
several chapters in both areas. She spoke about her attendance at the holiday
events at the Veterans organizations and Chapters in her area.
Vice-Chair Whitesinger recognizing the Sheriff's Department for their
professionalism as the honor guard at Deputy Cockings’ funeral and expressed
condolences to his family. She spoke about the recent fires in California, noting the
lessons in compassion and the importance of addressing urban-interface fires. She
emphasized the need for communities to work together in fire mitigation efforts and
acknowledged the widespread impact of the fires, which have caused
unprecedented devastation.
Chairman Whiting expressed concern about the upcoming fire season,
emphasizing the importance of preparation and praying for rain. He thanked the
Board for their trust and acknowledge the genuine care they show for their
constituents. He reflected on attending Deputy Cockings’ funeral and expressed
appreciation for the emotional and supportive gestures observed, particularly from
Supervisor Whitesinger. He spoke about the value of kindness, grace, and
assuming positive intent in interactions with others, encouraging everyone to
support each other and remain accountable as they move into 2025.

INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN                                                                                                                     
THE NA V AJO NATION                                                                                                                                                             
AND                                                                                                                                                                                        
THE NA V AJO COUNTY , ARIZONA                                                                                                                       
DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS 
 
This Intergovernmental Agreement ("IGA'') is entered into as of this ___ day of _   by and 
between the Navajo Nation, through the Navajo-Hopi Land Commission Office, hereinafter referred to as 
the "Nation," and Navajo County, a political subdivision of the State of Arizona, through its Department of 
Public Works, hereinafter referred mas "Navajo County."  
WHEREAS, the Nation has established the Navajo- Hopi Land Commission Office for the 
administration and utilization of the Navajo Rehabilitation Trust Fund, as authorized by the Navajo-Hopi 
Land Commission, to improve the economic, educational, and social conditions of the families and Navajo 
communities affected by the Healing decision, the provisions of Public Law 93-531, as Amended, and the 
establishment of District Six as exclusively Hopi Land; and  
WHEREAS, Navajo County supports the Nation, BIA, and Navajo Department of Transportation 
through its Department of Public Works in the maintenance of public roadways and related transportation 
structures within the unincorporated areas of the county under the jurisdiction of its Board of Supervisors; 
and  
WHEREAS, it is the mutual desire of the Nation and Navajo County to achieve their goals and 
work in harmony for the common purpose of protecting the public health, safety, and welfare of the people 
of the Nation residing in Navajo County through a cooperative relationship between the parties; and  
WHEREAS, each party to this IGA respects the sovereign status of the other and wishes to 
establish procedures to fully implement the government- to-government relationship with respect to 
transportation projects of mutual interest and benefit. In recognition of the sovereign status of the Nation, 
Navajo County respects the Nation's government, values, cultures, and laws; and  
WHEREAS, Navajo County has authority to enter into this IGA and participate in transportation 
projects of mutual interest and benefit with the Nation pursuant to the laws of the State of Arizona, 
specifically A.R.S. § 11-952; and  
WHEREAS, the Nation has authority, as a sovereign nation, to enter into this IGA and participate 
in transportation projects of mutual interest and benefit with Navajo County; and 
WHEREAS, the Nation granted Navajo County $265,667.35 from the Navajo Rehabilitation Trust 
Fund for the purpose of conducting road maintenance and improvements on the Navajo Nation pursuant to 
an agreement entered on November 10, 2016 and that agreement expired on November 10, 2023. 
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties hereby agree to the following: 
I. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES 
 
A. The purpose of this IGA is to authorize Navajo County to continue using the remaining funds 
previously granted to it from the Navajo Rehabilitation Trust Fund  for the purpose of  
conducting road maintenance and improvements on the Navajo Nation. 
 
B. The parties mutually agree that this IGA is intended to encourage consultation and

<!-- page 19 -->
cooperation with one another on transportation projects of mutual interest and benefit, 
particularly projects that support the mission and objectives of the Navajo -Hopi Land 
Commission Office. 
 
C. The parties will work together to find funding sources that help further the objectives of the    
 Nation and improve the roads utilized by the relocatees. 
Il.  RESPONSIBILITIES 
A.     Navajo County shall do the following: 
1.  Use funds previously received from the Navajo Rehabilitation Trust Fund under the 
agreement entered on November 10, 2016 to conduct road maintenance and 
improvement within the following six (6) Chapters identified by the Nation: 
Birdsprings, Dilkon, Indian Wells, Jeddito, Teesto, and White Cone. 
2.  Maintain the funds in a unique account. All funds remaining at the end of three (3) years 
will be returned to the Nation. 
3.  Utilize the BIA, Navajo County, or NDOT for labor, equipment, and material applied 
on the selected roads. 
4. Complete road maintenance and improvement activities pursuant to the Budget 
incorporated herein and attached as Exhibit "A." 
5.  Provide a quarterly financial report t o the Nation via mail, showing the account status 
and identifying expenditures for the quarterly report. 
6.  Provide on a bi-annual basis a project status and financial report to the Nation. 
B.     The Nation shall do the following: 
1.  Allow Navajo County to retain the remainder of the funds previously received from the 
Navajo Rehabilitation Trust Fund under the agreement entered on November 10, 2016 
for road maintenance and improvement within the following six (6) Chapters identified 
by the Nation: Birdsprings, Dilkon, Indian Wells, Jeddito, Teesto, and White Cone for a 
duration of 3 years from the date this IGA is fully executed. 
3.   Review reports submitted by Navajo County on a quarterly basis. 
III. TERMS OF AGREEMENT 
A.   Designated Contact Person. The primary points of contact for carrying out the purposes     
  and objectives of this IGA and supplying copies of all correspondence, reports, and    
  invoices, shall be: 
 
  Navajo-Hopi Land Commission Office  
  ATTN: Deputy Director  
  PO Box 2549  
  Window Rock, Arizona 86515  
 
  Navajo County Department of Public Works  
  ATTN: Director 
 Madhav Mundle

<!-- page 20 -->
PO Box 668 
Holbrook, Arizona 85901                                                                                                                           
  
B.   Meetings. The primary contacts as described herein, and selected members of their staff,    
  will meet at least bi-annually to review the project status and to identify and seek to     
  remove obstacles impairing the achievement of the transportation-related goals,   
  objectives, and tasks. 
 
C.   Location of Improvements. The selection of roads to be improved will be determined by  
  NDOT, the BIA, and the six Chapters identified herein. 
 
D. No Waiver. In executing this IGA, neither the Nation nor Navajo County waives any rights, 
including but not limited to: treaty rights, immunities, sovereign immunities, jurisdictional 
defenses, or defenses based on their protecting laws. Specifically, nothing in this IGA shall be 
construed as a waiver of sovereign immunity by the Navajo Nation, consent to be sued, or 
consent to jurisdiction of any federal or state court. Nothing in this IGA creates, implies, nor 
should be construed to create any right of ac tion by either party against the other, or in any 
third party. The acceptance of performance, or failure to object to, any breach, default, or 
failure of performance, under the terms of this IGA shall not constitute a waiver of the right 
to demand performance as specified in the IGA. 
 
E. Agreement to Work in Good Faith. In good faith, the County manager, Director of Public  
Works, and other Navajo County employees, in their official capacities or through their  
designees, shall endeavor to implement the terms of this IGA. 
 
F.   Dispute Resolution. All disputes and controversies regarding this IGA shall be resolved by    
  the Director of the Navajo-Hopi Land Commission Office and the Director of Navajo  
  County's Department of Public Works. If these officials are unable to resolve the dispute or  
  controversy, the officials listed below may participate in the resolution. 
  
 Navajo Nation Official:  
 
 Navajo County Official: Bryan Layton, Navajo County Manager  
 
G. Liability. Navajo County agrees to hold harmless and indemnify the Nation against any 
and all losses, costs, damages, claims, accident or injury to person or property including 
death, attorneys’ fees, expenses, and other liability whatsoever (collectively, “Claims”), 
arising under, related to, or in connection with this IGA , except to the extent such 
claims are directly caused by the gross negligence or wanton and willful conduct of the 
Nation or to the extent they result from the negligence of Nation officials or employees 
as provided for and in accordance with 1 N.N.C. §551 et seq. The Nation is responsible 
for the maintenance and upkeep of the work completed at the conclusion of the project. 
Navajo County does not assume any responsibility for liability for the continuing 
maintenance and upkeep of the work completed under this IGA. 
 
H.   Modifications. Any modifications to this IGA shall be made only by written amendment,  
  signed and executed by all parties.

<!-- page 21 -->
I. Availability of Funds. The liability of the Nation under this IGA is contingent on the 
availability of funds pursuant to 2 N.N.C. §223 (A) and (B). 
 
J. Applicable Law and Jurisdiction. Navajo County shall comply with all Navajo 
Nation laws, as they may be amended from time to time, including, but not limited to, 
the Navajo Preference in Employment Act, 15 N.N.C. §601 et seq., the Navajo Nation 
Business Opportunity Act, 5 N.N.C. §201 et seq., and applicable regulations. This IGA 
shall be governed by the laws of the Navajo Nation. Matters not addressed by Navajo 
Nation law may be decided by reference to the laws of the State of Arizona. Jurisdiction 
shall be solely in the courts of the Navajo Nation.
 
 
I V. DURATION AND TERMINATION OF AGREEMENT 
A. This IGA shall become effective when signed by both parties and shall continue in force for 
three (3) years  from the date both parties’  sign. Termination may be initiated by either party 
after thirty (30) day written notice to the other party of its intention to terminate. 
 
B. The Nation may terminate this IGA at any time if the work or services provided by Navajo 
County are not satisfactory, if Navajo County should default on any provision within this IGA, 
or if Navajo County fails to submit required reports and other documents as required within the 
defined time schedules. 
 
C. If this IGA is terminated prior to its expiration, Navajo County shall immediately return all 
remaining funds to the Nation. 
 
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the duly authorized officials of the parties have executed this IGA on the dates 
affixed by their signatures, with the effected date as stated above.

A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS, CANCELLING THE ELECTIONS FOR 
TIMBERLAND ACRES DWID; AND APPOINTING THE CANDIDATE(S) OR DEEMING THE POSITION VACANT, 
PURSUANT TO ARS § 48-1012 (E) 
 
 
 
WHEREAS, ARS § 48-1012 (E) provides as follows with respect to Domestic Water Improvement District Board of 
Directors positions: 
 
“If only one person files or no person files a nominating petition for election to fill a position on the board of directors 
of the district, the county board of supervisors, by resolution, may cancel the election for that office and appoint the person 
who filed the nominating petition to fill that position. If no person files a nominating petition for an election to fill a district 
board office, the county board of supervisors, by resolution, may cancel the election for those offices and those offices are 
deemed vacant and shall be filled as otherwise provided by law. A person who is appointed pursuant to this section is fully 
vested with the powers and duties of the office as if elected to that office.” 
 
         and 
 
WHEREAS, A.R.S. § 16-410 (A) authorizes the Board to take such action no earlier than one hundred and five 
(105) days before the election, and it is now less than one hundred and five (105) days before March 12th 2024 Special 
Election at which the Domestic Water Improvement Districts Board of Directors will be elected; 
 
         and 
 
WHEREAS, the officer in charge of elections, has certified that the number of persons who filed nominating 
petitions to fill the Domestic Water Improvement Districts Board of Directors positions is less than or equal to the number of 
positions available, attached hereto and incorporated herein as “Exhibit A”; 
 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Supervisors as follows:  
That the elections for the Timberland Acres DWID board member positions, attached hereto and incorporated 
herein as “Exhibit A”, are hereby cancelled and appointed by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors.

Title: White Mountain Apache Tribe Crosswalk Striping Partnership
Submitted By: Nicole Reske, Tribal Government Relations Liaison
Department: Administrative Services
Presented By: Nicole Reske
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Task Agreement between the White Mountain Apache Tribe Division of
Transportation and Navajo County to reimburse for crosswalk re-striping. 
Background:
The White Mountain Apache Tribe Division of Transportation requested Navajo County for assistance
on the crosswalk re-striping project at the intersection of East Fatco Road and Fat County Road. This
particular crosswalk was chosen due to safety concerns about the lack of visibility for the White
Mountain Apache Timber Company employees who use it daily. WMAT DOT would like to restripe the
crosswalk to increase visibility, as well as remove excessive soil and plant build-up on the asphalt's
surface prior to sealing. This would be the first Task Agreement under the Memorandum of Agreement
that went into effect on November 15th, 2024.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval.

Task Agreement No. 1
White Mountain Apache Tribe – Division of Transportation
Fatco Road Crosswalk Striping Project
On January 28th, 2025, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors by motion, approved the expenditure of
up to $4,000.00 from the Highway User Revenue Fund (HURF) allocated to Navajo County District V for
the expenditure on transportation related projects. Through the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with
the White Mountain Apache Tribe, Division of Transportation (WMAT DOT) the County has agreed to
reimburse, up to four thousand dollars for assistance in re-striping of two crosswalks and other related
work at the intersection of East Fatco Road & Fat County Road. A detailed Scope of Work (SOW) is
described in the attached Memorandum from WMAT DOT, dated January 13, 2025.
The WMAT DOT will follow their adopted policy(s) and process(es) to identify and hire a contractor to
complete the work as outlined in the attached Memorandum.  All work related to the project will be
overseen and directed by the WMAT DOT.  Upon satisfactory completion of the project and the invoice
paid, the WMAT DOT will submit a receipt to the County for reimbursement.  All funds approved by this
Task Agreement shall be expended before June 30, 2025.
The WMAT DOT warrants and represents that the materials purchased with the Allocated Funds will be
used for maintenance activities on roads within Navajo County, which are open to the public and eligible
for the expenditure of HURF monies under the Arizona Constitution and related Arizona Revised
Statutes. The WMAT DOT agree to fully cooperate in any audit of the Allocated Funds by the Arizona
Auditor General. For any material acquired in whole or in part with the Allocated Funds, the acquiring
party shall be solely responsible for all expenses of storing and installing the infrastructure. The County
shall have no responsibility or liability whatsoever regarding such material. The Tribe shall be responsible
for identifying, prioritizing, scheduling, and performing all activities for which the Allocated Funds are
used in whole or in part. It is understood that the County’s sole obligation hereunder is to make payment
of the Allocated Funds.
The Allocated Funds under this agreement shall be paid by Navajo County directly to the invoicing party
upon the County’s receipts of invoices or billing statement that show the items have been purchased and
approved by the Tribe. The total of all invoices shall not exceed the approved amount in this Agreement.
TERMINATION OF TASK AGREEMENT: This Task Agreement may be terminated at any time by
mutual written consent, or by the County, with or without cause, upon giving thirty (30) days’ written
notice.  The County, at its’ convenience, by written notice, may terminate this Contract, in whole or in
part.  If this Contract is terminated, the County shall be liable only for payment under the payment
provisions of this Contact for services rendered and accepted material received by the County before the
effective date of termination.
The request for payment of invoices along with an approved invoice from Tribe will be sent to:

Title: MOA BIA Ft Apache and NC Road Related Activites
Submitted By: Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Administrative Services
Presented By: Nicole Reske
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Memorandum of Agreement between the Bureau of Indian Affairs, Fort Apache
Agency Transportation Department and Navajo County for road related maintenance activities. 
Background:
The Fort Apache Bureau of Indian Affairs has helped support the White Mountain Apache Tribe with
road maintenance while the Tribe works on further developing their own Division of Transportation to
accommodate the needs on the reservation. The Fort Apache BIA had previously signed a Memorandum
of Agreement with Navajo County in 2010, which has since expired. The Government Relations Team
worked over the course of the past year to reaffirm the relationship with both our federal and tribal
government partners to support our Navajo County residents. This MOA allows the County to assist the
Fort Apache BIA through partnership in supplying or transporting materials for projects, providing
project planning assistance, and assisting in road repair or maintenance activities if agreed upon by the
Board of Supervisors. Additional projects may be written into an Agreement and added to this MOA by
the authorized representatives of participating parties and shall be governed by the terms of this MOA.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval.

Board of Supervisors Regular 4. c.        
Meeting Date: 01/28/2025  
Title: Navajo County Design & Construction Standards
Submitted For: William Flake, Assistant County Engineer 
Submitted By: William Flake, Assistant County Engineer
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Will Flake
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 02-2025 approving the Navajo County Design &
Construction Standards & Specifications Manual to provide standards, specifications, and guidelines that
complement and support the County Ordinances and Regulations.
Background:
The Navajo County Design & Construction Standards & Specifications Manual (Manual) has been
developed to establish a comprehensive set of standards, specifications, and guidelines that complement
and support the County’s existing ordinances and regulations. This Manual provides design professionals,
developers, contractors, and County staff with the necessary technical direction for preparing construction
documents involving the installation or construction of public and private infrastructure. It is intended to
promote public safety and health while balancing affordability and supporting innovative design and
construction practices. By offering clear and consistent guidance, the Manual aims to facilitate uniformity
in the plan preparation process while accommodating sound engineering judgment and creative
approaches that protect public welfare.
This Manual serves as a supplement to existing County plans, ordinances, and regulations, including the
Comprehensive, Transportation, and Area Plans; Subdivision Regulations; Zoning Ordinances; Flood
Plain Regulations; and more. It has been carefully crafted to satisfy the requirements of the Arizona
Revised Statutes, ensuring proper regulation of land subdivision while providing a clear and user-friendly
framework for property owners and developers. Governed by its principles, all projects within the
unincorporated areas of Navajo County will benefit from improved clarity and consistency in design and
construction processes, enhancing the quality and safety of development throughout the County.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of the Resolution adopting the Navajo County Design & Construction
Standards & Specifications Manual.

Design & Construction Standards & Specifications Manual 
  
January 2025 iii  
Foreword 
The Navajo County Design and Construction Manual provides guidance to the public, 
developers, and design engineers on how new public roadways are to be designed and 
constructed within the County. This document is based on national and local experience 
and recommended practice. It represents a compilation of information and draws heavily 
from the Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) design manuals and guidelines; 
Maricopa County, Arizona Design Manual s; publications of the American Association of 
State Highway and Transportation Officials; the Institute of Transportation Engineers; and 
the American Society of Civil Engineers. 
 
This Manual has been formatted so that changes and updates to individual procedures 
can be made without the need to reproduce the entire document. Recipients of this 
Manual should maintain their copy by inserting procedure updates and discarding dated 
material. Navajo County will provide updates to holders of this Manual on an as needed 
basis. Please contact the Navajo County Public Works Department at the following 
address to obtain additional copies of this Manual, or to subscribe to Manual Updates. 
 
Contact: Navajo County Public Works Department 
100 W Public Works Drive 
Holbrook, AZ 86025 
Telephone: (928) 524-4100 
 
Website:  Navajo County, AZ | Official Website (navajocountyaz.gov)

100 General Conditions and Requirements 
 
101 Purpose and Intent 
The purpose of the D esign & Construction Standards & Specifications  
(Manual) is to provide standards , sp ecifications, and guidelines that 
complement and support the County Ordinances and Regulations. This 
Manual will provide both general information and specific design 
standards to design professionals who are preparing development 
construction documents that include or  involve the installation or 
construction of public or private infrastructure. 
 
The intent of this Manual is to promote public safety and health while, at 
the same time, assuring reasonable economy for affordable development. 
In addition, this Manual aims to present clear and concise direction 
regarding technical requirements, policie s, and process to facilitate 
consistent uniform design during the plan preparation phase. However, 
the information presented is not intended to supersede sound engineering 
judgement. Accordingly, creative, innovative, or cost -reducing use of 
materials, system design or construction practices may be accepted by 
the County plan review personnel upon finding that public welfare is duly 
protected. 
 
Proposed variances from this Manual must be submitted  to the County 
and approved before the project design is finalized. In the event of 
differences between this Manual and the scope of work or provisions of 
an executed County design contract, the executed contract shall govern. 
 
It is anticipated that the primary users of this Manual will be private parties, 
consulting engineers, developers, contractors, public utilities, and County 
staff. 
 
102 Legal Authority 
This Manual is not intended  to interfere with, repeal or do away with law 
or right, or annul any other ordinance, rule or regulation, statute, or other 
provision of law except as provided in this Manual. Where any provision 
of this Manual imposes restrictions different from those im posed by any 
other provision of law, the provision that is more restrictive or imposes 
higher standards upon the development and use of land shall control.

102.1 County Code, Ordinances and Regulations 
The purpose of this Manual is to satisfy the requirements of Arizona 
Revised Statutes, which requires the County to regulate the subdivision 
of all lands. This Manual is adopted as a guidance document that has 
been carefully crafted to clearly outline meth ods, procedures, and 
requirements for the use of property owners and subdividers in 
subdividing land within the County. 
 
This Manual is a supplement to the requirements in the Comprehensive, 
Transportation and Area Plans; Subdivision Regulations; Building 
Information; Zoning Ordinances; Flood Plain Regulations and 
Ordinances; and other regulations for land development within the 
County.  
 
This Manual shall govern all projects within the unincorporated County 
limits. 
 
102.2 Applicability 
This Manual is applicable to projects constructing public and private 
infrastructure (i.e. public streets and facilities or private facilities installed 
by a Public Utility or Franchisee, etc.) within dedicated public Right -of-
Way (R/W) or easements. 
 
This Manual applies to rural and urban roadways except for freeways and 
freeway-type improvements. In these latter cases, the current applicable 
standards of the Arizona Department of Transportation shall apply.  
  
This Manual generally does not apply to resurfacing, restoration, or 
rehabilitation (3R) projects, minor improvement program (MIP) projects, 
or maintenance projects. These projects aim to extend the pavement 
structure's usable life or keep the facility operating in its as-built condition. 
Design standards have evolved over the years, and bringing previously 
constructed facilities into conformity with current standards is not always 
feasible. For clarification, consult with the County.  
  
The County must review and approve all engineering plans, 
specifications, and documents for public works improvements and private 
improvements which require County authorization or permits.

All work on property owned or controlled by the County shall require an 
Encroachment Permit. Private development work within the County’s 
jurisdiction may be conveyed by the plat process. Inspections of the 
construction of public and private improvements by the County and written 
acceptance of the construction by the County is required for all County 
permitted work. 
 
102.3 Severability 
If any part of this Manual, as approved by the County Engineer, shall be 
found invalid, all other parts shall remain in effect. 
 
The County Engineer may incorporate minor changes to this Manual as 
they become necessary.  
 
103 County Road System 
The County Road System includes  approximately 720 miles of roads. 
These roads are maintained by preventing, reducing, and restoring 
deterioration of the roadway infrastructure through road surface and 
roadway structure maintenance and preservation activities. 
 
Before the County accepts a road into the County Road System for 
maintenance, it shall meet the standards contained in this Manual. If field 
conditions change after plan approval, improvements shall be made, as 
necessary, to bring the transportation facilities up to these standards.  
 
For the purposes of this Manual, the following definitions for maintenance, 
preservation, rehabilitation/reconstruction, and construction shall be used: 
• Roadway maintenance is defined as any work that is performed 
to maintain the condition of the roadway or to respond to specific 
conditions or events that create a need to restore the roadway to a 
functional state of operation. 
• Roadway preservation is defined as any work that is planned and 
performed to improve or sustain the condition of the roadway in a 
state of good repair. Preservation activities generally do not add 
capacity or structural value but do restore the overall condition of 
the roadway. 
• Roadway rehabilitation or reconstruction is defined as any work 
that extends the service life of existing roadways either by restoring 
or reconstructing the pavement surface. Such work may include 
scarifying and mixing deteriorated pavement structure into a

• Roadway construction is defined as any work that changes the 
geometric prism or surface type of the roadway or completely 
removes and replaces the existing pavement structure. Such work 
may include roadway widening, overlays greater than two inches in 
thickness, major drainage improvements , safety improvements, 
and signing and marking. 
 
New roads or other public improvements will only be considered for 
acceptance if they have direct access to another County-maintained Road 
or another road that is maintained by a government entity.  
 
104 Project Classifications 
A Guidance Flowchart for Applicability of this Manual to a  proposed 
project is shown in Figure 104.1 
 
104.1 Capital Improvement Projects 
Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) are projects that are installed as part 
of a Capital Improvement Plan. CIP projects are typically County funded 
projects, usually inside the public Right-of-Way, that are managed by the 
County and designed by private engi neering consultants. Ultimately, 
design services and construction of a CIP project are awarded by the 
County. 
 
104.2 Development Projects 
Development projects are projects with construction improvements that 
are to be installed as part of new land development. Requirements are 
outlined in this Manual as well as the County codes, ordinances, and 
regulations. Refer to the Planning & Developmen t Services website for 
specific information regarding the processes. The website includes the 
applications, permits and checklists outlining each step in the process. 
 
104.3 Utility Projects 
This manual shall apply to every new placement of a utility and every 
planned, non -emergency replacement of existing utility poles, 
underground facilities, and other utility system structures within the 
County right -of-way. Every effort shall be made to me et the standards 
during emergency replacements.

105 References 
All references in this Manual  shall be to the editions or versions of 
documents in effect at the time a complete permit application is accepted 
by the County unless a Developer is otherwise vested by applicable law. 
When a publication is specified, it refers to the most recent date of issues, 
including interim publications, unless a specific date or year of issue is 
provided.  
 
105.1 Comprehensive Plan 
The purpose of a Comprehensive Plan is to guide and accomplish 
coordinated, adjusted, and harmonious development of the County, 
pursuant to the present and future needs of the County. The County’s 
Comprehensive (Plan) has been developed to conserve the County’s 
natural resources, ensure efficient expenditure of public monies, and 
promote the health, safety, convenience, and general welfare of the 
public. 
 
Developers and Professional Engineers shall review the Comprehensive 
Plan to assure their proposed construction improvements reflect and 
implement the goals and policies outlined in the Comprehensive Plan. 
 
105.2 Transportation Plan or Study 
The purpose of a transportation plan or study is to develop multi -modal, 
multi-jurisdictional transportation plan that outlines the region’s 
transportation priority projects and provides a plan for ultimate 
implementation. The County’s Transportation (Study)Plan is focused 
around identifying regional mobility needs that can accommodate the 
anticipated future population and employment growth. 
 
Developers and Professional Engineers shall review the Study 
Transportation Plan to assure their proposed construction improvements 
reflect and implement the goals and policies outlined therein.  
 
See Chapter 400 for discussion on Federal Functional Classifications. 
 
105.3 Area Plans 
The purpose of an area plan is a stand -alone document that further 
defines the County’s planning policies, objectives, and goals for specific 
areas within the County. An area plan builds on the overall goals 
presented in the Comprehensive Plan.

105.4 Zoning Ordinances 
The purpose of zoning ordinances is to implement the Comprehensive 
Plan. 
 
105.5 Subdivision Regulations 
The County Subdivision Regulations can be found on the County’s 
Planning & Development Services website. 
 
105.6 Permit Applications and Process 
County Permit Applications and Process are a series of documents which 
are to be utilized through the planning process. The Developer/Engineer 
shall utilize these documents for guidance on submittal requirements and 
ensure that adequate information is provided for reviews. 
 
105.6.1 Other Permits 
Permits from controlling Federal, State, or County Agencies are required 
prior to the issuance of construction permits by the County.  
 
Arizona permits are required prior to the issuance of construction permits 
by the County, including but not limited to: 
• Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) for any work 
performed in State rights-of-way. 
• Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), Arizona 
Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (AZPDES), Construction 
Activity General Permit (GCP) is required prior to approval of 
construction plans. 
• Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) approval to 
construct both water and sewer systems must be obtained prior to 
approval of construction plans and prior to issuance of County 
permits. 
• See the ADEQ website for additional  information on permits that 
may be required. 
 
U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) controls pollution (noise, air, 
water, sewage). Permits from controlling Federal Agencies are required 
prior to the issuance of construction permits by the County, including but 
not limited to: 
• U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) controls all work affecting 
“The Waters of the United States”.

106 Definitions 
All words in this Manual shall be first defined  as provided herein and, if 
not defined herein, shall be defined as in the Zoning Ordinances, 
Subdivision Regulations or according to the customary dictionary 
definition. Words used in the present tense include the future tense; words 
used in singular incl ude plural, and words used in plural include the 
singular; the words “shall” and “must” are always mandatory; the word 
“person” includes a firm, association, organization, partnership, trust, 
corporation, company, and/or an individual. 
 
Asphalt:  A commonly utilized surface for roads and parking areas, known 
as Asphaltic Concrete Pavement, is a type of paved roadway. 
 
Base Flood: The flood having a 1% chance of being equaled or exceeded 
in any given year i.e., the 100 -year flood as defined by the Federal 
Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) or the effective Flood Insurance 
Study (FIS) for the County.

Basin, Detention: A storm water storage facility that temporarily stores 
surface runoff and releases it at a controlled rate through a positive outlet. 
A detention basin and park may be joined to serve both recreational needs 
and as a water storage facility. 
 
Basin, Drainage: A geographical area that contributes surface runoff to 
a particular concentration point. The terms “drainage basin,” “tributary 
area” and “watershed” are used interchangeably. 
 
Basin, Retention : A storm water storage facility that stores surface 
runoff. Stored water is infiltrated into the subsurface or released to the 
downstream drainage system or watercourse (via gravity outlet or pump) 
or evaporated after the storm event. A retention basin and  park may be 
joined to serve both recreational needs and as a water storage facility. 
 
Berm: An earthen mound, either natural or man-made. 
 
Bicycle Lane:  A paved area located within a street right -of-way and 
between the curbs that is designated for bicycle or other non -motorized 
traffic. 
 
Bicycle Path: A paved area located within a street right -of-way but not 
between curbs that is designated for bicycle or other non-motorized traffic. 
 
Bicycle Trail: A paved or improved surfaced trail, located outside of a 
street right-of-way, utilized for bicycle, pedestrian or other non -motorized 
traffic. Public utility maintenance vehicles may be permitted use if joint 
access is allowed. 
 
Board: The Board of Supervisors of Navajo County. 
 
Board of Adjustment: The Board of Adjustment of Navajo County. 
 
Building: Any structure having a roof and used or built for the shelter or 
enclosure of persons, animals, chattel or property of any kind, as defined 
in the Subdivision Regulations. 
 
Code: The County code and ordinances adopted by the Board of 
Supervisors of the County.

natural surface of the land or natural vegetation. 
 
Easement: A right granted to a governmental body, public, or persons 
over privately owned land for specific uses and purposes as so 
designated.

Final Approval: County approval of the final plat or improvement plans 
as evidenced by County certification of the plat or plans. Final approval 
constitutes authorization to record or construct. 
  
Finish Grade: The final grade and elevation of the ground surface after 
grading is completed and in conformance with the approved grading 
plans. 
 
Flood Hazard Zone: Any land area partially or wholly within a delineated 
floodplain susceptible to flood related damage as designated on the Flood 
Management Plans. Such flood hazard zones may include, but not be 
limited to, areas highly susceptible to erosion, stream meander sensitivity, 
moveable bed, scour, wave action, shallow ponding, and subsidence. 
 
Flood Insurance Study : A collection and presentation of flood risk 
information pertaining to designated watercourses, lakes, and coastal 
flood hazard zones within the County. Upon the completion of a flood 
study for the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), the gathered 
information and maps are compiled into a Flood Insurance Study (FIS). 
The FIS report includes comprehensive flood elevation data presented in 
flood profiles and data tables. 
 
Floodplain: Lowlands adjoining the channel of a river, stream or 
watercourse, lake or other body of water, which have been or may be 
inundated by floodwater, and those other areas subject to flooding. A 
floodplain may be that area further defined by the Drainage Policy of 
Navajo County and as shown on Federal Emergency Management 
Agency (FEMA) Flood Insurance Rate Plats (FIRM) or an approved flood 
control study. 
 
Flood Prone Area: Any area within a floodplain. 
 
Floodway: The channel of a wash or other watercourse and the adjacent 
land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the 100-year flood 
without cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than one 
(1) foot. 
 
Freeway: A major highway that provides for the expeditious movement of 
large volumes of through traffic and has full access control via

Legal Access: Access provided to real property connecting the property 
to the public street system. Access may include a public or private street 
or access easement as approved by the County. 
 
Map of Dedication:  A form of plat that dedicates Right -of-Way, and/or 
easements. 
 
Natural Features, Significant : includes washes, significant vegetation, 
and significant rock outcroppings provided these features are in their 
undisturbed natural state.

Slope: The vertical rise in feet measured over a horizontal distance of 
100 feet, expressed as a percentage, measured generally at right angles 
to contour lines but which shall not extend across significant changes in 
grade. A portion of the 100 -foot line shall extend across property lines if 
necessary to obtain the 100-foot measurement at a property line so long 
as not more than 50 feet shall so extend. 
 
Special Area of Special Flood Hazard Area: Land within a floodplain 
that is subject to inundation by the Base Flood.  
 
Street: Any thoroughfare, avenue, boulevard, road, lane, parkway, place, 
viaduct, easement for access, or other way that is an existing state, 
county, or municipal roadway; or a street or way shown in a plat heretofore 
approved pursuant to law or approved by official action; or a street or way 
in a plat duly filed and recorded in the County Recorder's office. A street 
includes the land between the Right -of-Way lines whether improved or 
unimproved and may comprise pavement, shoulders, curbs, gutters, 
sidewalks, parking areas, landscaping, and above and below ground 
utilities.  
 
Street, Arterial: A roadway that is of regional importance and is intended 
to serve high volumes of traffic traveling relatively long distances. An 
arterial is primarily intended to serve through traffic. Service to abutting 
land is limited and access is controlled. Opposi ng traffic flows are often 
separated by a raised medium. Arterials typically have up to three lanes 
in each direction. 
 
Street, Collector: A roadway that provides for traffic movement between 
arterials and local streets and carries moderate traffic volumes over 
moderate distances (less than 3-miles). Provides direct access to abutting 
land and has some access control through spacing and loca tion of 
driveways and intersections. Opposing traffic flows are generally 
separated by a continuous left turn lane. Collectors typically have 2 lanes 
in each direction. 
 
Street, Cul-de-sac: A short local street having one end permanently 
terminated in a vehicular turnaround or an equally convenient form of 
turning, with backing areas as may be recommended by the County 
Engineer.

108 Waivers 
Technical provisions of this Manual may only be waived by the County. 
Any proposed departure from these standards will be judged on if the 
requested waiver is in the public interest and does not compromise public 
safety or the County’s infrastructure inves tment. All known deviations 
must be approved prior to approval of the Plans for construction. 
 
Developers and their engineering consultants, project designers, and 
others interested in preparing a design exception request are encouraged 
to discuss their potential waiver requests with the County prior to initiating 
the analysis and documentation effo rt. This is to enable discussion and 
determination of the technical and alternatives analysis and associated 
documentation requirements and to open communications between the 
County and the developer or consultant. Such communication will help to 
ensure the proposed design will be in the community’s best interests. 
 
108.1 Types of Waivers 
 
108.1.1 Administrative Waiver 
An Administrative Waiver is for minor deviations that: 
1. Do not involve safety or offsite impacts, 
2. Involve minimal review, 
3. Do not involve the broad public interest, 
4. Are similar to other approved modifications and 
5. Occur routinely. 
 
Examples of an Administrative Waiver include: 
• Minor access spacing changes when no alternative is feasible. 
• Minor increase in the maximum number of lots served by 
driveways. 
• Reduced cross sectional requirements, in order to match existing 
roadway and curbs.

108.1.2 Technical Waiver 
A Technical Waiver is for moderate deviations that: 
1. Require limited engineering analysis and County review, 
2. Have minimal expected safety impacts, 
3. Have minimal potential offsite impacts, and 
4. General minimal public interest. 
 
Examples of a Design Waiver include: 
• Use of attached sidewalk in lieu of detached sidewalks based on 
site conditions.  
• Use of roll curb and gutter in lieu of vertical curb and gutter. 
• Removal of on-street parking. 
• Modification to medians, access locations or lane channelization 
when no offsite impacts result. 
 
108.1.3 Design Waiver 
A Design Waiver is for major deviations that: 
1. Have unique characteristics that have the potential for significant 
impacts to the public or County, and 
2. Require extensive analysis and documentation. 
 
Examples of a Design Waiver include: 
• Alternative roadway pavement design.  
• Reduced left turn or right turn pocket storage. 
• Cross circulation or roadway spacing changes when the obligation 
may be passed on to other properties. 
• Design changes concerning traffic or pedestrian safety. 
• Access changes with potential material impacts to other parties. 
• Pre-development versus post -development detention or retention 
requirements. 
 
108.2 Waiver Requirements 
A request for a waiver must be made in writing and include the following: 
1. Appropriate waiver request form. 
2. Narrative that describes the project and proposed deviation. The 
narrative shall include the following: 
a. Section of this Manual, Technical Specification, or Standard 
Detail which relates to the proposed deviation. 
b. Justification for the proposed deviation – specifically a 
detailed explanation stating the extraordinary factors that do

108.3 Waiver Determination 
The initial ruling will be made by Planning and Development Services. The 
initial ruling will include a verification that the applicant has appropriately 
classified the waiver type (i.e. Administrative, Technical, or Design). 
Appeals can be made to County by including a copy of the waiver request 
and all supporting documents and calculations, along with a letter 
describing in detail the reasons for the appeal.  
  
Failure to comply with the approved or conditionally approved waiver will 
be cause for: 
1. Denial or revocation of engineering plan approvals and permits.  
2. Withholding or release of financial assurances.  
3. Removal and reconstruction.  
4. Delay of final inspection.  
5. Delay or denial of final approval.  
6. Denial of occupancy certificates (temporary and permanent).  
7. Notice to surety or other financial institution and/or legal action for 
forfeiture of financial assurances.  
8. Code enforcement.  
9. Any other applicable penalties as provided by law. 
 
See Appendix A for Waiver forms, checklists and approval criteria.

109 Time Limitation of Construct Plan Approval 
The approval of road construction plans shall be valid for a period of two 
(2) years from the date of final design approval by the County. 
Improvements not under construction within this period must be 
resubmitted and reapproved by the County unless a long er time period 
has been specifically authorized by the County with the County’s original 
approval. 
 
Requests for extensions must be submitted in writing with appropriate 
justification warranting such an extension. Road construction plans may 
be required to be revised to meet with updated standards if changes have 
occurred since the date of original approval. 
 
A written decision will be conveyed within 20 business days of receipt of 
complete submittal.

200 Land Division 
This Chapter describes the County’s processes for all types of land 
divisions: minor land divisions (MLDs), Final Plats, condominium plats, 
and re-plats. The Developer of each land division is expected to construct 
the public improvements necessary to serve the lots created by the land 
division, and to assure construction of the public improvements.  
 
201 Purpose 
All minor land divisions, Final Plats, condominium plats, and re -plats are 
processed, reviewed, and approved through the steps described in this 
Manual. The main purpose of these platting processes is to provide for 
the land division and associated dedicat ions necessary for orderly 
development. 
 
202 Applicability 
This Chapter identifies processes and minimum criteria for platting 
purposes per the County’s Subdivision Regulations. 
 
203 General Information 
The Owner is responsible for planning, constructing, and financing all 
public improvements associated with land divisions (dividing, assembling, 
and platting property) and land development. Standard public 
improvements such as streets, sidewalks, streetlights, water, sewer, and 
drainage facilities may be required for a subdivision. Additional public 
improvements, such as trails, irrigation, parking, recreation areas and 
amenities are expected where the subdivision warrants the enhanced 
level of services. Th ese public improvements must be completed and 
accepted before the County will issue a certificate of occupancy.  
 
Improvement plans, as prepared by a Professional Engineer registered in 
the State of Arizona, shall be subject to County approval prior to 
recordation of the Final Plat. The final plat may not be recorded until it and 
the improvement plans have been approv ed nor until an approved 
covenant to construct and assurance have been secured. 
 
203.1 Pre-Application Conference 
A pre -application conference is required for all subdivisions and land 
developments that require public hearings.  The pre -application 
conference between County and the applicant to discuss a proposed 
development application typically lasts 30 to 60 minutes. The County will

Information exchanged at the pre -application conference allows the

2. Provide the applicant with the appropriate development application 
checklist(s) and any related information; or  
3. Require additional information to be submitted, and a subsequent 
pre-application conference to be conducted for further review. 
 
204 Minor Land Division (MLD) 
The Minor Land Division map process is an administrative process with 
map approval granted by the Planning & Development Services. The 
review/approval process is generally intended to ensure that the proposed 
division or future division of land will result  in lots which meet minimum 
area and width requirements of the Zoning Ordinance, produce legally 
recognized land division (in which the parent parcel has been divided less 
than 4 times). The required right -of-way(s), easement(s), and 
dedication(s) are to be made by separate instrument that will be reviewed 
by Planning & Development Services, Public Works, and then recorded 
through the County Recorder’s Office. The dedication recording 
number(s) will need to be added to the MLD prior to recordation of the 
MLD. A land division resulting in greater than 5 parcels requires the 
preparation of a plat map. All rights -of-way and/or easement dedications 
shall be in accordance with this Manual. The preparation, submittal, 
review, and approval of all MLDs located insid e the limits of the County 
shall proceed through the following progressive stages and by following 
the MLD Process. Additional information may be obtained from the 
County’s Comprehensive Plan, Zoning Ordinances and other policies, 
regulations, and standards (including the State Subdivision Statute).

Hillside Development Areas contain slopes in excess of 10% and special

additional information for development located in these sensitive areas. 
Where possible and appropriate, the combining of submittals and  
maps may be acceptable on less complex lots and site conditions.  
 
Please contact the Planning & Development Services for more 
information  
regarding Hillside Development Areas and submittal requirements and 
processes. 
 
208 Changes to a Recorded Land Division 
An Owner/Developer may want to make changes to an approved, 
recorded land division. Different kinds of changes require different kinds 
of procedures. The nature and complexity of the change will dictate which 
procedure applies and is generally related to t he number, size, location, 
zoning, recordation, and history of the affected lots. The general 
parameters of each kind of change are set forth below. However, each 
change is unique in its effects, so the general rules may not apply in every 
case. Changes to  recorded plats are subject to the County’s approval. 
The County will meet with the applicant to review the extent and effect of 
the changes and advise the applicant which procedure is appropriate to 
make the changes.

209 Amended Plats or “Re-Plats” 
A re -plat must be in substantial conformance with the approved 
preliminary plat and all applicable County Codes, Ordinances, and 
Regulations. The applicant is responsible to obtain and fulfill the 
requirements of County Codes, Ordinances, and Regulations w hether or 
not they are referenced or stated in this Manual. The re -plat is subject to 
Board of Supervisors approval and shall be recorded in the County 
Recorder’s Office. Submittal requirements for a re -plat are the same as 
for a Final Plat. Once a propert y has been previously platted, all 
subsequent changes must be through a re-plat. 
 
210 Administrative Changes to a Recorded Plat 
(Affidavit of Correction) 
Minor corrections of errors may be accomplished without re-recording the 
subdivision plat through the Corrective Replat administrative process. 
Allowable corrections under this process are engineering errors and name 
changes, typographical errors, misspellings, etc. Administration changes 
to the recorded plat must be reviewed by Planning & Development 
Services, prior to recording.  
 
If the proposed change is an obvious engineering error and not a design 
error; and the correction does not change or relocate any parcel or 
easement boundary or line or change the legal description or the land 
area included in the subdivision, it can be cl assified as an engineering 
error. 
 
210.1 Procedure 
1. The Subdivider shall file an application for Corrective Replat with 
all necessary back-up information.  
2. The application shall contain a form with the following information:  
• The corrections and/or changes requested.  
• The date that the plat was recorded.  
• The docket and/or page number of the plat that is to be 
modified.  
• Written consent to the correction or change by the current 
owners of record of all of the property affected by the 
correction or change (as shown by a title report furnished by

Improvement District for the maintenance of the landscape, irrigation 
system and drainage facilities located within the rights-of-way, tracts and

prior to recordation of the Final Plat.

300 Survey Standards and Improvement Plans 
The following sections outline the County’s infrastructure requirements 
associated with the development process. They are by nature general in 
scope. Reference should be made to the appropriate Chapters within the 
balance of this Manual for specific details. 
 
301 Purpose 
The purpose of this Chapter is to present information, minimum specific 
guidelines, and provide minimum design criteria and guidance regarding 
the preparation of all types of improvement plans. This includes related 
work such as land surveying, use of GIS Data, preparation of Record 
Drawings, deliverable format, and the general process for plan submittal 
review to the County. 
 
302 Applicability 
Improvement Plans for all public and private projects shall be prepared 
and submitted to Planning & Development Services Department. The 
striping and signage plans shall include signage stating that the streets 
are privately maintained and shall provide guards, gates, or other means 
of denying access to the general public, and other street signs as required. 
 
303 General Information 
It is not intended by these guidelines to repeal, abrogate, annul, or in any 
way impair or interfere with existing provisions of other laws or ordinances 
except those specifically repealed with private agreement, restrictive 
covenants running with the land to which the County is a party. Where 
these guidelines impose a greater restriction on lan d, buildings, or 
structures than is imposed or required by such existing provision law, 
contract, ordinance, or deed, the provisions of these guidelines shall 
prevail.  
 
Most work involving construction and/or design will fall under the 
regulations and authority of the Arizona State Board of Technical 
Registration. Plans, drawings, specifications, estimates, legal 
descriptions, and other work produced by non -registrants wi ll not be 
accepted or reviewed by the County. All work must bear the seal and 
signature of the registrant and conform to the code and rules of the Board 
of Technical Registration.

304 Survey Standards 
 
304.1 Codes, Regulations and Standards 
All surveying and mapping activities associated with projects which will be 
reviewed and permitted by the County shall comply with the rules and 
specifications of State Statutes, this Chapter, the Arizona Boundary 
Survey Minimum Standards (ABSMS), the Fede ral Bureau of Land 
Management (BLM) Manual of Surveying Instructions, the National 
Geodetic Survey (NGS) Standards and Specifications for Geodetic 
Control Networks, and MAG Specifications pertaining to all land and 
property monuments. In general, this means that these activities must be 
performed by or under the responsible charge of an Arizona Registered 
Land Surveyor or registrant in a category appropriate to the activity. 
 
The perpetuation of survey monuments is required and intended to protect 
both public and private property rights in accordance with federal and 
state law. 
 
Refer to Federal Survey Standards for projects adjacent to Federal lands. 
 
304.1.1 Definitions 
Benchmarks: A point of reference by which something can be measured. 
A benchmark is usually a permanent mark established at a known 
elevation that is used as the basis for measuring the elevation of other 
topographical points. In the County, section corners, quarter -section 
corners, and National Geodetic Survey (NGS) control points are used as 
benchmarks.  
 
Grid: Use a combined scale factor to convert the horizontal control point 
values (grid) to ground measurements. The responsible survey registrant 
for each project shall provide the combined scale factor, adjustments, 
rotations, and other pertinent meta -data used  to obtain ground 
coordinates, as part of the project deliverable.  
  
Ground: The surface of the earth and in relation to surveying, a 
modification of the grid coordinate system obtained by applying the 
combined scale-factor and a rotation at a particular point on the grid with 
the intention of obtaining near accurate ground distanc es as would be 
measured with conventional survey equipment.

Monuments: In relation to surveying, an object used to define a property 
corner or survey control point. These would typically be brass caps found 
flush on pavement or in hand holes at section corners or street 
intersections and capped rebar and PK nails found at pro perty corners. 
When set by a Registered Land Surveyor, they must bear the registrant’s 
license number. 
 
305 Types of Surveys 
 
305.1 Boundary Survey 
Perform all land survey work per the guidelines of the Arizona Boundary 
Survey Minimum Standards. These standards may be obtained from the 
State of Arizona Board of Technical Registration’s website or in person at 
1110 West Washington Street, Suite 240, Phoenix, Arizona, 85007. 
 
305.1.1 ALTA Surveys 
ALTA surveys will be based on the latest revision of the American Land 
Title Association, and National Society of Professional Surveyors 
Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/ NSPS Land Title 
Surveys. 
 
305.2 Coordinate System, Datum and Units 
Place all projects on a ground datum based on the Arizona State Plane 
Coordinate System (SPCS).  
 
Use of another coordinate system requires review and approval by the 
County. 
 
305.2.1 Horizontal Datum 
Use the SPCS 1983, East Zone utilizing the appropriate Grid Adjustment 
Factor (G.A.F) until the SPCS of 2022 is adopted and implemented by the 
State of Arizona and ADOT.  
 
Refer to the National Geodetic Survey and Arizona Revised Statutes for 
additional information on SPCS 2022. 
 
Control monument data used shall be documented, described, and 
referenced by name, position, elevation and date on the plans.

305.2.2 Vertical Datum 
The vertical datum shall be North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD 
88) or the current datum as defined by the National Geodetic Survey 
(NGS). 
 
Augment GPS surveys with level and continual survey work as necessary 
to obtain the desired accuracy for design. 
 
305.2.3 Units 
Use International feet for all projects. One foot is exactly 0.3048 meters. 
 
305.2.4 Modified Ground Coordinate Systems 
The use of modified coordinate systems to achieve accurate ground 
distances must be accompanied by a control statement provided on the 
plans or survey drawings to which they apply. Information included in the 
control statement should include but not be limited to: base point or base 
points used and their coordinates in both the grid and ground systems, 
scale factor, rotation, and calibration or localization parameters used. The 
use of a ground system does not override other provisions of this Manual 
and the modified coordinate system used must tie directly back into the  
Horizontal Datum as specified in this Section. 
 
Include m etadata that defines the coordinate system used. Note t he 
epoch date such as NAD 83(2011). When a projection system is used 
other than Arizona State Plane such as a Low Distortion Projection (LDP) 
provides necessary information to re -create that projection. Define t he 
projection such that grid distances are equivalent to “ground” distances 
within the project area. 
 
305.3 Monuments and Benchmarks 
Perform monument perpetuation with every project, all work performed by 
the County, contractors and every private land development project or 
Right-of-Way permit within the County.  
 
All CIP contracts that may disturb monuments shall include monument 
perpetuation in the scope of work.  
 
Upon completion of construction of the project, a Registered Land 
Surveyor shall verify existing monuments (protected in -place) and any 
new monuments installed by the Contractor. Punch and stamp the

305.3.1 Existing Monuments 
When monuments exist that control the location of subdivisions, tracts, 
boundaries, roads, streets, or highways, or provide horizontal or vertical 
survey control, the monuments shall be located and referenced by or 
under the direction of a Registered Land Surveyor prior to the time when 
any streets, highways, other rights -of-way, or easements are improved, 
constructed, reconstructed, maintained, resurfaced, or relocated. A 
Registered Land Surveyor shall make a diligent search for, and locate 
monuments lying  within the streets, highways, other rights -of-way, or 
easements, and any monuments that may be disturbed by construction 
lying outside the streets, highways, other rights-of-way, or easements. 
 
Identify any monuments to be re-monumented by the RLS as a part of the 
work on the Plans, Record of Survey and/or Final Plat and shall be paid 
for as a part of the work. 
 
Disturbed or displaced m onuments by construction shall be reset by the 
RLS at Contractor’s cost and not charged to the County or the Owner. 
 
Monuments uncovered or found during construction shall not disturbed or 
removed until observed, located, and referenced by a Registered Land 
Surveyor. 
 
305.3.2 New Monuments 
Install MAG Detail 120, Type A  with a ½” recess frame and cover 
monuments at all section corners, quarter corners, and center of sections 
and at all centerline intersections, P.C.’s, P.T.’s of each curve for arterial 
and major collector streets. Use MAG Detail 120, Type B monuments on 
all other streets and shall also include centers of cul-de-sacs. 
 
Surveyors shall comply with the requirements of Arizona Boundary Survey 
Minimum Standards or Arizona Revised Statutes, as it relates to filing a 
Record of Survey, Results of Survey, or Corner Record with the County 
Recorder.
