1004.1.4 Control Noxious and Invasive Species 
• Revegetated areas decrease and prevent the intrusion of noxious 
and invasive non-native plant species.  
 
1004.2 Seeding during Grading and Slope Construction 
Tilling/Ripping: Cuts, fills and disturbed areas require tilling or ripping to 
a depth of 6 inches or 12 inches.  
 
Minibenching: Cut slopes constructed in rip-able material should be deep 
tilled or mini -benched as they are constructed. Deep tillage or 
minibenching can only be accomplished on 3:1 and steeper slopes during 
the construction of those slopes. 
 
1004.3 Completing Seeding Work 
Seeding work can be carried out at any time of the year. It is important to 
include a variety of species in the seed mixes that can germinate in both 
warm and cool seasons, as well as in different moisture conditions. 
 
To ensure effective project staging and scheduling, it is recommended to 
complete seeding in multiple mobilizations. This approach can help 
minimize the need for temporary erosion and sediment control measures, 
as well as reduce the number of mobilizations  required. It is crucial to 
complete the seeding process within 14 -days after the slope has been 
finished. 
 
1004.4 Seed Mix Design 
Every site is different and seed mix design depends on site -specific 
characteristics such as temperature, precipitation, soil type, landform, 
land use, etc. Any plant species recommendations are not meant to be a 
definitive authority. It is important to ob serve the site vegetation and 
environmental factors. It is recommended to select a combination of 
species to cover a range of growth seasons and bloom times. 
 
1004.4.1 Categories 
Standard: These species commonly grow to some extent in most places 
in the County. 
 
High Elevation : These species commonly at elevations 7000 feet or 
higher, such as Pinon-juniper woodlands or Ponderosa forests.

Wetlands: These species commonly grow near springs, streams 
(riparian), or where groundwater is close to at the surface. 
 
Sandy Soil: These species can tolerate dry habitats with well drained 
sandy soils, such as sand dunes, but moisture is still required to germinate 
and grow, and mulching is recommended for moisture retention. 
 
Erosion Control: These species grow in areas susceptible to wind or 
water erosion, such as dry washes, slopes, or sandy soils. The tend to 
grow fast, large, and spread once established. 
 
Pollinator: These are mainly wildflower species that have large or many 
colorful flows that attract pollinator species such as insects and birds. The 
inclusion of these species is recommended in any mix to improve habitat 
for pollinators, for landscaping, near gardens or agricultural fields. 
 
Clay: These species are able to grow in clay soils. Clay soils tend to retain 
water and often have high alkalinity, preventing many species from 
growing. If the soil pH is greater than 7, then it is recommended to include 
these species in the mix. 
 
Ornamental: Any native plant can be used for ornamental purposes. 
However, these species are especially useful in landscaping because they 
are perennial, showy/unique flowered, large, attract wildlife, colorful, 
and/or retain aesthetics year-round. Native plants are preferred.

or varieties may exist. The Arizona Native Plant Society (AZNPS) and 
local nurseries can provide further assist ance and information on the 
selection of seeds and/or plants that are suitable for the project site.

1004.5 Seeding Steps 
 
1004.5.1 Tillage 
Deep tillage is an environmentally friendly erosion control Best 
Management Practice (BMP) that often involves ripping the soil. 
 
Tillage helps decrease surface runoff, enhances infiltration, and increases 
water availability in the soil for seed germination, plant growth, and 
establishment. 
 
When dealing with fill slopes, better revegetation outcomes are usually 
achieved. However, cut slopes made in geologically compacted material 
may need to be ripped, tilled, or minibenched to facilitate water infiltration 
and storage, improve seed germinati on, and allow root penetration for 
sustainable revegetation. 
 
1004.5.2 Amending the Soil 
To establish, support, and sustain vegetation, it is essential to provide the 
necessary nutrition, biological activity, and soil chemistry. This can be 
achieved through the use of low solubility/slow -release fertilizers, sulfur, 
and compost. These amendmen ts can be broadcasted or hydraulically 
applied over rough, ripped soils before the final tillage process. This

1004.5.3 Seed Application 
Apply seed through drilling or hydroseeding methods. 
 
Final application of seed and mulch should be made as soon as possible 
after grading of an area is completed. This provides erosion and sediment 
protection and time for vegetation to become established and the project 
to meet Final Stabilization requirements. 
 
1004.5.4 Straw Mulching 
Mulching is an effective method to prevent erosion and sediment loss, as 
well as retain moisture in the soil for seed germination and the growth of 
permanent vegetation. 
 
By utilizing certified mulching that is free from weeds and securely applied 
through crimping, tacking, or hydraulic methods, the risk of introducing 
harmful weeds is significantly reduced. 
 
To maximize the benefits of mulching, it is recommended to apply it the 
same day as seeding. This ensures that the soil remains protected and 
conducive for the successful establishment of seeds. 
 
1004.5.5 Rain and Time 
With rain/snow and time vegetation will typically establish if the previous 
seeding steps are implemented properly and in the correct sequence. 
 
1004.6 Seeding Specifications 
Each project site possesses distinct vegetation characteristics. Utilize 
ADOT Seeding Specifications to establish the seeding requirements for 
every individual project. 
 
1005 Landscape and Irrigation Plan Requirements 
An approved landscape plan is required prior to any site clearing for non-
single family residential purposes. Landscape plans shall be in 
accordance with this section and apply to new development and 
redevelopment, excluding single family residential projects. The 
landscape plan shall be prepared by a landscape architect, a professional 
landscape designer, or a plant nursery.

Landscape plans shall include the following: 
1. A site plan drawn to scale providing sufficient detail to evaluate the 
features of landscaping and irrigation required by this Section. The 
site plan shall show the location of property lines, proposed 
contours, drainage structures, subsurface utilities, e xisting and 
proposed development including all buildings, parking, pedestrian, 
and circulation areas. The plan shall show the location of all 
proposed landscaped areas, and the dimensions and total area (in 
square feet) for each interior parking lot landscaped area. 
2. The location, design and materials of all landscape areas including 
planting strips along all streets, earth berms, retaining walls, 
fences, water features, detention areas, trash enclosures, lighting, 
and paved areas. Where fencing is used for required sc reening, a 
scaled elevation drawing of the fence must be included. 
3. The location, size, and type of all proposed plant and non -plant 
materials, including any existing vegetation to be retained and 
existing trees over 6” caliper proposed to be removed. 
4. A chart comparing the landscaping requirements to the proposed 
materials and area covered, including, but not limited to, the 
following information: 
a. Total parking lot and circulation areas, including interior 
drives and driveways (in square feet); 
b. Total number of parking stalls required and total provided; 
c. Total parking lot landscaped area required and total 
provided (in square feet); 
d. Total buffer and screen landscaped area required, and total 
provided (in square feet); 
e. Total site landscaped area required, and total provided (in 
square feet); 
f. Total quantity and size of plant material required and the 
total provided; 
g. Size, type, and quantity of non-plant material to be provided; 
h. Any other information as the Planning and Development 
Services Director may determine is necessary to ensure 
compliance with the Standards. 
5. All landscape plans must provide an irrigation plan. Irrigation 
systems shall be designed to maximize efficient water use and 
minimize the waste of water. An automatic irrigation system 
designed to provide efficient irrigation coverage is required.

1006 Landscape Design  
Landscape design within the County right -of-way shall take the following 
into consideration: 
• All landscape plans must use native and/or drought tolerant plant 
materials appropriate for their location. Invasive plants and noxious 
weeds are prohibited. Preferred landscaping materials are native 
plants as defined by the Native Plants for Northern Ari zona 
Landscapes compiled by The Arboretum at Flagstaff. A detailed 
plant list shall be included with all plans. The list shall include both 
the botanical and common names. 
• Plants should be grouped in strategic areas and not spread thinly 
around the site. 
• New vegetation shall be selected, planted, and maintained so that 
at maturity it will not interfere with utility lines, snow storage areas, 
vehicular parking, pedestrian circulation, traffic sight visibility at 
driveways and Street intersections, and will not cause damage and 
upheaval of sidewalks and pavement. 
• Plantings which bear fruit, nuts, or seeds that, when dropped, will 
interfere with, or impede storm water drainage flow shall not be 
permitted. 
• All landscape designs shall take into consideration the need for 
Defensible Space. 
• All landscaped areas shall incorporate a ground cover to tie the 
landscaping together and to discourage weed growth. 
• A mix of deciduous and evergreen plant materials is desired. 
Invasive species should not be considered.

1006.1 Placement of Trees and Shrubs 
• Trees shall not be planted in public utility easements, water and 
wastewater easements, and the trunk of a tree shall be at least 8 
feet between the nearest edge of the water and wastewater pipe to 
the center of the tree trunk. 
• Trees shall be located away from underground utilities to avoid 
conflict with mature tree roots.  
• Trees that are to be planted abutting or under overhead power lines 
shall conform with the specific utility company’s (SRP, APS, etc.) 
approved plant species list.  
• Landscaping shall be located to prevent conflicts with signs, street 
and site lighting, sidewalks/paths, fire hydrants, median crossings, 
and above and underground utilities. 
• Hostile vegetation (i.e., cacti) shall be located a minimum of 10 feet 
from any sidewalk/path, trail, or pedestrian access route to assist 
in minimizing hazards. 
• Thornless trees and shrubs shall be used adjacent to public 
facilities (trails, parking, sidewalks, etc.) 
• A clear sight triangle shall be maintained at all street intersections 
and driveway entrances. Such clear sight triangle shall be 
determined by measuring 25 feet along each right -of-
way/easement line at street intersections, and along the right -of-
way/easement line and the driveway for driveway entrances. 
Landscape materials in this area shall have a clear trunk height of 
6 feet from grade level; mature shrubs, groundcover, or other 
materials shall not exceed 3 feet in height from grade level. 
• Trees must be planted to allow for maximum growth in height and 
shape without the need for pruning in excess of that required to 
maintain the health of the plant. Trees shall be located so that the 
mature tree canopy does not extend into the rights -of-way as 
shown in Figure 1011.1.

1006.3 Medians 
Plant material is prohibit in medians, unless otherwise approved by the 
County. Medians narrower than 4 feet wide must be paved with brick 
pavers or a County-approved stamped concrete finish in accordance with 
MAG Standard Details and Specifications. 
 
1006.4 Grading 
The completed landscape grading must be even and consistent. Soil or 
rock mounds should seamlessly integrate with the surrounding terrain, 
with mounds having a maximum slope of 4:1 (H:V) (25%). 
 
1006.5 Mounding of Soil or Rocks  
Mounding of rocks or soils in the County Right -of-Way is not permitted 
unless approved the County.  If located within Sight Distance Triangles, 
mounds must adhere to height limitations and meet the criteria specified 
in the AASHTO Roadside Design Guide for slopes and clear zone. It is 
encouraged to utilize landscape areas for bio-swales and bio-retention to 
enhance water conservation and promote rainwater harvesting.

1006.6 Ground Cover Material 
Ground cover plant material and decomposed granite shall conform with 
the following requirements: 
• All plant material in a groundwater Active Management Area is 
subject to the Groundwater Code. 
• All plant material utilized in County right-of-way medians shall be in

sidewalks in County right-of-way, shall be smooth and uniform, and 
have a surface height of a minimum of ½ inch below the abutting

Boulders are not permitted in County Right-of-Way without approval from 
the County.

All plant material within the County Right-of-Way shall be irrigated, unless 
approved otherwise by the County. The responsibility of maintaining the 
irrigation systems lies with the property owner or owner's association. 
Landscape irrigation systems shall be separated from the water source by 
a backflow preventer.

1008 Parking Lot Landscaping 
Landscaping shall be evenly distributed across parking and driveway 
areas, both on the perimeter and within the parking area, to create a partial 
canopy as requested by the County. In cases where islands are necessary 
or already present, they shall be properly landscaped. 
 
Table 1008.1 Parking Lot Landscaping Requirements 
 
A 5-foot-wide strip of landscaping must be provided along the side or rear 
property lines where parking lots are located. This strip serves as a 
perimeter and should be landscaped. 
 
To protect the landscaped areas next to parking and access points, a 
6-inch vertical concrete curb, 6 -inch bumper stops, or similar materials 
shall be installed. This is necessary to control stormwater flow and prevent 
damage from vehicles. 
 
The curb or barrier around the landscaped areas can also serve as a 
wheel stop, as long as it doesn't exceed a vehicle overhang of 2½ feet 
and doesn't cause any damage or obstruction to the landscaping. For a 
single vehicle overhang, a minimum 5-foot wide planter is required, while 
a double vehicle overhang requires an 8-foot-wide planter. 
 
It is not allowed to park vehicles, construct buildings, or store equipment 
in the required landscaped areas. 
 
To ensure safety, trees used in parking islands must have a clear trunk 
height of 6 feet from the ground. Mature shrubs, groundcover, or any other 
landscaping material should not exceed 3 feet in height from the ground 
to avoid obstructing drivers.

1009 Buffer and Screen Landscaping 
Front and street side landscape areas shall be fully landscaped with a 
minimum of 1 plant unit for every 100 linear feet of frontage when 
requested by the County. Additional plant units may be necessary for 
greater buffer or screening as determined by Plan ning & Development 
Services.  
 
Detention basins and drainageways within setback areas or other visible 
locations on sites shall be adequately landscaped. Two (2) plant units are 
required for every 100 feet of the basin perimeter, measured at the top of 
the basin. Native groundcover seed  mix or lawn mix shall be used on 
detention basin surfaces, with the possibility of using river rock or a similar 
non-plant alternative subject to approval by the County. 
 
1009.1 Screening 
Where landscape screening is required by the County, such landscaping 
shall be in addition to the general landscaping requirements. 
 
Any fences or walls adjacent to County roads or State Highways shall 
have a unifying theme and provide variation by using changes in height, 
different material combinations, offset angles, articulation, and/or plant 
materials. 
 
1010 Site Landscaping 
In addition to the required buffer and screen landscaping, as well as 
parking lot landscaping, the building site shall incorporate landscaping 
that visually integrates the structure(s) with the site: 
• The site landscaping shall include one plant unit for every 100 
linear feet of perimeter of the building footprint, and located within 
50 feet of, and adjacent to, the perimeter of the building. In 
situations where the use or building design makes planting  within 
50 feet impractical, such as mini storage warehousing, it may be 
permitted to place some or all of their on -site building landscaping 
beyond the 50-foot limit, subject to the approval of the Planning and 
Development Services Director. 
• If phasing is proposed or if only a portion of the parcel is being 
developed, the undeveloped area shall be maintained with existing 
native plants. If the area has been disturbed or the existing 
vegetation consists primarily of weeds, the area must be 
successfully revegetated with a substantial mix of native and/or

The County has the authority to approve alternations to the standards in 
this Chapter if it is determined that:

provide relief and would deviate the least from the relevant 
provisions of this Chapter.

The plan will not receive approval if the County finds that the proposed 
landscaping or irrigation designs do not meet this Standard.

1100 General Information 
The County administers all utility planning, permitting and construction 
processes within its right -of-way in accordance with the Arizona Utility 
Coordinating Committee (AUCC) Public Improvement Guide, the 
Maricopa Association of Governments (MAG) Specific ations and this 
Manual. 
 
The purpose of this Chapter is to present to those design professionals 
involved in private land development projects, County projects, other 
public utility projects, County franchisee’s or County Licensee’s that 
provide utility service, general information regarding the processes that 
are required during the construction document preparation, plan review, 
approval and permitting stages and provide con struction guidelines for 
working in the County rights-of-way, public utility easements, and private 
streets. 
 
The information provided in this Chapter is not intended to cover all 
situations that arise but shall provide general guidance. It is not a 
substitute for sound engineering and design principles. 
 
Utilities are those companies, corporations, or entities that provide some 
type of utility service, whether it is electricity, telecommunications, water, 
sewer, or information services. Within the County, utilities are provided 
by, but not limited, to the following companies or utilities. 
 
1101 Codes, Ordinances, Standards and Permits 
The County is responsible for reviewing and granting permission for the 
placement of all proposed utilities and for all construction or maintenance 
work in public rights -of-way and public utility easements by issuing a 
permit. 
 
Right-of-way encroachment permits shall be secured in advance of all 
work performed in County right-of-way. See Chapter 1300 and Appendix 
A. 
 
Encroachment Permits for utility construction are required in County right-
of-way, there is an implication and expectation that construction permitted 
and accepted by the County meets commonly accepted standards for 
safety and utility.

The applicant is responsible for obtaining approval from any other

by other regulatory agencies. 
 
1101.1 Pavement Cuts 
The County requires all pavement cut activities to have an approved 
permit and location to be restored in accordance with this Manual. 
 
1101.2 Construction Work Hours 
General work hours are from 6:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. year -round. The 
contractor may submit a Waiver Request for work outside of the approved 
general work hours. The County will review each project and modify the 
general work hours based on project location, type and/or activities. Work 
hours shall be discussed at the Pre -Construction meeting when 
applicable.  
 
Weekend/holiday or “off -hour” work is not permitted without the prior 
approval of the County. 
 
1102 Public and Private Utilities 
The County grants permission for placement of all proposed utilities and 
for all construction or maintenance work in public rights-of-way and public 
utility easements through the Right-of-Way/construction permits process. 
These permits are issued to utilit y companies, irrigation, power 
companies, governmental agencies, as well as other private companies 
providing cable television, communication lines, telecommunications, 
electricity, gas, irrigation, and wireless providers.  
  
Utilities are provided by but not limited to the companies or utilities shown 
in Table 1102.1.

1102.1 Coordination Required 
The County requires utility provides to coordinate the location of their 
facilities within County Right -of-Way and easements and within private 
streets. Reflect utility coordination on the plans submitted for review.  
 
1102.2 Conflict Review 
The County requires submittal communication with all potential utility 
conflicts within the project area. Provide proof of utility conflict resolution 
with each plan review. 
 
1102.3 Underground and Overhead Utilities 
The County recommends installing electric lines (69kV or less) and 
communication lines underground in accordance with the requirements of 
the Arizona Corporation Commission.  
 
Comply with all utility company requirements for underground installation.  
 
1102.3.1 Overhead Clearance 
The minimum overhead clearance is 18 feet. Overhead lines shall not 
obstruct or interfere with traffic signal visibility. 
 
1103 Water, Sewers, and Sewage Disposal 
 
1103.1 Definitions 
For the purpose of this Chapter, the following words, terms and phrases 
shall have the following meaning ascribed to them, except where the 
context clearly indicates a different meaning: 
 
Act or “the Act”:  The Federal Water Pollution Control Act, also known 
as the Clean Water Act. 
 
Approach mains : Those mains subject to repayment and defined as 
follows: 
1. Mains extended beyond the limits of the project or mains 
constructed through the project or mains constructed along the 
frontage or boundary of the development; and 
2. Mains which serve other property owners other than the owner who 
is developing the property; and

3. Mains which are constructed to contain additional capacity to

Approval authority: The United States Environmental Protection Agency 
(EPA), Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), County, or 
any other authority responsible for the administration and enforcement of 
all applicable Federal, State, and City laws, including the Act and general 
Pretreatment Regulations. 
 
Approved: Accepted by the County as meeting an applicable 
specification stated or cited in this code, or as suitable for the proposed 
use. 
 
AZPDES (Arizona Pollutant Discharge Elimination System:  The 
regulatory program administered by the Arizona Department of 
Environmental Quality pursuant to Arizona law. 
 
Best Management Practices (BMP):  Schedules of activities, pollution 
treatment practices or devices, prohibition of practices, general good 
housekeeping practices, pollution prevention, waste minimization, 
educational practices, maintenance procedures, and other management 
practices or devices to prevent or reduce the amount of pollutants entering 
the sanitary sewer system, surface water, air, land or groundwater. BMPs 
also include treatment requirements, operating procedures, and practices 
to control plant site runoff, spillage or leaks, sludge or waste disposal, or 
drainage from raw materials storage. Best Management Practices may 
include a physical, chemical, structural or managerial practice or device 
that can help to achieve compliance with this Chapter. 
 
Categorical Industrial User: An Industrial User subject to a Categorical 
Pretreatment Standard or Categorical Standard. 
 
Categorical Pretreatment Standard or Categorical Standard:  Any 
regulation containing pollutant discharge limits promulgated by the EPA. 
 
Civil Sanction: That part of the law (i.e., this code) which is designed to 
secure enforcement by imposing a penalty. A punitive act taken by the 
County against an individual or customer, which has violated this code.

County: Navajo County, Arizona and/or the Public Works Department.

Industrial Unit:  A business use or an activity involving and/or 
including, but not limited to, resource extraction, manufacturing, 
fabrication, assembly, and warehousing. 
 
Institutional Unit: A use or activity involving and/or including, but not 
limited to a pubic and public/private group use of a nonprofit nature, 
typically engaged in public service or a religious institution, hospital, 
public or private school or college, and public agency. 
 
Environmental Protection Agency or EPA:  The U.S. Environmental 
Protection Agency or where appropriate the term may also be used as a 
designation for the administrator or other duly authorized official of said 
agency. 
 
Existing source: Any source of discharge, the construction or operation 
of which commenced prior to the publication by EPA of proposed 
Categorical Pretreatment Standards, which will be applicable to such 
source if the standard is thereafter promulgated in accordance with 
Section 307 of the Act. 
 
Holding Tank Waste: Any waste from holding tanks such as vessels, 
chemical toilets, campers, trailers, septic tanks and vacuum -pump tank 
trucks. 
 
Indirect Discharge or Discharge: The introduction of pollutants into a 
treatment works from any non -domestic source regulated under Section 
307(B), (C), or (D) of the Act, (33 U.S.C. 1317), into the treatment works. 
 
Industrial waste: Any liquid, free-flowing waste, including cooling water, 
resulting from any industrial or manufacturing process or from the 
development, recovery, or processing of natural resources, with or without 
suspended solids excluding uncontaminated water. 
 
Minor Land Division: 
1. The division of one parcel of land into five or fewer parcels. 
2. Application for a building permit on a single lot, parcel or tract that 
is not a lot, parcel or tract located within a recorded subdivision, 
and which may be divided into one or more additional lots, parcels, 
or tracts, regardless of whether the property owner has indicated 
any intent to do so.

National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit: A 
national pollutant discharge elimination system permit, issued by the EPA, 
or an Arizona pollutant discharge elimination system permit (AZPDES), 
issued by the State of Arizona, which imposes standards governing the 
quality of the treatment effluent discharge into a navigable water of the 
United States. 
 
National Pretreatment Standard, Pretreatment Standard or 
Standard: Any regulation containing pollutant discharge limits 
promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency in 
accordance with Section 307 (b) and (c) of the Act, which applies to 
Industrial Users. This term included prohibitive discharge limits 
established pursuant to 40 CFR 403.5. Reference the standards located 
in 40 CFR Chapter i, Subchapter n., Parts 405–471. 
 
National prohibitive discharge standard or prohibitive discharge 
standard: Any regulation developed under the authority of 307(B) of the 
Act and 40 CFR 403.5. 
 
Natural outlet:  Any outlet into a watercourse, ditch, or other body of 
surface or groundwater. 
 
Permittee or permit holder: Any person who owns, operates, processes, 
or controls an establishment or plant being operated under a valid 
industrial waste permit to discharge wastewater. 
 
Person: Any individual, partnership, co -partnership, firm, company, 
corporation, association, joint stock company, trust, estate, governmental 
entity or any other legal entity, or their legal representatives, agents, or 
assigns. The masculine gender shall include the feminine, the singular 
shall include the plural where indicated by the context. This definition 
includes all Federal, State, and local governmental entities. 
 
Pollution: The man -made or man -induced alteration of the chemical, 
physical, biological and radiological integrity of water.

Pollution prevention: Source reduction and other practices that reduce 
or eliminate the creation of pollutants through either or both of the 
following: 
1. Increased efficiency in the use of raw materials, energy, water or 
other resources, or 
2. Protection of natural resources by conservation. 
 
Potable Water:  Domestic water delivery system after treatment 
designated to meet the Environmental Protection Agency's and Arizona 
Department of Environmental Quality's drinking standards. 
 
Property Owner:  The person, company, entity or developer which is 
developing the property. A property owner may in certain circumstances 
also be the individual requiring an approach main extension and/or be a 
customer (or future customer). 
 
Sanitary sewer:  A sewer which carries sewage and to which storm, 
surface, and groundwaters are not intentionally admitted. 
 
Septic tank waste:  Any sewage from holding tanks such as vessels, 
chemical toilets, campers, trailers, and septic tanks. 
 
Sewage: Human excrement and gray water (showers, dishwashing, 
laundry operations, etc.). 
 
Sewage treatment plant:  Any arrangement of devices and structures 
used for treating sewage. 
 
Sewage works, sewer system or sewerage works:  All facilities used 
for collecting, pumping, treating, and disposing of sewage. 
 
Sewer: A pipe or conduit for carrying sewage. 
 
Shall: Mandatory. May is permissive. 
 
Storm sewer or storm drain: A sewer which carries storm and surface 
waters and drainage but excludes sewage and polluted industrial wastes. 
 
Storm water: Any flow occurring during or following any form of natural 
precipitation and resulting from such precipitation, including snowmelt.

or private company  and all lines and facilities related to the provision, 
distribution, collection, transmission, or disposal of water and wastewater, 
singularly or collectively. 
 
Waste minimization: An activity which eliminates or reduces the amount 
of any pollutant from entering the waste stream or the environment. This 
may include a change in raw materials, operational improvement, process 
improvement, product reformulation, reuse or reclamation. 
 
Wastewater: Liquid and water-carried industrial wastes and sewage from 
residential dwellings, commercial buildings, industrial and manufacturing

booster stations, storage facilities and related equipment/appurtenance,

the point of delivery. 
 
Waters of the State: All streams, lakes, ponds, marshes, water courses, 
waterways, wells, springs, reservoirs, aquifers, irrigation systems, 
draining systems and all other bodies or accumulations of water, surface 
or underground, natural or artificial, public or private, which are contained 
within, flow through, or border upon the State or any portion thereof. 
 
1103.2 Property Owner Responsibility 
The property owner shall have complete responsibility for the installation 
and maintenance of adequate water and sewar facilities on their property 
and the County shall not in any way be responsible for the installation, 
maintenance, inspection, or damage of such facilities or damage caused 
by any defect in such facilities on the customer’s property.

1103.3 Water and/or Sewer Main Extensions 
If it becomes necessary to extend water  or sewer mains from a distant 
point in order to serve a new development, the cost of the main extension 
will be the responsibility of the developer. 
 
The plans and specifications for the approach main must be approved by 
the County. 
 
The property owner must pay all costs for constructing mains of such sizes 
as to afford adequate service during peak demands for the entire area to 
be served by the extension main. 
 
The property owner's engineer shall submit (i.e., recommend) for County 
approval the required size and layout of water mains that will meet 
domestic water needs and fire flow requirements as required by this code. 
 
The field engineering, plans and specifications required shall be prepared 
by the developer and approved by the County prior to construction. The 
engineering costs for preparation of plans and staking of the water and/or 
sewer main extensions on the property which are incurred by the property 
owner. The County shall perform the inspections during construction. 
 
The County may require the construction of the water and/or sewer main 
extension to meet additional specifications and requirements if such is 
determined to be in the best interest of the County and necessary to 
protect the public health, safety and welfare. 
 
1103.4 Fire Hydrants 
Fire hydrants, valves, pipes and fittings required for hydrant installation 
shall be installed by a licensed contractor on behalf of the property owner 
in accordance with plans approved by the County. 
 
1103.5 Unnecessary Water Waste, Turnoffs and Water Leaks 
Water running off a landscaped area to another area where the water is 
not beneficially used, such as on to streets, sidewalks, gutters, alleys, 
public utility easements, public or private parking areas is prohibited. 
 
1103.6 Unsanitary Disposal of Waste 
It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit, or permit to be deposited, in 
an unsanitary manner, upon public or private property within the County,

1103.7 Treatment of Polluted Wastes 
It shall be unlawful to discharge without a County permit to any natural 
outlet within the County, or in any area under the jurisdiction of the County, 
any wastewater, industrial wastes, or other polluted waters, except where 
suitable treatment has been provided and as authorized by the County. 
 
1103.8 Private Sewage Disposal Systems (Septic) 
All development within a wastewater service area and within a quarter of 
a mile (1,320 feet) from a sewer line is required to connect to that sewer 
system. The extension of a sewer line and the connection to the sewer 
line will be constructed in accordance with County standards and County 
approved plans. Such extension and connection shall be the sole financial 
responsibility of the developer and/or customer. The connection to the 
sewer system and the extension of the sewer line are a condition of 
issuance of a building permit. The County will have discretion to allow 
variances to this requirement for single lot residential developments if 
such development is on a major arterial road or if the connection is 
determined not to be feasible. 
 
Where a public sanitary sewer is not available the building sewer shall be 
connected to a private sewage disposal system  that is  permitted and 
complies with Section 8.5 of the Subdivision Rules and Regulations . A 
private sewage disposal system shall be constructed, maintained, and 
operated at all times in a sanitary manner and in accordance with the 
terms of any private sewage disposal system permit issued by the state 
and county. 
 
None of the provisions of this section shall be construed to interfere with 
any additional requirements that may be imposed by the state and county. 
 
Refer to the ADEQ Onsite Wastewater Treatment Facility website for 
additional information.

1103.8.1 Requirements 
1. Determine the size and location of the septic system before setting 
up a house, structure, or well.  
2. Hire a state certified evaluator to conduct a soil and site evaluation. 
Evaluator shall excavate at least 3 test pits (two in the primary 
sewage disposal area and a third in the reserve disposal field area) 
to a depth of 12 feet and determine the capacity of the soil to 
absorb water and any limiting conditions. The evaluator designs a 
septic system that matches the development’s need and available 
space. 
3. The soil and site evaluation must be completed before applying for 
a sewage disposal permit. Applications are accepted and 
processed through the County. If an alternative system 
(composting toilets are an alternative system) is necessary (due to 
limiting c onditions, such as, lack of soil, high groundwater, 
impermeable layers, etc.), the evaluator shall recommend that you 
design a system to compensate for whatever the limiting condition 
is. The application for an alternative system may be reviewed by 
the Ari zona Department of Environmental Quality or the Health 
Department, depending on the system chosen. 
 
1103.8.2 Site & Soil Evaluator 
A qualified Investigator/Evaluator can be either: 
• Arizona registered professional engineer, 
• Arizona registered professional geologist, 
• Arizona registered sanitarian, 
• Individual with a certificate of training from a course recognized by 
ADEQ 
 
Refer to the County Building Information website for additional 
information. 
 
1103.8.3 Care and Maintenance 
Improperly maintained and failing septic systems are common sources of 
water pollution and potential public health hazards. Refer to the ADEQ | 
Be Septic Smart website for additional information.

1104 Permits within County Right-of-Way 
Obtain a separate right -of-way permit for projects where the 
(re)developer’s contractor(s) will be installing facilities (i.e. conduit, water, 
sewer, etc.). 
 
A contractor with the appropriate license, current County business 
license, and current Certificate of Insurance on file may obtain this permit 
from the County. 
 
Any maintenance or repairs performed on facilities located in County 
Right-of-Way or public utility easements require: 
• Submit construction plans to the County for review, comment 
and/or approval. 
• The contractor to obtain a permit before repairs are made. 
 
1104.1 Types of Permits 
Permits are required for not only constructing and maintaining utility 
facilities within rights-of-way, but also for all barricading for traffic control 
and locating existing facilities in County Right -of-Way and public utility 
easements. 
 
The County requires permits to ensure that all utility facilities are: 
• Constructed in the proper location with adequate spacing 
• Built with acceptable materials and in accordance with current 
specifications. 
• Installed in a safe manner. 
 
In addition, the permit ensures: 
• Infrastructure is protected. 
• Final completion is assured and accepted. 
• Liability issues are properly addressed. 
 
Submit engineered construction plans for review as part of the permit 
process. The objectives of this submittal are to make optimum utilization 
of the space available in the County’s right -of-way and public utility 
easements to ensure compliance with all C ounty policies; to coordinate 
with the construction work of other utility companies, agencies, and 
County projects; and to reduce risk and inconvenience to the public.

A general list of the permits issued by the County for work in the Right-of-
Way is as follows. 
 
1104.1.1 Utility Permit 
A Utility Permit is required  for work, trenching, potholing, boring, and 
maintenance to take place within County Right-of-Way. This permit allows 
the utility company, or a contractor hired by a utility company, to conduct 
work within the County Right -of-Way and is required prior to s ubmitting 
the Traffic Control Plan. Include the permit number on the Traffic Control 
Plan (TCP) so that County has all the information necessary to proceed 
with review of the TCP.  
  
If the permit application is contingent upon a customer/developer provided 
trench and conduit, then the customer shall obtain a trenching permit. No 
work shall begin within County Right -of-Way until the customer’s 
trenching permit has been issued. 
 
1104.1.2 Pothole Permit 
If the permit application is contingent upon a customer/developer needing 
to pothole within County Right-of-Way to verify utility depths or pothole for 
any other reason, then the customer shall obtain a pothole permit. No 
work shall begin within County Rig ht-of-Way until either a miscellaneous 
trenching permit or pothole permit has been issued.  
  
Perform vacuum excavation in the Right-of-Way as follows:  
• A pothole permit is required for all utility location work, and an 
approved traffic plan must be with the crew at all times.  
• Submit a site plan to the County showing the location and quantity 
of potholes.  
• Potholes shall not exceed 12 inches x 12 inches and shall conform 
to MAG Standard Detail 212, and MAG Standard Specification 355.  
• Within 7 working days, install a 6-inch-thick hot mix permanent 
patch, placed in 2 inch lifts, will be placed over one of the following 
backfill strategies:  
o Pea gravel for full depth on holes to be re-excavated.  
o ½ sack CLSM from 6 inches above the top of the highest 
utility to the bottom of the new asphalt.  
o No steel plates or plugs will be allowed.

storm damage, equipment failure, accidents, and other unanticipated 
causes where it is critical to restore/maintain distribution operating 
systems for the safety, health and welfare of the public and permission to 
set up traffic control for the performance of emergency work. If emergency 
repairs are to be made within County Right -of-Way and easements, the 
permit holder is required to contact Public Works as well as the Police 
Department prio r to beginning work. The only exception to this 
requirement is when a temporary facility is being constructed for the 
purpose of continuing an unexpected service disruption.

1104.1.3 Traffic Control Plan 
Prior to commencing construction, submit a Traffic Control Plan (TCP) to 
the County for review and approval. The TCP may be separate from the 
construction plans A completed TCP submittal form and the traffic control 
plan must be submitted to the County. 
 
The County shall determine if traffic hazards at construction projects 
warrant the use of Certified Civilian or Law Enforcement Flaggers to 
provide traffic control services. 
 
1104.2 Permit Application Plan Submittal and Approval 
 
1104.2.1 Minimum Standards 
Make all submittals of proposed utility construction documents via the 
MaintStar Permitting Center or at Public Works. 
 
Submit public or private utility plans to the County for approval to place 
their facilities within County Right -of-Way and public easements. Utility 
facilities range from totally utility owned & provided to utility facilities within 
a developer provided conduit. 
 
Include a permit application, filled out and signed by an appropriate and 
authorized representative of the utility provider, with the utility construction 
plan submittal. 
 
Submit a complete set of construction plans (drawings, details, notes, 
etc.) in PDF format through the MainStar Permitting Center. 
 
Prior to submitting a permit application, the utility company shall verify the 
address where the work will occur. The utility may verify addresses with 
Public Works. The County will perform a technical review upon receiving 
the application and plans to: 
• Verify that the work is in County Right -of-Way or public utility 
easement;  
• Check for compliance with construction standards and County 
requirements;  
• Approve alignments;

1104.2.2 Telecommunications Cable Installation (Copper or 
Fiber Optic) 
Install cable providing telecommunications service by connecting regions 
known as “Trunk Lines,” as described below: 
• Open Trench: Install the cable within a schedule 40 PVC or an 
approved equivalent conduit. Install conduit at a minimum depth of 
48 inches, as measured to the top of the conduit. Pour a 6-inch-
thick colored concrete cap above the conduit. Install color coded 
plastic warning tape with a minimum thickness of 5 mil and a 
minimum width of 3 inches in the trench above and centered over 
the concrete cap at a depth of 12 to 18 inches below the surface.  
• Crossing Under Existing Paved Street:  Jack and bore or 
directional drill cable under paved unless open trenching is 
authorized by the County. Place cable in a schedule 40 PVC 
conduit, or approved equivalent, at a minimum depth of 48 inches.  
• Existing Duct Banks: Install cables in a manner that provides the 
best protection for the cables and minimizes the chance for 
damage to the cables by excavation around the duct banks. 
• Fiber Optic Lines:  Install tracing wires with all fiber optic lines. 
Install tracer wire in the conduit or in the trench. 
 
Install telecommunications cables other than “Trunk Lines” as described 
below:

system design along with construction notes. 
• Submit a copy of the approval from the private water company to 
install their water utility mains & facilities within the County’s Right-
of-Way or public utility easements. 
• Obtain a separate Right -of-Way permit upon plan approval and 
prior to installation of these facilities.

1105 Right-of-Way (R/W) and Easements 
Utility companies that are recognized as a public utility or have been 
granted franchise agreements by the County to serve the citizens are 
allowed to place facilities within the dedicated public rights -of-way and 
public easements subject to the review and  approval of the County. All 
franchise agreements are on file in the office of the County Clerk and may 
be reviewed upon request. All other private facilities are prohibited from 
utilizing the public rights-of-way and public easements without a separate 
instrument of permission or right. 
 
The design professional and the non -County utility providers should be 
aware of, and become familiar with, the various regulations that pertain to 
land development within the County and its utility service areas. County 
ordinances provide for, and require that, all private land developments in 
the County be developed, operated, and maintained in accordance with 
applicable regulations, standards, and requirements. 
 
The developer shall dedicate all public utility easements necessary to 
provide utility service to the proposed project, including any easements 
from other property owners. All Public Utility Easements (PUE) shall be 
granted by grantor to grantee on the rec orded plat, survey, or separate 
instrument in the office of the County Recorder. 
  
Emergency encroachments, including excavation for public utility repairs 
necessary to protect the public safety, are allowed without a permit 
provided a permit is applied for the next working day, all traffic control and 
safety devices necessary are used, and final repairs are not performed 
until authorized by the County. 
 
Return existing improvements impacted by utility work performed in the 
County Right-of-Way to its original condition. 
 
1106 Relocation of Existing Utilities 
Relocation of existing utilities should be avoided, except where necessary 
due to construction or drainage requirements. Design of culverts, irrigation 
facilities, and/or storm drain systems should avoid or minimize any 
disruption of utility service.

1107 Location of New Utilities 
Except for minor service extensions to individual parcels, locate all 
longitudinal utility facilities in public utility easements. Where public utility 
easements do not exist, place utilities in the road right -of way in the 
following order unless otherwise approved: 
• Water on one side of the right-of-way 
• Sewer on the opposite side of the right-of-way 
• Gas, electric and communications outside the pavement. 
• All utilities within right -of-way crossing washes shall have 
protection against flood scour. 
• All utilities must be traceable either tracer wire, metal pipe or a 
method approved by the County Engineer. 
 
Unusual conditions or sites will be reviewed on a case -by-case basis as 
to the appropriate location of the facility. Utilize Record Drawings and 
physical verification to locate existing pavement and utility stubs and 
design to connect to the existing stubs where feasible. 
 
1108 Bridges, Box Culverts, and Pipes 
The placement of utilities on or attached to bridges is prohibited. The 
attachment of or running utilities through a culvert is prohibited.  
 
1109 Utility Coordination 
Close coordination with utility owners is very important to roadway and 
development projects to insure timely relocations. The design Engineer 
shall research utility information, determine the location and ownership of 
all utilities within the project limi ts and resolve each design issue 
associated with utilities. When two or more utility owners having the same 
type of facility within the project limits, the plans shall indicate the owner 
associated with each installation. Clearly identify utility ownership  of all 
utilities within the project limits on construction documents. 
 
1109.1 Utility Coordination on Capital Improvement Projects 
Following approval of each submittal, the design engineer or utility 
coordinator shall furnish plan sets for each utility and agency impacted by 
the project. Direct contact with utility company engineers for design 
coordination will be initiated by the uti lity coordinator or design engineer. 
The design Engineer shall record minutes of all meetings and provide the

The developer, engineer or contractor shall be responsible for utility 
designation, potholing, and manhole invert elevations.  Show utility 
designation and potholing results on the paving plans, paving profiles, 
culvert profiles, storm drain profiles, private irrigation profiles, cross -

Include northing/ea sting and station/offset from centerline of new

The design Engineer shall evaluate the existing utility company as -built 
plans and pothole data to determine conflict locations and notify the 
County of these locations. The design Engineer shall provide utility conflict 
locations, preliminary utility comp any relocation designs, and show any 
associated right-of-way or easement requirements (for utility relocations) 
on the Preliminary Design (60%) plans noted above. Include final utility 
relocation designs on the Final Design (95%) submittal plans. The sealed 
plans shall reflect the new utility locations and all other existing utility 
locations. 
 
1110 Design Requirements 
 
1110.1 General 
Locate all above ground utilities and signal poles behind future sidewalk 
in urban areas. Locate new or relocated above utilities as close to the 
right-of-way line as is practical. 
 
Do not locate utility manhole frames and covers, clean outs, and valve 
boxes in any curb ramp, curb, or gutter. 
 
1110.2 Road Cut Suspension 
The County has established a road cut suspension on roadways under its 
jurisdiction. Newly paved roads shall not be cut for a period of 1 year. 
Newly chip sealed roads may not be cut for a period of 1 year. If work is 
required to cross these road sections under suspension, then all roadway 
crossing work must be bored or pushed under pavement. Water boring is 
not permitted under a paved roadway. Chip sealed surfaces include chip, 
fog, CLSM, scrub sealing and micro - surfacing. Paved surfaces include 
overlays, reconstruction, and new construction.

If boring is not feasible then the designer or contractor may request  
suspension waiver from the County. If approved, then trench repair per 
ADOT Detail C-07.06 is required . An early cut fee in the amount of 
$300.00 plus $20.00 per linear footage of trenching is require d. The 
asphaltic concrete trench repair shall meet the following requirements: 
1. Replace asphalt longitudinally, as measured parallel to the 
roadway alignment, and extend from 10 feet downstream to 10 feet 
upstream as measured longitudinally along the road to the 
outermost trench limits. 
2. Replace asphalt laterally from roadway centerline to edge of 
pavement if the pavement removal does not cross the road 
centerline. If the pavement removal crosses the centerline, full 
width of the road from edge of pavement to edge of pavement shall 
have the asphaltic concrete replaced. 
a. Asphaltic concrete shall be 4 inches thick or match existing 
pavement depth, whichever is greater. 
b. Small trench repairs that are less than one square foot in 
area, may be hot patched as approved by the County. 
 
1110.3 Minimum Separation and Cover Depth 
Maintain adequate separation between proposed utilities/facilities and all 
other utilities. Measure utility separation from the outer edge of conduits 
or structures.  
 
1110.3.1 Horizontal Separation 
The minimum horizontal separation between utilities within the County’s 
right-of-way are as follows: 
• Minimum separation between water and sewer lines shall be per 
ADEQ guidelines. Three (3) feet between power/communication 
line trench and water lines. 
• Two (2) feet between power/communication line trench and sewer 
lines. 
• One and a half (1.5) feet between gas line trench and water lines. 
• Three (3) feet between gas line trench and sewer lines. 
• For all other utilities, maintain two (2) feet separation. 
 
The horizontal separation dimensions are minimums; therefore, additional 
clearances may be required depending on the number and size of utilities 
in a trench.

1110.3.2 Vertical Separation 
The minimum vertical separation between utilities within the County’s 
right-of-way is: 
• Two (2) feet between all crossing utility lines. 
• Minimum vertical separation of water and sewer lines shall be per 
ADEQ guidelines. 
 
The vertical separation dimensions are minimums; therefore, additional 
cover and/or clearances may be required depending on the number and 
size of utilities in a trench or utility owner criteria.

1110.3.4 Horizontal Bores 
Developers and contractors are encouraged  to use jack and bore or 
directional drilling in lieu of pavement cuts. Designs with pavement boring 
shall include a boring profile to ensure proper separation is maintained 
from all existing utilities. Profiles of existing utilities shall be potholed prior 
to start of work and included on the boring profile. Utility potholes shall 
remain open and covered with a steel plate at the critical crossings in 
order to visually verify depth of bore and utility conflicts. 
 
1110.4 Pavement Cuts and Trenches 
Adhere to the following requirements of installing utilities within County 
roads: 
1. Obtain necessary permits for work in County Right-of-Way. 
2. Coordinate sawcutting, backfill, subgrade preparation, and/or 
placement and compaction of ABC and AC with the County prior to 
starting work to allow for observation by the County. 
3. Trim existing pavement to a neat edge and seal the joint with tack 
coat in accordance with ADOT Standard Specifications Section 
404 to insure a proper bond between the existing and new 
pavements. 
4. Remove excavated pavement material from the site and dispose 
of in accordance with State and County laws and regulations.  
5. Where trenching is through geogrid, membrane layers or chemical 
stabilizers, the material shall be replaced in kind or as approved by 
the County. 
6. Disturbance of any survey monument is not permitted. 
7. All aggregate base courses (ABC) shall be in accordance with 
ADOT Standard Specifications. 
 
1110.4.1 Construction Requirements 
 
1110.4.1.1 Clearing and Grubbing 
Remove all trees, shrubs, other landscaping materials, and debris in the 
right-of-way within 5 feet of the edge of the trench and as necessary for 
construction of trench. Remove from the job site all rocks dug out of trench 
and within construction path unless the homeowner requests in writing 
they be moved to their property.

1. Compact shading material to 95% (or to 90% if in sand) of AASHTO 
T-99 maximum density for a minimum depth of 6 inches over the 
utility. 
2. Compact select backfill to 90%  of AASHTO T-180 maximum

3. Compact to 98% of AASHTO T-180 or 102% of AASHTO T-99 
maximum density an 8-inch lift of ABC Class 2 to the bottom  of 
asphalt elevation of the road. 
4. Permit Holder’s may request to use a County-approved, seasonally 
appropriate CLSM or lean concrete may be installed from finished 
shading material to bottom of SURFACE MATERIAL ELEVATION. 
Surface shall be restored as described herein. 
5. The pavement shall be sawcut and removed back an additional 
12 inches on each side of the trench from disturbed subgrade or to 
a minimum of 3  feet, the existing aggregate base moistened and 
compacted to 95% AASHTO T-180 maximum density or 100% of 
AASHTO T-99 maximum density and the pavement replaced to a 
minimum of one (1) inch thicker than the existing pavement or 3½ 
inches thickness whichever is greater. Placement of asphalt 4 
inches or greater shall be in two (2) or more lifts. 
6. At Permit Holder’s option and with advance approval from the 
County, trench may be compacted to 100% of AASHTO T-180 
maximum density, and pavement replaced to the thickness of 
existing pavement. 
7. Complete street cut pavement patching work within 24  hours of 
completion of work. The use of steel plates set flush to pavement 
may be approved for use by County. Where the utility provider will 
be placing facilities in developer provided conduit, the developer is 
required to provide construction plans showi ng the alignments, 
trenches, and bore holes required to install the utility conduit. It is 
the responsibility of the project developer and utility provider to 
coordinate this requirement with each other. 
8. Depending on the condition of the existing pavement, additional 
removal and replacement of pavement, wider than the trench, may 
be required. Full removal and replacement of the pavement area 
between the trench and lip of gutter is required when the distance 
between the trench and the edge of pavement or lip of gutter is  4 
feet or less. In addition, should any raveling or damage occur to 
the existing pavement within the construction area, the damaged

Additional Requirements for Paved Areas within 1 foot of the Center 
of a Lane or the Centerline 
1. Submit at least one compaction report every 200 feet for each 
horizontal 12-inch lift or every 200 feet at random elevations with 
diagonal backfilling. Diagonal backfilling is not permitted without 
County approval. 
2. Ditches and fill slopes shall be brought to finished grade with select

3. Transverse trenches require in addition to item 1, at least one

length of the crossing. 
 
Additional Requirements for Transverse Trenches 
1. Compact each 8" AB C Class 2 lift to 100%  of AASHTO T -99 
maximum density, submit compaction report for each lift. 
2. Replace aggregate surface (Class 6) as appropriate. Compact to 
98% of AASHTO T-180 or 102% of AASHTO T-99 maximum 
density an 8 -inch lift of ABC Class 6 to the bottom  of asphalt 
elevation of the road. Submit certified compaction report for each 
lift every 200 feet. 
 
1110.4.1.3 Unpaved, Gravel or Earth Surfaced Roads 
1. Surface replacement of gravel surfaced roads shall be consistent 
with the existing surface material in place and consist of select 
material or ABC as directed by the County. 
2. Fill placed on existing gravel surfaced roads or earth surfaced 
roads to obtain minimum allowable cover over the pipe for utility 
lines shall be placed to proper grade for the full width of the existing 
roadway and shall be compacted and graded to the satisfaction of 
the County Engineer. 
3. Submit at least one compaction report every 200 feet for each 
horizontal 12-inch lift or every 200 feet at random elevations with 
diagonal backfilling. Diagonal backfilling is not permitted without 
County approval.

1110.4.2 Individual Excavations for Manholes, Sewer, Water or

1. Compact shading material to 95% (or to 90% if in sand) of AASHTO 
T-99 maximum density for a minimum depth of 6 inches over the 
utility. 
2. Compact select backfill to 95% of AASHTO T-180 maximum 
density for each lift above the shading material and submit certified 
compaction report for each lift accomplished within the road prism. 
Lifts greater than one (1) foot thick will be tested every vertical foot. 
Backfill of such excavations shall proceed approximately level 
across the entire excavation. 
3. Replace Base and Surface materials as described in the Paved 
Area, Longitudinal trenches section. Cold mix may be used as a

1110.4.2.1 Materials and Testing 
Paved Areas 
1. Conform to ADOT Standard Specifications for all pavement cuts 
with backfill consisting of either ABC or controlled low -strength 
material (CLSM) as approved by the County and utility. 
2. Conform to ADOT Standard Specifications Section 409 for asphalt 
material used for replacement of pavement cuts or as directed by 
the County. 
3. Replace the thickness of the pavement and aggregate base with a 
consistent thickness and thicknesses shall not be less than 2½” AC 
or 6” ABC. Minimum thickness requirements for asphalt pavement 
and aggregate base shall be measured compacted to 100% of 
AASHTO T-99 maximum density for the material. 
4. Conform to ADOT  Standard Specifications Section 401 for 
concrete pavement replacement. No on-site batched concrete is 
allowed. The thickness of concrete pavement replacement shall be 
consistent with the thickness of the existing section, but in no case 
less than 6 inches. 
5. Conform to ADOT Standard Specifications Section 303 for all 
aggregate base courses (ABC).

4. CLSM may be brought to surface as a temporary measure but shall

1110.4.3 Within Primitive or Non-Maintained County Roads 
Trenches and individual excavations within primitive or non -maintained 
county roads will be in accordance with the above, or as agreed in 
advance by the County and the Permit Holder. 
 
1110.4.4 Requirements for Outside of the Roadway Prism 
Trenches located in area from ditch bottom to outside right -of-way line 
shall be compacted to a minimum of 90% of AASHTO T -99 maximum 
density but with no compaction reporting required. However, the County 
reserves the right to have Permit Holder submit compaction rest report(s) 
on suspect trench compaction anywhere within the right-of-way. 
 
1110.4.5 Additional Requirements 
1. Trenches located within 5 feet of the downstream end of crossroad 
culverts shall be compacted to a minimum of 100% of AASHTO T-
99 maximum density in 12-inch lifts, 15 feet each side of the culvert 
and the surface protected with at least 9-inches of rip-rap (D50 = 6 
inches) on an appropriate geotextile, 5 feet perpendicular on each 
side of culvert opening by 5  feet away from the opening. As an 
alternative, CLSM may be used in the trench five (5) feet either side 
of the culvert. 
2. Ditches and fill slopes shall be brought to finished grade with select 
native materials and compacted. 
3. Shading material shall have a minimum thickness of 6  inches 
above the utility line, or as specified by the utility, whichever is 
greater.

1110.4.6 Restoration 
1. Permit Holder shall video the entire length of the project before 
starting work. This should be done in coordination with the 
Inspector. Video shall clearly identify roadway features, including, 
but not necessarily limited to, condition of surface, culvert s, and 
signs. Special attention should be given to any existing damage or 
deterioration. This video shall be available to Inspector at the time 
of the final inspection. 
2. All driveways and culverts shall be replaced to their original 
condition or better. Culvert pipes removed for utility installation 
shall be replaced with new 18 -inch diameter pipe unless the 
County approves a different size in writing. The County may, at its 
option, furnish 18  inch diameter or equivalent culvert pipe to 
replace existing undersize culverts at the time the existing pipe is 
removed and also may restore all or portions of the drainage 
system with its own crews. 
3. Street signs, traffic signs, delineator posts, mailboxes, etc., 
removed for construction purposes shall be re -installed by the 
contractor in their same location. Those posts/signs damaged 
during their removal or by Contractor’s operations shall be replaced 
with new posts/signs at no cost to the County. If the Contractor 
cannot, for any reason, reinstall signs in their precise same

approved in advance by the Engineer. 
8. Pavement replacement shall be to the same standards as new or 
overlay pavement construction on county roads, including, but not 
limited to, the requirements for submitting a mix design for 
approval, weather limitations on pavement placement, and 
construction methods, equipment, and tolerances. All pavement 
replacement shall be true to line and grade and shall not deviate 
more than 0.01' from the approved profile, nor more than  one-
eighth (1/8) inch from a ten  (10) foot straight edge. The crown 
(cross-slope) shall be 2% or shall match the adjacent pavement 
unless otherwise approved by the Engineer. 
9. Asphalt replacement shall utilize a locally available hot -mix 
asphaltic (HMA) concrete produced in compliance with ADOT  
Standard Specifications Section 406, 409, or 416, or the County 
specifications. The HMA mix may be an off -the-shelf or stock mix

15. Restoration of undeveloped, unmaintained, or primitive roads shall

16. Shoulders and roadside ditches shall be restored with a road

with a backhoe or loader bucket is not sufficient for final restoration. 
17. In certain cases, the County may, at its sole option, restore ditches, 
driveway culverts, and/or shoulders with its own personnel and

1111 Engineered Utility Plans 
Engineered utility plans must be submitted for review as part of the permit 
process. The objectives are to make optimum utilization of the space 
available in the County Right -of-Way and public utility easements to 
ensure compliance with all County policies ; to coordinate with 
construction work of other utility companies, agencies, and County 
projects; and to reduce risk and inconvenience to the public.  
  
The purpose of this section is to provide the designer with information that 
is necessary to assist in the approval of utility plans. A list of 
common/generic items that must be included on all construction plans is 
provided below. This list should not be construed as an all-inclusive list as 
there may be specific information required by the reviewer to clearly 
identify scope of work. The following items are minimum requirements and 
should assist the designer in the development and approval of the utility 
plans.  
  
Utility plans should contain as much information as possible to ensure 
approval. The following checklist is to offer comments on the plans 
submitted for approval for a utility construction permit. The checklist also 
serves to minimize comments on the plans  and to maintain consistency 
among plan reviewers. Plan approval and issuing permits depend on 
following this section and providing all required and pertinent information 
on the construction documents. 
 
1111.1 Utility Plan Requirements 
Utility plans must comply with the requirements of Chapter 300 of this 
manual and the following: 
• Job name/project name (development projects).  
• Work order number.  
• Existing and proposed rights -of-way/ tract(s) and adjacent 
easements with dimensions. Right -of-Way lines shall be labeled 
“R/W” or “ROW”.  
• Dimensioned ties to monument lines in streets and to property lines 
in alley and easements.

• Completed title block including job number and construction

• Utility company logo and job number.  
• County General Notes for Utility Construction.  
• Trench detail showing type, width, depth and number of conduit to

• Stationing and offsets for all existing and proposed facilities within 
the proposed construction site.  
• Total linear trench/bore footage and total linear/bore footage in the 
Right- of-Way.  
• Joint trench must identify all companies in trench.

1111.3 Special Requirements 
• Minimum overhead clearance shall be 18 feet.  
• The MAG Standard Specifications and Details, including current 
County supplements will be followed for the installation of both 
underground and overhead facilities. Permits for overhead lines 
must comply with any agreements with licensed or franchised utility 
companies. 
 
1111.4 Above Ground Structures 
• All structures height, width, length must be dimensioned. 
 
1111.4.1 Cabinets under 3 feet in Height 
• No structure to exceed 36 inches in height in front yard of 
residential homes.  
• Dimensions of structure.  
• 18-inch setback from back of sidewalk to face of structure.  
• Flush to sidewalk elevation if adjacent to sidewalk.  
• Pad size and location in detail. 
 
1111.4.2 Cabinets over 3 feet in Height 
• No front yard placement of structures over 36 inches in height 
allowed.  
• Dimensions of structure.  
• Three pictures (front, left and right views) of proposed site with 
cone at proposed structure locations.  
• Four pictures if along a rear yard if structure could possibly affect 
swimming pools, etc.  
• Pad size and location in detail.  
• Structure cannot be placed in sight-triangle. 
 
1111.5 Plan Review 
County staff will perform a conflict review of the proposed utility plans for 
compliance with County Standards.  
  
Plan review fees shall be collected at time of plan submittal and permit 
fees will be collected upon issuance of the permit. 
 
The fee and insurance requirements may be satisfied by license or 
franchise agreement.

Upon completion of the review, a permit will either be issued to the 
applicant, or the application will be returned for further modifications. If 
additions or corrections are required, the applicant will be notified and 
must resubmit after changes have been made.  
  
Utility Permits are generally issued for 180-calendar days and extensions 
may be issued on a case-by-case basis. If more than two extensions are 
requested, a new plan and permit submittal will be required. Special 
conditions or stipulations may have been added to the permit application 
before compliance.  
  
The following on the permit form evidences approval of the Utility 
application:  
• Identification of the date of the original issuance.  
• Identification of the date that the initial issuance of the permit 
expires.  
• As with the correction reports, the approved permits are available 
from the MaintStar Permitting Center or pickup at the Public Works 
Department in Show Low.  
• A conduit plan shall be shown on compliant developer or utility 
provider improvement plans prior to utility permit issuance. 
 
1111.6 Permit Extensions 
As stated on the permit, construction of the utility facility shall begin within 
180-days of the permit issuance, otherwise the permit expires by limitation 
and re -application must reoccur. Two extensions of the same 
application/permit form are allowed if work has not commenced within 
180-days of the permit issuance. 
 
The utility provider shall provide a copy of the prior permit issued along 
with the utility plans. 
 
Permits that have expired by limitation 2 (two) times and the utility facility 
is still required and/or necessary, the utility provider shall complete a new 
application form and submit 3 (three) copies of the plans, and 4  (four) 
copies if trenching is required, for review and/or approval.

1112 Utility Plan Submittal, Plan Review and 
Permitting 
 
1112.1 Utility Plan Submittal and Review 
Submittals of the construction documents for the proposed utilities shall 
be made to Public Works. 
 
1112.2 Utility Conflict Review 
In addition to County review, construction plans shall be sent to all 
applicable utility companies for a conflict review. The utility companies 
shall then sign the cover sheet of improvement plans or provide letter 
confirming that they have seen the plans,  are aware of the scope of the 
project, have identified existing and proposed utilities conflicts in relation 
to the project and agreement to mitigate all conflicts with their facilities. 
The County Engineer shall not approve construction plans until all 
potentially affected utilities have signed the plans or provided this written 
correspondence. 
 
It is understood and agreed that the Engineer and/or owner has 
considered all of the permanent and temporary utility appurtenances in 
their existing and relocated positions, as shown on the plans and 
specifications for the project. Therefore, the owner sha ll bear all risk and 
cost arising from problems associated with utility locations. County 
approval of plans and/or issuance of permits shall not affect this 
presumption. 
 
1112.3 Encroachment Permit 
 
1112.3.1 Permit Application 
The Navajo County Encroachment Permit is to be filled out, signed by an 
appropriate and authorized representative of the utility provider, and 
included with the construction plan submittal. Copies of the application 
form are available in Appendix A, the Navajo County website, or from the 
County. 
 
1112.3.2 Permit Issuance 
Navajo County Encroachment Permit applications will only be accepted if 
all request information is supplied, or provisions are otherwise made. The 
approved permits are either e -mailed to the applicant or are available at

1200 General Information 
The County maintains approximately 720 miles of roads. These roads are 
maintained by preventing, reducing, and restoring deterioration of the 
roadway infrastructure through road surface and roadway structure 
maintenance and preservation activities. Work it ems include surface 
patching, depth patching, chip sealing, double chip sealing, asphalt 
overlays, crack sealing, snow and ice management, grading of gravel 
roads, road sweeping, shoulder work, and various pavement maintenance 
techniques. All traditional m aintenance activities will be reviewed with 
attention to budget constraints on an annual basis. The maintenance 
schedules will be adjusted as necessary where the safety aspect of the 
work being performed will be the deciding factor.  
 
The Public Works Department shall, under direction of the Board of 
Supervisors, provide road construction and maintenance services in an 
equitable and objective manner.  To prioritize these services, a road 
classification system is used, taking into account the road's function and 
Average Daily Traffic (ADT).  
 
All roadways within the County Maintained Road System are classified 
according to Federal Function Classifications (FFC), which serve as a 
guideline for construction and maintenance. For more information on FFC, 
see Chapter 400. 
 
Maintenance activities are determined based on a road's FFC in the 
County Road Maintenance System.  
 
Furthermore, the County may consider adding existing roads into the 
maintenance system, based on the County’s Improvement District policy, 
when it is deemed appropriate to do so.

1201 County Maintained System 
 
1201.1 County Highways 
County Highways are the only category of public roads that the County is 
authorized to allocate public funds for new construction, alterations, or 
improvements. These roads must officially be established by the Board of 
Supervisors in pursuant to Arizona Revised Statutes (ARS).  
 
All County Highways are included in the County Maintained Road System. 
The County is committed to maintain and improving these highways in 
accordance with the law. Considerable public resources have been 
invested in these roads, and it is the County’s responsibility to ensure that 
they continue to meet the needs of the public. 
 
1201.2 Improvement Districts 
Public roads that meet the criteria outlined in the ARS or have been 
constructed or improved to current County standards , at no cost to the 
County, through the establishment of a County Improvement District may 
be eligible for maintenance. However, maintenance services are only 
provided to roads that have been accepted by the Board of Supervisors 
through a resolution for inclusion in the County Maintained Road System. 
Once accepted, these roads will be maintained in accordance with the 
assigned FFC. 
 
1201.3 Primitive Roads 
Primitive roads are not designed or constructed to any standard and are 
not regularly maintained. The County is not liable for damages as a result 
of using a primitive road.  
 
1202 Public Right -of-Way not a part of County 
Maintained Road System 
Roads currently in use that have not been officially incorporated into the 
County Maintained Road System, along with "paper" rights of way granted 
to the public through easements or other recorded documents but not yet 
accepted into the County Maintained R oad System, fall outside the 
County's maintenance jurisdiction.

1203 Process of Adding a Road into the County 
Maintenance System 
For any routine maintenance work performed to make a roadway 
passable within a public easement that is not a County maintained 
roadway the owner performing the routing maintenance work may not 
need a permit unless the owner or its contractor is moving more  than 50 
cubic yards of roadway material, performing any permanent 
improvements, or creating permanent obstructions to the public 
easement. 
 
Figure 1203.1 shows the typical process for adding a road into the County 
Maintenance system.  
 
 
1203.1 Step 1: Petition the Public Works Department 
Residents may request the County to add a public road to the Maintained 
Road System. Petitions shall contain the following: 
1. Submit a petition to the County, signed by two or more residents 
who have direct access to the road in question. 
2. Provide evidence of the existing right -of-way and obtain from a 
Registered Land Surveyor who is licensed to practice in the State 
of Arizona. This certification shall confirm that the existing road is 
located within a dedicated public right-of-way. 
 
After receipt of a petition, eligibility will be assessed by the County.

1203.2 Step 2: Staff Field Checks 
County staff will conduct on-site inspections to assist in the determination 
of eligibility.  
 
The County will review and verify the following: 
1. A publicly dedicated easement. 
2. Construction occurred at no expense to the County. 
3. An Average Daily Trips (ADT) count exceeding 50 trips. 
4. Compliance with minimum geometric standards. 
5. Contains appropriate drainage features. 
6. Roadway has sufficient surfacing material, such as aggregate base 
or approved materials, to allow for maintenance without damage to 
County equipment. 
 
The minimum geometric standards shall be defined by either the AASHTO 
Guidelines for Geometric Design of Low -Volume Roads , or this policy, 
depending on which is more restrictive. 
 
1203.2.1 Engineering Evaluation 
The County is authorized to conduct traffic  counts as necessary . The 
County will evaluate roads with more than 50 Average Daily Trips (ADT) 
to determine their safety and suitability for maintenance. Where a road 
meets maintenance and safety criteria, but lacks the required Right -of-
Way or has inadequate Right-of-Way, the County may begin the process 
of acquiring Right-of-Way and incorporating the road into the maintenance 
system.  
 
The determination of eligibility for County maintenance is the duty of the 
County Engineer or designee as per the ARS.  
 
1203.2.2 Qualification Requirements 
Achieving compliance with the regulations stated in this Chapter and 
abiding by the laws of the state can be accomplished using three methods: 
1. Subdivision Streets: Public subdivision streets constructed to 
County standards, at no expense to the County, and in accordance 
with an approved plat as per the ARS may be accepted for 
maintenance within one year of their completion. 
2. Existing Dedicated Public Roads: Existing roads dedicated to 
the public must conform to Section 1203.2.
