1204 Removal from the County Maintenance System 
If it is determined that a road within the County Maintained Road System 
has not been significantly utilized by the public for a period of five (5) 
years, the County is authorized to initiate Board proceedings to remove 
the road from the system. Furthermor e, the County has the ability to 
pursue appropriate Board action to relinquish all rights and interests in 
County Highways and other roads or sections that no longer meet the 
needs of the traveling public or were never accessible for public use. 
 
1205 Snow Removal, Salt, and Cindering 
Difficult driving conditions resulting from snow and/or ice necessitate an 
immediate response from County maintenance forces to mitigate these 
driving conditions until weather improves and driving conditions can return 
to normal. The goal of this work is to provide emergency service access.  
 
1205.1 Driveways 
Driveway snow clearing is the responsibility of the driveway owner and/or 
resident. 
  
Location The road must be directly accessible from a publicly 
maintained road. 
Drainage Drainage along the road must be such that frequent 
maintenance is not necessary in wet weather.

Conditions 
Sufficient workable material is required for routine 
grading to maintain a safe and comfortable road. The 
surface material shall not cause excessive wear and 
tear on the grader during routine maintenance.

1207 Culvert Installation Program 
The County has a program to ensure the proper installation of culverts 
within public Right-of-Way. Residents are responsible for any Illegal head

1207.3 Procedure 
To participate in this program, residents require a right-of-way permit and 
communicate their intention to participate. Right -of-way permits can be 
obtained using the MaintStar Permitting Center, or alternatively, from the 
Public Works Department in Show Low or Holbrook.

1208 Adopt-a-Roadway 
The County is actively involved in minimizing litter on County roads. This 
goal is achieved through regular litter clean -up activities and promoting 
responsible litter disposal among motorists. The County's Adopt -a-
Roadway Program plays a crucial role in these efforts. 
 
This program invites non-political groups and individuals to participate in 
litter clean -up along designated sections of County roads. The County 
installs signs acknowledging the contributions of these organizations or 
individuals, recognizing their ongoing commitment and assistance. 
 
To express an interest in the Adopt-a-Roadway program, contact Navajo 
County Public Works at (928) 524-4100. 
 
1208.1 Policy 
Only County maintained roads  sections that are considered suitable for 
this activity will be designated. Ensuring the safety of Adopt -a-Roadway 
workers is of the utmost importance.  Adoptable segments should ideally 
be around two (2) miles long, although shorter lengths may be allowed in 
areas with heavy litter, provided they are not less than one (1) mile in 
length. 
 
1208.1.1 Eligibility 
Individuals, private corporations, non -profit organizations, and non -
political organizations are eligible to participate in litter cleanup activities 
on a specified portion of a County road through a revised right-of-way Use 
Permit, provided they adhere to the regulations outlined in this Manual.  
 
Permits will not  be issued to political organizations in an effort to avoid 
what could be considered as endorsement signs.

1208.1.2 Rules and Conditions 
1. Children who are under the age of twelve  (12) are prohibited from 
participating or being present in the right -of-way for any purpose. 
The organization responsible for the event must ensure that there 
is sufficient supervision, with at least one (1) adult aged 21 or above 
for every ten (10) members who are under the age of 18. 
2. Alcoholic beverages are prohibited at the Adopt -a-Roadway litter 
pick up site. 
3. The participating organization will designate an Adopt-a-Roadway 
supervisor from its members to oversee the work conducted in the 
right-of-way. 
4. Adopt-a-Roadway workers are required to participate in ADOT's 
Safety Briefing, including watching the Safety Briefing Video before 
each litter pick up activity. 
5. Before each litter pick up, the Adopt -a-Roadway supervisor must 
provide safety precaution training to all workers participating in the 
program. 
6. The safety requirements linked to the Right -of-Way Use Permit 
must be followed by all Adopt-a-Roadway workers at all times. 
7. Perform clean-up activities at least two times (2) per year. 
8. The participating organization must coordinate their pick -up 
schedules with the County to prevent conflicts regarding the 
utilization of County roads or rights -of-way. This coordination also 
helps in facilitate the smooth removal of the filled litter bags. 
9. Prior to beginning work in the right-of-way, every participant (or the 
parent or guardian of a minor) must sign the waiver for each pick 
up event. 
10. The permit will be granted for a duration of at least two (2) years. It 
can be extended if the organization has satisfactorily complied with 
the conditions of the Right-of-Way Use Permit. 
11. The County Engineer or designee has the authority to enforce any 
additional prerequisites and stipulations that may be deemed 
necessary.

1300 Policy 
Access management refers to the control and regulation of vehicular entry 
onto public roadways from adjacent properties. It encompasses legal, 
administrative, and technical strategies that a political jurisdiction employs 
to safeguard the well -being and se curity of its residents. Additionally, 
access management governs the level of control imposed on roadways 
and is crucial for supporting the capacity of public roadways and 
facilitating access to private land. 
 
Different types of roadways fall under the administration of various 
entities, such as the State, a city, town, or county. The guidelines outlined 
in this document specifically pertain to access to properties and roadways 
within the jurisdiction of the Cou nty. In cases where access is managed 
by multiple jurisdictions, the responsibility for adhering to the guidelines or 
regulations is shared among all relevant entities. 
 
Any access points onto County right -of-way shall be obtained through a 
permit. Depending on the circumstances, roadway accesses may 
necessitate a Traffic Impact Analysis/Statement and the construction of 
right and/or left -turn lanes. Additional traffic con trol measures or 
improvements to the roadway may also be required. 
 
1301 Right-of-Way Use Permits 
 
1301.1 Purpose and Authority 
The Arizona Revised Statutes (ARS) authorizes the Boards of 
Supervisors to “lay out, maintain, control and manage” the public roads in 
areas of the county that are not incorporated. According to the ARS, the 
Board “may impose restrictions and limitations upon the use of the public 
roads as it deems best for the public safety or welfare.” Additionally, the 
ARS provides that the County, as the agent of the Board of Supervisors, 
“shall have charge of all highways, other engineering construction and 
improvements, alterations and repairs to county property.” 
 
Case law has established that the utilization of public rights -of-way for 
purposed other than their primary intended use is subordinate to the 
utilization by the authority that controls the roadways. 
 
On June 8, 1971, the County Board of Supervisors adopted a resolution 
imposing certain regulations for construction activities in the public rights-

of-way in the unincorporated areas of the County. These regulations 
mandate that a permit shall be obtained from Public Works. 
 
The public agency has the authority to periodically update permit 
requirements and construction specification to reflect changes in 
construction methods and liability exposure. 
 
The purpose of these stipulations and specifications is to consolidate and 
standardize permit requirements for work within public rights-of-way under 
the control of The County to ensure adequate protection of lawful users of 
public rights-of-way. The inten tion is not to replace any other mandates 
imposed by Federal, State, or local regulatory agencies or codes, as well 
as those of individual utilities. 
 
The specifications detailed herein are intended to serve as the minimum 
standards for all construction within existing or proposed County rights-of-
way, whether they are already established or planned. When conducting 
work within existing public rights-of-way, the permit issued by County shall 
specify which sections of that shall be complied during the work. 
 
Failure to conform to these specifications may be considered a violation 
of the ARS, and subject to the penalties therein specified. Encroachments 
installed without a permit are subject to removal and restoration of the 
right-of-way at the owner’s expense. 
 
The County may, in certain cases, require the permit holder to furnish a 
performance bond or other financial assurance for major or extensive 
projects, and/or may accept a financial assurance in lieu of certain testing 
requirements. 
 
1301.2 Requirements for Work inside County Right-of-Way 
 
1301.2.1 General Requirements 
All work above, below or within County right-of-way requires a permit from 
the County, except for routine maintenance as defined in  Section 1203. 
This requirement applies to any public right -of-way or easement. The 
permit will be issued to the owner of the encroachment, or alternatively, 
the contractor responsible for the work may apply for the permit. A 
physical copy of the permit must be kept on -stie for the duration of the 
project.

and are subject to immediate removal when observed by County

All work within public rights -of-way, such as landscaping or driveway 
construction between the edge of the traveled roadway and the easement 
or property line, shall be performed by a licensed, bonded, and insured 
contractor, or a franchised or Improvement District utility. A property 
owner may install a driveway culvert, construct a driveway, or install minor 
landscaping materials for their own single-family residence. 
 
Contractors shall hold a contractor’s license of an acceptable grade and 
type, as determined by the County, when a significant portion of the work 
is within public right -of-way. However, if the work within the public right -
of-way is minor or incidental to the main effort on a residential lot, any 
contractor licensed for the work may perform the work within the public 
right-of-way. Examples of minor work within the public right-of-way include 
the installation of short-side utility service(s) to a single -family residence, 
the construction of a driveway and culvert as part of a single -family 
residence, and landscaping outside the roadway prism. All road crossings, 
whether through boring, direction drill, or open cut, shall be made by a 
Licensed Contractor or a qualified crew from the local utility. 
 
All utility work within the public right -of-way shall adhere to the 
requirements of the approved project plans, utility specifications and/or 
the County construction specifications, and this manual. 
 
The permit holder shall ensure compliance with all applicable Federal, 
State, and Local laws, including but not limited to, OSHA, EPA, and utility 
protection (Blue Stake) requirements. Work shall be done in accordance 
with the latest edition of the Arizona  Department of Transportation 
Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction as modified 
herein, except as approved in advance by the County. 
 
The County reserves the right to inspect the work periodically or 
continuously as it affects the public right -of-way, reduce or eliminate 
requirements and stipulations, and close the permit when all work and 
punch list items are finished. The Inspector’s s pecific role is to ensure

The permit holder shall ensure that copies of all required test reports shall 
transmitted to the County through the Owner’s Engineer in a timely basis. 
The County shall receive compaction test reports no later than the 
following working day after the test is p erformed. Late test reports shall 
constitute grounds for the County to impose more stringent construction 
requirements or suspend operations under the permit. 
 
A Traffic Control Plan shall be submitted a minimum of 5 days prior to the 
start of construction for a Use Permit. 
 
Failure to provide proper traffic control per the submitted plan may result 
in the issuance of an immediate STOP WORK order and/or revocation of 
the permit. 
 
1301.2.2 Notices and Public Information 
The permit holder shall notify homeowners in advance of work that will 
take place in front of their property and that extend beyond one (1) working 
day. This notification may be given through various means such as a 
letter, personal contact, or the use of “Doorknob Hangers,” among others. 
 
The permit holder shall inform the public about complete or partial road 
closures, as required by the County, through local radio station. This 
notice shall be given at least 24 to 48 hours in advance of the start of work. 
The notice shall include the spec ific location and duration of the travel 
restrictions, along with recommend alternative routes for the public. 
 
The permit holder shall notify the County prior to removing or obscuring 
any traffic control device, such as signs, pavement markings or signals. 
Replacement of such devices shall be as directed by and under the 
supervision of the Engineer. 
 
The permit holder  is responsible for notifying utilities, local authorities, 
emergency service providers, and other relevant parties at least 48 hours 
before starting construction. 
 
The permit holder shall notify the County Sheriff’s Dispatch whenever road 
or lane closures are installed or removed on major roads. 
 
The permit holder shall notify the County at least two working days in 
advance to the start of any work under an annual or one-time right-of-way

permit holder shall inform the appropriate County Departments prior to the 
approval of the permit. 
 
1301.2.3 Driveways, Culverts, and Landscaping 
Heated driveways, sidewalks, or other landscape features shall be clearly 
shown on the permit application if they are to be installed within the public 
right-of-way. The use of glycol or any other toxic or hazardous materials 
in these systems is prohibited within the public right-of-way. The County, 
its contractors, or agents, as well as other permit holders or their 
contractors shall not be responsible for replacing of any features that are 
installed in violation of the permit or without a permit. 
 
New or restored driveway pavement shall conform with the established 
road grade and shall not extend above the plane of the extended roadway 
crown within the roadway prism. 
 
Driveway culverts shall be at least 18 inches in diameter or equivalent 
arched corrugated metal pipe. Larger sizes may be required when local 
drainage conditions warrant. Smaller sizes or other materials are not 
acceptable unless approved in advance by the  engineer. Arched, or 
“squashed” or “flat bottom” pipe shall be installed with the flatter side 
down, and in such a manner as to remove any bow or curvature of the 
pipe. 
 
1301.2.4 Sanitary Provisions 
The contractor is responsible for ensuring that there are appropriate 
sanitary facilities available for the workers at the job site. These facilities 
shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition, in accordance with 
the regulations set by the State  and local health boards, as well as other 
relevant authorities.

1301.2.5 Trenching Operations 
During trenching operations, it is required that an OSHA certified 
Competent Person or a Registered Professional Engineer (Civil or 
Geotechnical) supervise the work. This person shall have the authority to 
stop the work if any unsafe trench conditions are identified. The County 
also reserves the right to stop trenching operations in the right -of-way if 
the trench is deemed unsafe, regardless of its depth, or if the contractor 
fails to have a Competent Person present when the trench exceeds 4 feet 
in depth. 
 
During non-working hours, the maximum limit for open trenches is 50 feet. 
These trenches shall be protected in a manner approved by the County . 
Any specific variations to these requirements will be evaluated on a case-
by-case basis. 
 
1301.2.6 Safety Gear 
ANSI/ISEA 107-210 Class II safety apparel  is required working within in 
County right-of-way or easements. This i ncludes the use of shirts, vests, 
jackets, and bibs, in addition to all necessary  personal protective 
equipment. In cases where fire-resistant or non-spark-generating clothing 
is required, Nomex vests and/or shirts are available in the appropriate 
colors. 
 
1301.2.7 Traffic Control 
To ensure compliance with Part VI of the Manual of Uniform Traffic Control 
Devices (MUTCD), a Traffic Control Plan (TCP) shall be submitted to the 
County for approval at least three (3) working days before any work 
begins. A copy of the approved TCP shall be available on the jobsite 
at all times while work is in progress. 
 
The permit holder is responsible for ensuring that at least two (2) ATSSA, 
or equivalent, certified flaggers are present and actively working whenever 
work equipment is within the roadway prism or when equipment is 
entering, exiting, or working on the roadway. For short periods of time not 
exceeding ten (10) minutes out of any one (1) hour on low volume 
roadways, flaggers shall be equipped with a STOP/SLOW sign on a 72" 
staff.  
 
Flaggers, other than uniformed police officers, shall not direct traffic to 
operate contrary to any visible regulatory signs. For example, if there is a

under flagger control. Requests to remove or cover up regulatory signs 
shall be shown on Traffic Control Plan (TCP) and approved by the County 
in advance. 
 
Traffic control takes precedence over all other construction activities 
within the right-of-way, especially in emergency situations. If construction 
equipment, materials, or operations obstruct one lane of traffic, flaggers 
shall be present and active at all times. If there are not enough workers to 
flag traffic and carry out construction tasks simultaneously, work must 
cease until substitute flaggers are available, all signs are visible, and 
adequate flaggers are present. Sufficient flaggers must be on han d to 
ensure continuous flagging during operations that require it. 
 
The set-up of flagging and traffic control must start with the least restrictive 
measure (the flagger or road closer) and shall be removed in reverse 
order. 
 
All personnel involved in setting up or removing traffic control must have 
at least one vehicle with flashing lights positioned between them and the 
oncoming traffic for protection. 
 
1301.2.8 Blasting 
No blasting activities are permitted  within the right -of-way without the 
explicit approval of the County and local authorities and must be carried 
out by a blasting contractor who is duly licensed, bonded, and insured. All 
requests for blasting approval shall be submitted IN WRITING at least two 
(2) weeks before the planned start date. 
 
Coordination with the County is required for any blasting within 1000 feet 
of a road to ensure adequate warning for motorists. Additionally, blasting 
zones shall display the necessary warning signs as outlined in Section I 
of the MUTCD. 
 
During non -working hours, roads may only be closed with the prior 
approval of the County. The permit holder is responsible for providing 
adequate lighting, detour signs, maintenance, changeable message 
signs, and advance notice to users of the road. In exceptional cases where 
one lane of a road needs to remain closed during non-working hours, the 
County may approve the posting of the roadway for one -way traffic with

overnight road closure is in effect, flaggers are required to be on site

1301.2.9 Temporary Facilities and Maintenance of Work Area 
No soil processing shall take place in County rights -of-way without the 
County’s written approval in advance. 
 
STOP and YIELD signs that are removed or covered up by construction 
activities shall be replaced with temporary ones on a support as shown on 
the TCP when flaggers are not present. The permanent replacement of 
these signs shall be reviewed and approved the County. 
 
Soil disposal or processing on private property is only allowed with the 
property owner's written consent. If the disposal exceeds fifty (50) cubic 
yards or is within a wash or flood plain, the written approval must be 
accompanied by a copy of the approved grading plan and permits. 
 
Trenching spoil shall be removed from the traveled portion of the right-of-
way prior to the end of each workday to ensure unobstructed two -way 
traffic. If this is not feasible, then traffic control measures shall be 
implemented in accordance with an approv ed TCP prepared in 
accordance with the MUTCD and approved by the County. 
 
Temporary ditches shall be constructed to divert stormwater away from 
the work area, taking into account weather conditions, in order to prevent 
erosion or sedimentation downstream of the project. If necessary, erosion 
barriers may be required. Drainage facilities shall be restored daily when 
the National Weather Service predicts a 50  percent or higher chance of 
precipitation within the next 72 hours, regardless of other project activities 
such as cleanup and restoration, or when any work is being carried o ut 
within the right-of-way between November 1 and March 1. 
 
All paved surfaces shall be power swept and/or washed clean at the end 
of each workday, or as necessary based on conditions. The surfaces shall 
be sufficiently clean to prevent the formation of dust or the occurrence of 
muddy or slippery conditions.

Unpaved roads within the work area shall be graded using a road grader 
at least once a week to ensure they remain accessible to all passenger 
vehicles throughout the duration of the permitted work. This maintenance 
shall also be done as needed to address a ny ruts, bumps, mud, or mud 
holes. It is important to note that back dragging with a bucket is not an 
acceptable alternative method. 
 
If the permitted work is not completed before winter weather , the permit 
holder shall be responsible for winter maintenance, including snow 
removal and ice control, 24 hours a day. The permit holder shall have 
snow removal and ice control equipment with operators ready on -site 
within two (2) hours of being notified by the County. 
 
During cold months when snow or ice conditions are present, the permit 
holder shall ensure that the permitted work does not impede public snow 
removal and ice control operations. Additionally, trench plates shall not be 
left in place beyond the end of the working day if the US Weather Service 
predicts snow or ice before the next working day. 
 
1302 Access Control 
Access within the County shall be subject to the following guidelines. 
 
1302.1 Access to State Highways 
• Access to state highways is regulated by the Arizona Department 
of Transportation (ADOT). 
• Encroachment permits for access to State Highways must be 
obtained from ADOT. 
 
1302.2 Access to City/Town Streets 
Access to city streets within incorporated areas is subject to regulation by 
the relevant city or town. Encroachment permits for access on these 
streets shall be obtained directly from the appropriate city or town. 
 
1302.3 Access to County Roads 
The County regulates access to roads and streets owned and maintained 
by the County. Any new construction intended to connect into County 
roads shall first obtain approval through a valid County encroachment 
permit.

Existing accesses to County roads, regardless of their current usage, shall 
not be modified or rebuilt without a County-issued encroachment permit. 
 
Encroachment permits shall be required for the following: 
• Property division, creating new parcels 
• Change in zoning 
• Significant change in structural modifications, remodeling, or 
business expansion 
• Use of the access increases in actual or proposed vehicular volume 
by 20 percent or more.  
• Directional characteristics, such as left turns, increases by 
20 percent or more. 
• Change in property use causes an impedance to the flow of traffic 
on the County road. 
• Relocations or realignments to existing driveways.  
• Changes in the type of traffic utilizing the access (usually an 
increase of larger heavier vehicles) increases by 20 percent or 
10 vehicles per day. 
• Modification of existing access  
• Private streets accessing County roads. 
• Direct access onto a County road has been in a state of non -use 
for more than four (4) years, and improvements are needed. 
 
The number of access points shall be minimized. Access points will only 
be approved if they are accompanied by an approved project site plan. 
 
Changes in advertising, landscaping, general maintenance, or aesthetics 
that do not impact internal or external traffic flow or safety do not require 
a new driveway permit. In general , any proposal that necessitates  a 
discretionary review will be considered a potential change of use. 
 
1302.4 Access to County Roads within National Forest, BLM, 
or State Trust 
Access to County roads within National Forest, BLM, or State Trust shall 
comply to Section 1302.3 and the following: obtaining prior approval from 
the landowner is required for access that connects to federal or privately 
owned land outside of County right-of-way, or if the access is solely within 
County right -of-way on federal or privately owned land . Furthermore,

1303 Intersections 
See Chapter 600 for intersections located within County Right-of-Way. 
 
Subdivision intersections shall be located per the County Subdivision 
Regulations. 
 
See Chapter 400  for traffic impact analysis associated with proposed 
developments. 
 
1303.1 New Intersections or Modifications to Existing 
Intersections 
A proposed development’s impacts to the capacity of an existing or 
proposed intersection shall be determined as part of the TIA. The TIA will 
identify the necessary improvements that need to be made. Unless there 
is a prior development agreement in place, full build-out improvements are 
required. 
 
1304 Driveways and Turnouts 
A driveway, also known as a turnout, refers to any access built within 
County right-of-way that connects the roadway to neighboring property 
without obstructing any sidewalks, border areas, streets, or roadways. 
See Chapter 600. 
 
1305 Mailboxes and Newspaper Delivery Boxes 
No mailbox or newspaper delivery box (hereafter referred to as mailbox) 
is allowed in the County’s rights-of way if it interferes with the safety of the 
traveling public or the function, maintenance, or operation of the highway 
system. A mailbox installati on that does not conform to the provisions of 
this regulation will be considered a safety hazard. Any violation could 
result in a written order requiring the owner to remove the safety hazard. 
If the safety hazard is not removed, the County will remove the  hazard 
and bill the owner. 
 
The mailbox owner is responsible for and shall hold the County harmless 
and defend any and all claims for personal injury and property damages 
that might be brought as a result of the installation and existence of 
mailboxes within County right-of-way. 
 
The property owner is solely responsible for mailbox maintenance.

All mailbox units, attachments, details, supports, and installation shall be 
in strict accordance with the United States Post Postal Service rules and 
regulations and in compliance with this Manual. 
 
1305.1 Mailbox Material 
Mailboxes shall be of light sheet metal or plastic construction conforming 
to the requirements of the U.S. Postal Service  and attached to a support 
structure (post) with sufficient strength to prevent the box from separating 
from the post if struck by a vehicle. Newspaper delivery boxes shall be of 
light sheet metal or plastic construction of minimum dimensions suitable 
for holding a newspaper. Heavy steel, cast iron, or decorative mailboxes 
are not allowed in County right-of-way.  
 
1305.2 Types of Mailboxes 
 
Table 1305.1 Typical Post Mounted Mailbox Size 
 
• Single: One mailbox on a single support. 
• Double: Two mailboxes on a single support. 
• Multiple: three to five mailboxes on a single support. A multiple 
mount is typically used  if there are three or more mailboxes at a 
single location.  
• Neighborhood Delivery and Collection Box Units: NDBCUs, or 
community mailboxes, are a type of mailbox installation that serves 
a large number of residents, such as at an apartment complex or 
mobile home part.  
 
1305.3 Mailbox Placement Considerations 
Proper placement of mailbox supports is the key to reasonable ease of 
service by postal carriers and the safety of carriers and other motorists. 
There are three placement considerations for mailboxes: the height of the 
mailbox above the road or shoulder surface, the lateral offset from the 
edge of the road, and the longitudinal placement within a turnout or from 
an intersection.

1305.3.1 Longitudinal Placement 
Longitudinal mailbox placement relates to the distance between a mailbox 
and other mailboxes, the beginning or end of the mailbox turnout, and an 
intersection (if the mailbox installation is close to an intersection). 
 
Distance between Individual Mailboxes and Mailbox 
Installations: There should be a separation of approximately 2 ft between 
single and multiple mount mailboxes or between a single/double mailbox 
installation and a multiple mailbox installation. There should be 
approximately 4 ft between adjacent multiple mailbox instal lations. 
Figure 1305.1 illustrates mailbox separation distances. 
 
Figure 1305.1 Approximate Distance between Mailbox Installations 
 
 
Road with Mailbox Turnout: There should be a minimum of 14 feet from 
the mailbox to the beginning of the 8 -foot-wide all-weather surface and a 
desirable distance of 6 feet from the last mailbox to the end of the 8-foot-
wide all -weather surface. Figure 1305.2 illustrates the longitudinal 
placement within a mailbox turnout.

acceptable location, preferably outside the clear zone and directly 
adjacent to the right-of-way line.  
 
1305.3.3 Exceptions 
Exception to the lateral placement criteria above may exist on residential 
streets and certain designated rural roads where the County deems it in 
the public interest to permit lesser clearances or to require greater 
clearances. 
 
1305.3.4 Very Low Volume Rural Roads 
Rural roads falling under this classification with low-operating speeds, the 
County may find it acceptable to offset mailboxes a minimum of 7  feet 
from the traveled ways and under some low-volume, low-speed conditions 
may find clearances as low as 30 inches acceptable. 
 
1305.3.5 Height 
The base of the mailbox should be installed at a typical height of 42 inches 
above the outside edge of the travel lane, shoulder, or turnout. 
Figure 1305.7 illustrates the height of mailboxes. 
 
Figure 1305.7 Height of Mailbox

1305.4.1 Types of Supports 
There are two general types of mailbox supports and specific hardware 
associated with each type of support: 
 
• Single Mailbox Support:  Any of these supports can be used to 
support a single mailbox.  
o Square Wood: A 4 x 4-inch square pressure treated wood 
post. 
o Round Wood: A 4 -inch-diameter round pressure treated 
wood post. 
o Thin-wall Steel Tube:  A 2 - to 2½ -inch diameter thin -wall 
steel tube. This type of post can be used with a small, 
medium, or large sized mailbox. 
o Channel Post: A 2 pound per foot channel post. This type 
of post can be used with a small or medium sized mailbox. 
• Double Mailbox Support:  This support is used to support two 
mailboxes on a single support. 
o Thin Wall Steel Tube:  A 2- to 2½-inch-diameter thin wall 
steel tube. 
o Channel Post: A 2 pound per foot channel post. 
• Multiple Support: Either of these supports can be used for three 
or more mailboxes. 
o Coat Hanger Support:  A 2 -inch-diameter thin -wall steel 
tube support frame that has a shape similar to an upside -
down coat hanger. See Figure 1305.8. 
 
Figure 1305.8 Coat Hanger Multiple Support

1305.5.1 Mailbox Bracket 
The mailbox bracket details should be of sufficient strength to prevent the 
box from separating from the post top if the installation is struck by a 
vehicle. The exact support hardware dimensions and design may vary, 
such as having a two -piece platform bracket, or alternative slot and hole 
locations. The product must result in a satisfactory attachment of the 
mailbox to the post, and all components must fit together properly. 
 
1305.6 Mailbox Attachments 
Several items can be attached to a mailbox or mailbox support, including 
an object marker, emergency location number, and newspaper tube.

1305.6.1 Object Markers on Mailbox Supports 
Object markers shall comply with the MUTCD. 
 
On two-lane, two-way roads, object markers shall be placed on both sides 
of the mailbox support. In other cases, mailboxes shall have a yellow 
Type 2 object marker facing traffic on the near side of the roadway. The 
Type 2 object marker can be either of the following: 
• A 6 -inch-wide by 12 -inch-tall rectangular unit with reflective 
sheeting bolted or affixed to the support. 
• A 12-inch strip of sheeting wrapped around the support post. 
 
The top of the Type 2 object marker should be 6 -8 inches below the 
bottom of the mailbox. Figure 1305.14 and Figure 1305.15 illustrate the 
use of the object marker on mailbox supports.

1305.6.3 Newspaper Tube 
A lightweight tube for newspaper delivery can be attached to a mailbox 
support if the tube meets all of the following conditions: 
• It does not touch any mailboxes. 
• It is mounted below the mailbox and above the object marker. 
• It does not extend beyond the front of the mailbox. 
• It does not display any advertising other than the name of the 
newspaper. 
• It does not present a hazard to traffic or to mail delivery. 
 
The newspaper tube should be placed on the downstream side of the post 
so that an object marker can be placed on the side facing traffic. See 
Figure 1305.17.

1400 General Information 
The County Drafting Guidelines sets forth requirements and regulates all 
CADD production by County personnel, consultants, and contractors. 
 
This manual is a living document. The County will update this manual 
when necessary. 
 
All plan sheets shall be 22” x 34”. 
 
1400.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to define the rules and regulations, and 
guidelines for visually communicating a project design. 
 
1400.2 Applicability 
These standards shall apply to electronic drafting files associated with 
construction and reconstruction plans of transportation facilities or as 
required by the County. 
 
1400.3 Software 
All files shall be submitted in AutoCAD DWG file format. AutoCAD version 
shall be verified with the County prior to commencing work. 
 
1401 Submittals 
Most projects will require two types of submittals. The first is a hard copy 
submittal and the second is an electronic file submittal. For specific 
submittal requirements, refer to the project scope of work. 
 
For most projects, there are two types of submittals required with a 
submittal. The first is a hard copy submittal and the second is an electronic 
file submittal. For specific submittal requirements refer to the project 
scope of work.  
  
Electronic submittals consist of an “electronic project” on approved media. 
Refer to the “electronic projects” section of this Chapter and the project 
scope of work for specific requirements.

• External hard drive with USB interface connection  
• External thumb drive with USB interface connection  
• Compact Disc (CD)  
• Digital Versatile Disc (DVD)  
• Alternatively, files can be sent via secure FTP site.  
 
Note: S ubmitted media will not be returned  and o ther media may be 
delivered as approved by the County. 
 
1402 Electronic Projects 
Digital information associated with a project from conceptual design to as-
built plans will be stored in an electronic project. The directory structure of 
an electronic project will be used to store the CADD graphics files, survey, 
and engineering data fil es. Digital terrain models, project transmittals, 
letters, memos, and spreadsheets are also stored in an electronic project. 
The directory will be archived in its entirety to preserve the complete 
project.

and their files below a project directory (the picture below shows an 
example directory structure of an electronic project).

1402.2 Electronic Project Directories 
 
1402.2.1 Project Directory 
For County projects, the project folder name shall use the project number 
assigned by the County. 
 
No files will be placed directly under the project directory folder. 
 
1402.2.2 Data Directory 
The data directory contains project data not specifically associated with 
the design file graphics (i.e., correspondence, memos, transmittals, 
reports, etc.). 
 
Any file type or content may be placed in this location and subdirectories 
may be used. 
 
1402.2.3 Design Support Directory 
The Design Support directory includes all files used to support the design 
file graphics. Examples of design support files include all existing and 
proposed digital terrain models, geometry alignments, ASCII survey files, 
etc. 
 
Files should be limited to those used in the creation and/or modification of 
the design file graphics.  
 
Directory Name Content / General File Type Description 
Project The top-level directory of an electronic project.  
_data_ Used for Civil 3D shortcut information, survey files, and 
other related files. 
DesignSupport Files that are used in coordination with design graphics, 
such as block libraries, custom linetypes, aerial inages etc. 
DWG Design graphics that are used  in the plan set production 
and contains the plan sheets. Additional folders may be 
added. 
Plot A PDF for each sheet in a set of plans or files used to 
configure a printer/plotter.

1402.2.4 Design File Directory (DWG) 
The design file directory is where all AutoCad and Civil3D files are stored. 
It provides a single location for all project DWG files with the intent that no 
files will have broken paths if they are all located in the same directory. 
 
1402.2.5 Plot Directory 
The plot directory contains PDF files that are created. 
 
Only PDF files should be located here and must exactly match the hard 
copy delivered.

1404.1 Design Support Files  
Design Support files create or modify the design graphics. They can be 
Civil3D files or AutoCAD resource files that modify the look of the design 
graphics. This section deals only with symbology and feature names 
inside Civil3D files. 
 
1404.1.1 Geometry Naming 
It is recommended to have one alignment per file and the name of the file 
shall be named using a two -letter identifier, the road name or clarifying 
description, and a numeric designation.  
  
XX-Description_## 
  
For instance, the first centerline alignment for First Street would be called 
CL-FirstStreet_01. The approved two -letter identifiers are shown in the 
table on the following page.  
  
Vertical alignments and superelevation designs may be named the same 
as their parent horizontal alignment or simply named Profile.  
  
It is recommended to include metadata when creating any horizontal 
alignment, vertical alignment, or superelevation. The following information 
should be included: Creation date, designer name, start station location, 
or any additional information that is e asily understood by any future 
designer or reviewer.

1404.1.2 Templates 
Templates are divided into three zones: 
• Zone 1: points used in creating the roadway pavement (a.k.a. 
backbone) 
• Zone 2: points used to construct roadway shoulders. 
• Zone 3: all other points used for creating end conditions. 
 
Point names should be designated as right or left. For instance, a right 
roadway shoulder point name would be SH_Rt and a left shoulder point 
name would be SH_Lt.  
 
If more than one of a particular point type is given within a zone, a numeric 
qualifier should be added to the point name before the left or right 
designation.

1404.1.3 Corridors 
Corridor names should match the associated alignment name. Additional 
information should also be included to assist future designers or reviewers 
in understanding the purpose and location of the corridor. 
 
1405 Design File Content 
 
1405.1 Base Files 
The concept of base files is important because a design change made to 
the base file is reflected on each of the sheet files. Base files contain 
graphical data that is created during the design of a project. Base files are 
always created on a one -to-one scale. Each base file contains elements 
of a certain type. For example, a utility base reference file contains data 
such as telephone lines. When deciding what belongs in a base file versus 
what belongs in a sheet file it is helpful to think of the base file as “what is 
existing” or “what will be built” and a sheet file as “instructions on how to 
build it”. The table below lists all base files. 
 
Table 1405.1 Base File Naming

appear in the plans.

These guidelines apply to the naming of new levels created in a base file.  
• The name of the new level must start with the name of an existing 
level in the base file. 
• Append the new level with a plus (+) sign. “Bd_Barrier+Cones” is 
an example of appending “Cones” to the existing level “Bd_Barrier”. 
• Do not create levels with duplicate purposes within the same base 
file. If the level “Bd_RoadEdgeUnpaved” exists don’t create a level 
named “Bd_Road+EdgeDirt”.  
• Place all nouns before adjectives when naming new levels. Put 
“Edge” (noun) before “Unpaved” (adjective) when creating the 
Bd_Road+EdgeUnpaved level.

1405.2 Sheet Files 
Sheet files are the eventual products of a CADD-produced design. A sheet 
file represents the assembly of several of the base files to present the data 
required for a plan sheet. Each sheet file has a one-to-one correlation with 
a physical plan sheet. To pr oduce the plan set, reference base files are 
created, then sheet files. Annotation and symbols placed in sheet files 
must be placed at a set scale corresponding to the desired plot scale.

1407.2 Gray Scale and RGB Values 
Gray scaling is a method used in a CAD file to “gray out”, or dither, a 
specified portion of the design to visually depress the boldness of the 
features. For example, this method is used to reference existing survey 
features, to “dull” their appearance vis ually on the screen, and to 
additionally invoke the plotting output to be “shaded”. This proves 
beneficial in diminishing the focus on the existing survey while enhancing 
the proposed design, allowing the designer to see existing and proposed 
features together on the same design plan sheet.  
 
All gray scaling should be done in the CAD file by modifying the ByLayer 
symbology and/or overrides.

1407.3 Line Weights 
The line weight assignment is designated a thickness that is noticeable in 
the final printing/plotting of the design file. These preassigned values have 
been calculated to properly display the line weights in a PDF file at full 
scale and at half scale.  
 
(ANSI D Size – 22” x 34”, Half scale plot ANSI B Size – 11” x 17”) 
 
Using plot styles is recommended. Color -dependent plot style tables set 
style based on the color of the object. CTB files manages line weight 
through the graphic use of colors. Entity colors are mapped to logical 
pens, and each pen has an assigned value fo r thickness and tone. The 
designer is then capable of visualizing a plotted drawing by looking at the 
colors on the screen. Named plot styles (STB) can be assigned to an 
object independent of color. This allows objects to have a specific line 
weight and color by layer. Table 1407.3 is an example of a typical Color 
Table.

1407.4 Custom Linetypes 
Fundamental line work in drawings consist of the following linetypes: 
Continuous, Centerlines, Hidden lines, Dashed lines, multiple Fence and 
utility lines and Phantom lines. There are any number of linetypes that 
may be incorporated into drawings. 
 
Custom linetype symbologies shall follow the latest edition the Maricopa 
County Department of Transportation (MCDOT) CADD Standards 
OpenRoads Designer Version.  
  
LTSCALE is the AutoCAD line scale variable. In drawings with decimal 
units the Ltscale is normally set to the scale in which the drawing will be 
plotted, i.e 1’=40’ LTSCALE =40. In architectural drawings the LTSCALE 
is a multiplier used to scale up line definitions to fit the drawings plotted 
scale. For example, a drawing scale of 1/16"=1' -0" will have a LTSCALE 
of 192 for model space, 1/4” = 1’ -0” a LTSCALE of 48 and so forth. The 
zoom factor will then be 1/192 XP or 1/48 XP in the paperspace viewports 
to achieve the appropriate scale and linetype. The LTSCALE is applied to 
the linetype definitions used in the drawing to provide proportional spacing 
for all linework.

PSLTSCALE is an AutoCAD system variable in Realease12 and above. 
AutoCAD drawings that use single viewports should set this variable to 0. 
Hence the linetype scale will be the same as the model ltscale. The 
PSLTSCALE shall be set to "1" on drawings with mu ltiple view ports with 
multiple scales. This will enable all linetypes to be plotted according to the 
viewport scale factor (zoom XP). Drawings such as Detail Sheets may 
have numerous viewports of varying scales. All the linetypes will look the 
same when handled in this manner.

2. Work shall not be conducted between dusk and dawn, only during daylight hours. 
3. Work shall not be conducted on holiday weekends, or within twenty -four hours proceeding a holiday weekend unless specifically authorized as an

4. Litter pickup shall not be performed within six feet of the traveled way, upon bridges, culverts, medians or structures of any kind.

The intent of this form is to provide guidance for deviations from the approved Engineering Design and Construction Manual. 
Specifically, this outline details the three waiver types (Administrative, Technical and Design) and the respective fees for 
each type of request, accompanying timelines, the decision appeal process, acceptable justification for a waiver, as well as 
specific examples of types of waivers. The fees shown below cover the County staff time to administrate the application. 
All fees are non -refundable regardless of whether the County approves the waiver request. All engineering analysis is 
required to be sealed by a Professional Engineer in good standing in the State of Arizona.  
 
The following is required to be submitted with Waiver Request Form: 
 
 Fees associated with the application. 
 • Administrative Waiver ($100) 
• Technical Waiver ($250) 
• Design Waiver ($450) 
 
 Completed and signed Waiver Request Form. 
 County staff will determine if the Waiver Request Form is Technically Complete. If so, a notice of Technical Completion 
and a receipt for the filing fee will be sent to the applicant within fifteen (15) days of submittal of the form. Also, if th e 
form is deemed to not be Technically Complete, the applicant will receive notice within fifteen (15) days of submittal of 
the form. 
 
2 copies of the following: 
 Narrative describing the project as well as the proposed deviation submitted with the Waiver Request Form. The 
narrative shall include the following: 
 a. Section of Navajo County Engineering Design and Construction Manual and/or the Technical Specification or 
Standard Detail which relates to the proposed deviation. 
b. Justification for the proposed deviation - A detailed explanation stating the extraordinary factors that does not 
allow for the strict adherence to the County standard(s) or code justifying approval according to the Approval 
Criteria (See Page EW-3). 
c. Address the potential impact on the public infrastructure system (safety, functionality, maintainability).  
d. Any additional documentation and background information that is required to support the  request. 
 
 Engineering Analysis including supporting documentation, (i.e., traffic studies, structural analysis, hydraulic and 
hydrologic assessment, water and sewer reports, typical sections, alternative designs, etc.) for technical or design 
waivers. 
 
Forms without the required information will not be accepted. If you have questions regarding submittal requirements, you 
may call the 928-524-4100.

<!-- page 505 -->
Phone: (928) 524-4100  100 W Public Works Drive 
Office Hours: M-F 7:30 – 5:00 EW-2 Holbrook, AZ 86025 
 
Engineering Waiver Type 
(please check the appropriate box) 
 Administrative Waiver 
 
Minor deviations a) do not involve safety or offsite impacts, b) involve minimal review, c) do not involve broad public 
interest, d) are similar to other approved modifications, and e) occur routinely.  
Examples of Administrative Waiver include: 
 • Minor access spacing changes when no alternative is feasible. 
• A minor increase in the maximum number of lots served by driveways. 
• Reduced cross sectional requirements, in order to match existing roadway and curbs.  
Filing fee in the amount of:  Contact County for Waiver Fees 
 Technical Waiver 
 
Moderate deviations a) require limited engineering analysis and County review, b) have minimal expected safety 
impacts, c) have minimal potential offsite impacts, and d) generate minimal public interest.  
Examples of a Technical Waiver include: 
 Use of attached sidewalk in lieu of detached sidewalks based on site conditions.  
Use of roll curb and gutter in lieu of vertical curb and gutter. 
Removal of on-street parking. 
Modification to medians, access locations or lane channelization when no offsite impacts result.  
Filing fee in the amount of:  Contact County for Waiver Fees 
 Design Waiver 
 
Major deviation are unique cases that have the potential for significant impacts to the public or County and require 
extensive analysis and documentation. 
Examples of a Design Waiver include: 
 • Alternative roadway pavement design. 
• Reduced left turn or right turn pocket storage. 
• Cross circulation or roadway spacing changes when the obligation may be passed on to  other 
properties. 
• Design changes concerning traffic or pedestrian safety. 
• Access changes with potential material impacts to other parties. 
• Pre-development versus post-development detention or retention requirements. 
Filing fee in the amount of:  Contact County for Waiver Fees 
 
The initial ruling will be made by the County Engineering Department. The initial ruling will include a verification that the 
applicant has appropriately classified the waiver type (i.e. Administrative, Technical, or Design). Appeals can be made 
to County Engineer by including a copy of the waiver request and all supportin g documents and calculations, along 
with a letter describing in detail the reasons for the appeal. 
Failure to comply with the approved or conditionally approved waiver will be cause for  
1. Denial or revocation of engineering plan approvals and permits. 
2. Withholding or release of financial assurances. 
3. Removal and reconstruction. 
4. Delay of final inspection. 
5. Delay or denial of final approval. 
6. Denial of occupancy certificates (temporary and permanent). 
7. Notice to surety or other financial institution and/or legal action for forfeiture of financial  assurances. 
8. Code enforcement. 
9. Any other applicable penalties as provided by law.

Engineering Waiver Approval Criteria 
(for County use) 
In reviewing a Waiver request, the County shall consider the applicable factors that include, but are not limited 
to, the following: 
   
Yes No  
  Does the waiver violate or circumvent Federal or State Regulations?  
   
  Would granting the waiver create an undesirable precedent?  
   
  Will the proposed alternative provide a reasonable alternative to the current Standards and comparable 
level of protection to the public and County staff? 
   
  Does the strict application of the code requirement or Standard place an undue burden on the property 
inconsistent with the burden placed on other properties in similar situations under similar circumstances?  
   
  Does the strict application of the code requirement or Standard have an unreasonable adverse impact on 
the property owner’s ability to the reasonably use their property? 
   
  Will the proposed alternative adversely impact the operation and maintenance of the drainage, 
transportation, or utility infrastructure? 
   
  Is the proposed alternative consistent with the adopted regional, area or neighborhood plan?  
   
  Did applicant provide necessary documents to evaluate the proposed variance? See list of some 
possible documents under Engineering Analysis on Page 1. 
   
  Does the proposed waiver create a public health and safety issue? 
   
  Does the proposed waiver create undo financial hardship to the general public?  
   
All circumstances of the situation will be considered.

 CONTRACT FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES 
 
AGREEMENT made as of January 28, 2025, between Navajo County ("County") 
and Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. (“Consultant”). 
 
WHEREAS, County requires certain professional services for Navajo County Water 
and Wastewater Master Plan (“Project”); and 
 
WHEREAS, Consultant represents that it has the necessary expertise to provide such 
services in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows: 
 
1. Services.  Consultant shall perform the work described in Attachment A, Scope of 
Services and Fee Estimate dated January 9, 2025, in a competent and professional 
manner to the satisfaction of County.  The Scope of Services and the Consultant’s 
schedule and fee proposal are attached hereto and by this reference incorporated 
herein. 
 
2. Contract Documents. The Contract Documents comprise this Contract, Attachment 
A Scope of Services and Fee Estimate dated January 9, 2025, and addenda thereto, if 
any. If any incorporated term is inconsistent with the Contract, this Contract shall 
control. 
 
3. Consultant’s Expertise.  Consultant warrants that it has the ability, authority, 
capacity and professional expertise to perform this Agreement.  Consultant shall 
provide an adequate staff of experienced personnel, capable of and devoted to the 
successful accomplishment of the work to be performed hereunder.  Consultant shall 
assign specific individuals to key positions.  Once assigned to work under this 
Agreement, key personnel shall not be removed or replaced without County’s prior 
written approval.  
 
4. Independent Contractor.  Consultant acknowledges that it is an independent 
contractor.  Neither party is or shall purport to be an agent, employee, partner, joint 
venturer or associate of the other.  An employee or agent of one party shall not be 
deemed an employer or agent  of the other party for any purpose.  Taxes or Social 
Security contributions will not be withheld from any payment by County, and 
Consultant shall be solely responsible for such matters.

5. Subcontracts.  Consultant shall not enter into any subcontract with respect to any of 
the work to be performed hereunder without County’s prior written approval.  All 
subcontracts shall comply with applicable federal and state laws and regulations and 
shall impose on the subcontractor substantially the same obligations as are imposed 
on Consultant by this Agreement with respect to those matters covered by Sections 9, 
10, 11, 13, 16, 19, 22 and 23.  Consultant is responsible for full performance of this 
Agreement regardless of whether subcontractors are used. 
 
6. Time for Completion.  Consultant’s services will be provided in a manner consistent 
with the degree of car e and skill ordinarily exercised by members of the same 
profession currently practicing under similar circumstances.  Consultant’s services 
shall be performed as expeditiously as is consistent with professional skill and care 
and the orderly progress of the Project, and in accordance with an agreed upon 
schedule for the performance of the Services hereunder.  Time limits established by a 
schedule approved by County shall not, except for reasonable cause, be exceeded by 
County or Consultant.  The Schedule shall be adjusted, if necessary, as the Project 
proceeds.  The date for final performance shall be extended by the number of days 
that performance is delayed by governmental approval or review procedures or other 
causes beyond Consultant’s reasonable control, as jointly confirmed in writing by the 
parties’ representatives. 
 
7. Payment.  County shall pay to Consultant a not-to-exceed sum of sixty-eight 
thousand dollars ($68, 000.00) as payment in full for all services rendered by 
Consultant pursuant to this Agreement.  Payments shall be made within 30 days of 
County’s receipt of Consultant’s monthly invoices.  Each invoice shall detail the work 
performed during the billing period.  Invoice amounts in percent of Project cost shall 
not exceed the percentage of completion of the Project as approved by County.   
 
8. Defects in Work.  County may reject any work product that fails to meet customary 
professional standards or Project specifications.  Consultant agrees to promptly 
remedy all such deficiencies.  The parties shall make a good faith effort to resolve any 
controversy or claim through informal negotiation as set forth in Section 1 3.  No 
compensation shall be paid for any rejected work until such issues have been 
resolved. 
 
9. Insurance Requirements.   
 
A. Consultant shall maintain in effect, at all times during the term of this 
Agreement, insurance adequate to protect County and its agents, 
representatives, officers, officials and employees against such losses as set 
forth below.  Consultant shall provide County with a current Certificate of 
Insurance or a certified copy of the insurance policy naming County as an 
additional insured (except for Errors and Omissions / Professional Liability 
coverage). 
 
B. The following types and amounts of insurance are required as minimums:

the Agreement exceeds the cost of finishing the work (including any expenses 
incurred by County as a result of Consultant’s default), Consultant shall be 
entitled to payment for its performance up to the amount of such excess.  If the

difference to County.

terminate this Agreement in whole or part when in the sole discretion of County it

a reasonable allowance for profit and overhead, provided that such payments,

ATTACHMENT “A”  January 9, 2025 
 
ATTACHMENT “A” 
 
Water and Wastewater Master Plan                                     Scope of Services 
Navajo County 
 
 
Project Understanding 
 
To build upon the water resource goals and initiatives within the ongoing/draft 2050 Navajo County 
Comprehensive Plan, the County has asked Kimley-Horn to provide a proposal for a Water and 
Wastewater Master Plan. Please see below for specifics for each task. 
 
Scope of Services 
 
 
Water and Wastewater Master Plan 
 
1. Water/Wastewater Master Plan Framework: Kimley-Horn will host meetings with Navajo County 
staff to identify goals including but not limited to: 
 
• Identifying, mapping, and reviewing critical water and wastewater facilities across the county 
(treatment plants, storage tanks, transmission mains, joint service area infrastructure, etc.) 
• Encouraging expansion of water and sewer systems in populated areas. 
• Identifying opportunities for County to facilitate long-term investments. 
• Supporting upgrades to water and sewer districts that are out of compliance with ADEQ.  
• Updating subdivision requirements to ensure developers are adequately collecting, 
conveying, and ultimately treating wastewater. 
• Building upon the County’s stewardship of overall water supply portfolio including potential 
reuse, recharge, and conservation opportunities. 
• Quantifying fire suppression concerns and current/desired requirements. 
Goals identified within this task will be evaluated throughout the entirety of this master planning effort. 
Findings and recommendations will be documented within a Master Plan “Roadmap” report. Along with 
recommendations the Roadmap will provide guidance for continual implementation and follow up steps 
for each goal. 
2. Detailed Population and Flow Projections: Building upon high level population projections 
identified within the currently drafted 2050 Navajo County Comprehensive Plan, Kimley-Horn will 
provide more detailed water and wastewater flow projections for key communities/systems within 
Navajo County. Flow projections will be used to prioritize need and provide context for goals 
discussed above. 
 
2.1. Water Flow Projections 
2.1.1. Average Day, Peak Day, and Fire Demands. 
2.1.2. Projections to be quantified by community/system. 
2.2. Wastewater Flow projections 
2.2.1. Average Daily Flows, Peak Dry and Wet Weather Flows. Wet weather flows will be 
dependent on available flow monitoring data from utilities. 
2.2.2. Projections to be quantified by community/system. 
 
3. County-Wide Water and Wastewater Mapping: Kimley-Horn will coordinate with utilities to collect 
and digitize available system mapping. Key/critical infrastructure will be mapped only (treatment 
plants, storage tanks, larger pump stations/lift stations, sewer interceptors, water transmission mains,

<!-- page 545 -->
Navajo County Water and Wastewater Master Plan  Page 2 of 2 
ATTACHMENT “A”  January 9, 2025 
 
joint service area infrastructure, etc.). 
 
3.1. Water and Wastewater Geodatabase Generation 
3.1.1. Service Area and Designated Management Areas. 
3.1.2. Jurisdictional Limits. 
3.1.3. Infrastructure by utility by type. 
3.1.4. Infrastructure size (diameter). 
3.1.5. Infrastructure capacity (permitted) 
3.1.6. Effluent quality (if available) 
3.1.7. Geodatabase will be provided at close of task/project. 
3.2. Maps and Mapbooks 
3.2.1. Kimley-Horn will generate maps in ArcGIS Pro and will provide ArcGIS Pro .aprx files to 
County. 
3.2.2. Kimley-Horn expects to generate an overall water map, an overall wastewater map, and 
a mapbook zooming in on specific communities/systems. 
 
It is important to note that Kimley-Horn will work alongside the County to help facilitate sharing of 
data from each community/utility. Additionally, Kimley-Horn will partner with County to host meetings 
with all stakeholders. 
 
4. Review Standard/Policies and Provide Recommendations: Kimley-Horn will review available 
policies and planning and design standards. After review and evaluation Kimley-Horn will provide 
recommendations to implement new standards/strategies to support: development, environmental 
compliance, water quality, expansion, and conservation. Recommendations will be provided within 
the Roadmap report discussed above. 
 
 
Fee Estimate 
Task 1 – Water/Wastewater Master Plan Framework $  20,000 
Task 2 – Detailed Population and Flow Projections $    8,000 
Task 3 – County-Wide Water and Wastewater Mapping $  30,000 
Task 4 – Review of Standard/Policies $  10,000 
Total: $  68,000

PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number 03-2025,
approving/denying a Master Development Plan Amendment for Phases II, III, and IV of White Mountain
Lake Vistas, which allowed for a total of 216 single-family lots, to a new Master Development Plan
which will allow for 24 single-family lots, 133 manufactured homes, 133 multi-family units, storage and
parking facilities, existing golf course, and undisturbed/recreation area in the White Mountain Lakes area.
Background:
There is an existing, approved Master Development Plan for the subject site.  This Master Development
Plan was approved by the Board of Supervisors on December 20, 2004 and allowed for two-hundred
sixteen (216) single-family lots in the three unfinished phases of a four-phased, three-hundred (300) unit,
development.  Phase I of this development was platted in 2005 and amended in 2006.  This first phase
consists of eighty-four (84) single-family lots.  Phases II, III, and IV were never completed and are all
contained within the boundary of the subject parcel, APN # 304-21-371Q.  These phases are those being
requested to be amended with this proposal.
This project is designed to contain the following components: 
A maximum of two-hundred ninety (290) residential units, designated as follows: 
Twenty-four (24) single-family residential lots, on approximately 5.56-acres.
One-hundred thirty-three (133) manufactured home residential lots, on approximately
23.9-acres.
One-hundred thirty-three (133) multiple-family residential units on a total of approximately
7.38-acres.
An existing golf course, owned and maintained by Juniper Ridge Resort (approximately 3.0-acres)
An undisturbed creek bed area on the eastern boundary of the property, totaling approximately
16.0-acres.
Storage and parking.
One convenience store.
Connection to an existing water system.
Connection to an existing sewer system.
Recommendation: 
Navajo County Planning & Development Services Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning
Commission recommend approval of the Master Development Plan Amendment, subject to the conditions
listed in the Staff Report.

REQUEST DESCRIPTION:
Consideration of a request by Allen Land Development, LLC for a Master Development Plan
Amendment for Phases II, III, and IV of White Mountain Lake Vistas, which allowed for a total
of 216 single-family lots, to a new Master Development Plan which will allow for 24 single-
family lots, 133 manufactured homes, 133 multi-family units, storage and parking facilities,
golf course, and undisturbed/recreation area in the White Mountain Lakes area. APN#: 304-
21-371Q, T11N, R22E, S15 of the GSRM. Owner: Allen Land Development, LLC.  Agent:
Virginia Senior.
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:
To the north of this proposal are single-family residential subdivisions, known as White
Mountain Lake Vistas Unit I and White Mountain Lakes Unit VIII.  To the west of this property
is a Park Model/RV subdivision known as Juniper Ridge Resort.  To the east of this property
is a single-family residential subdivision, known as White Mountain Lakes Unit III.  To the
south of the subject property is State Land.
BACKGROUND/HISTORY:
There is an existing, approved Master Development Plan for the subject site.  This Master
Development Plan was approved by the Board of Supervisors on December 20, 2004 and
allowed for two-hundred sixteen (216) single-family lots in the three unfinished phases of a
four-phased, three-hundred (300) unit, development.  Phase I of this development was platted
in 2005 and amended in 2006.  This first phase consists of eighty-four (84) single-family lots.
Phases II, III, and IV were never completed and are all contained within the boundary of the
subject parcel, APN # 304-21-371Q.  These phases are those being requested to be amended
with this proposal.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
This project is designed to contain the following components:
 A maximum of two-hundred ninety (290) residential units, designated as follows:
o Twenty-four (24) single-family residential lots, on approximately 5.56-acres.
o One-hundred thirty-three (133) manufactured home residential lots, on
approximately 23.9-acres.
o One-hundred thirty-three (133) multiple-family residential units on a total of
approximately 7.38-acres.
 An existing golf course, owned and maintained by Juniper Ridge Resort (approximately
3.0-acres)
 An undisturbed creek bed area on the eastern boundary of the property, totaling
approximately 16.0-acres.
 Storage and parking.
 One convenience store.
 Connection to an existing water system.
 Connection to an existing sewer system.

ZONING DISTRICT:
ARTICLE  17 – (SD) – SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT ZONE
Section 1701 – Purpose
1. The purpose of the Special Development zone is to provide for the development of
subdivisions and other land use projects containing various dwelling types, necessary
commercial centers, off street parking areas, open space areas for recreation, and to preserve
a rural atmosphere.
2. Deviations from design standards for the specific zone or zones may be permitted provided
open spaces are developed and maintained for the use of the residents and provided further
that the parcel size, soil conditions, terrain, ground cover and other significant natural
features favor this type of development.

in the Zoning Ordinance for alternative housing types and patterns, planned

originally approved Master Development Plan.  Rather than being solely single-
family site-built residential, this site would allow for single-family site-built,
manufactured homes, and multi-family housing.
Goal 5: Improve the overall appearance of the County.

cultural resources, protecting wildlife habitat, natural plant communities, and riparian
areas, and encouraging protection of scenic vistas.
 The applicants have indicated that they will leave approximately 16.0 acres of
creek bed area undisturbed with their development.
Goal 6: Maintain compatible land use patterns while encouraging development.

including, but not limited to, setbacks, walls or fences, and landscaping.

Analysis:

<!-- page 555 -->
Rock Creek Development MDP-A
Board of Supervisors           P a g e6 | 
The proposed Master Development Plan Amendment meets all relevant goals and policies of
the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan.  The proposal provides a variety and flexibility of
housing, commercial development sited directly off a paved thoroughfare, is in a community
with fire and medical service, has multiple points of access proposed, connectivity proposed
with existing and unfinished roadway, leaves an existing riparian area untouched, while
providing a buffer with this untouched area, and looks to utilize existing water and sewer
infrastructure.
When looking at the neighborhood surrounding this development, there are a variety of
residential uses, all of which are closely related to this proposal.  Juniper Ridge Resort is a Park
Model/Recreational Vehicle subdivision and has five-hundred twenty-nine (529) lots on
approximately 138.75 acres, with an approximate density of 3.81 dwelling units per acre
(du/ac).  White Mountain Lake Vistas Unit I is a single-family residential subdivision with
eighty-four (84) lots on approximately 21.97 acres, with an approximate density of 3.82
dwelling units per acre (du/ac).  White Mountain Lake Unit III is a single-family residential
subdivision with three-hundred seventy-six (376) dwelling units on approximately 120.93
acres, with an approximate density of 3.11 dwelling units per acre (du/ac).
This proposal includes manufactured home lots adjacent to Juniper Ridge Resort, single-
family residential adjacent to White Mountain Lake Vistas Unit I, and an undisturbed creek
bed area adjacent to White Mountain Lake Unit III.  There are also commercial uses adjoining
Silver Creek Drive and multiple-family development within the interior of the property.  This
development includes up to a maximum of two-hundred ninety (290) dwelling units on
approximately 67.20 acres, with an approximate density of 4.32 dwelling units per acre
(du/ac).
Planning and Development Services Staff have received eleven (11) comments against this
proposal as of January 16th, 2025.  Comments against this project have primarily been focused
on a lack of age restriction being addressed, manufactured homes being proposed, multiple-
family apartments not being desirable/needed, not needing additional RV and vehicle storage,
camping on-site, ability for existing roadways to handle traffic, impact on water and sewer
infrastructure, density, impact on wildlife and environment, crime, and noise.
At the Thursday, December 19 th, 2024 Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission
Hearing, this item was recommended for approval to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors.

This item has been noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised Statutes and

The proposed amendments meet several applicable goals within Navajo County’s
Comprehensive Plan, as noted within this report.

PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT SERVICES RECOMMENDATION:
The Navajo County Planning and Development Services Staff and the Navajo County Planning and
Zoning Commission recommend approval of the Master Development Plan Amendment, subject to
the following conditions:
1. All Federal, State, and Navajo County permits required for each lot must be obtained and
adhered to.
2. This Master Development Site Plan shall allow for a maximum of two-hundred ninety (290)
residential units.  Of these two-hundred ninety (290) residential units, there shall be a
maximum of twenty-four (24) single-family residential lots, one-hundred thirty-three (133)
manufactured home residential lots, and one-hundred thirty-three (133) multiple-family
residential units.

<!-- page 557 -->
Rock Creek Development MDP-A
Board of Supervisors           P a g e8 | 
3. Any commercial development within this Master Development Plan Amendment shall
require Site Plan Review approval from the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission,
prior to development.
4. A Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA), Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer
Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report for the
development, prepared by a Professional Engineer, licensed in the State of Arizona, shall be
submitted to and approved by the County Engineer’s office before the Tentative Plat and/or
Site Plan Review is submitted to the Planning and Zoning Commission.
5. All required offsite improvements identified in the TIA, Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain
Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design
Report shall be constructed or financially assured before the stage of development is
constructed that requires the improvement.
6. Sufficient off-road drainage easements shall be made available to accommodate major
drainage as required.
7. Drainage structures, including detention or retention ponds, shall be proposed with the Final
Plat and/or Site Plan Review, as required.
8. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations shall be met before approval of the
Tentative Plat and/or Site Plan Review. Variances shall be requested in accordance with
Section 4.12.
9. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations and Requirements, Flood Control
Ordinance, Building Safety Ordinance, and applicable codes shall be adhered to and approved
at the proper Tentative Plat, Final, or Building Permit and construction phase (to include,
without limitation, the Traffic Impact Analysis, Drainage Study, Floodplain Study,
Construction Improvement Plans, and Grading Plans).
10. Approval of the Master Development Site Plan is conditioned upon the submittal for a request
for either a Tentative Plat or for a Site Plan Review to the Planning and Zoning Commission,
along with proof of compliance with the above conditions, within 24 months of the date of
Board of Supervisors Resolution. If this condition is not met, approval shall be revoked, and
the Master Development Site Plan shall become null and void. This condition shall be
conclusively deemed to have been satisfied unless the Board of Supervisors causes a notice of
revocation to be recorded in the Office of the Navajo County Recorder within 30 days after
the expiration of the 24-month period (or any extension thereof).

RECOMMENDATION
Navajo County Planning and Development Services Staff
recommend approval of the Master Development Plan
Amendment for Rock Creek Development, subject to 10
conditions:
MDP-A 24-002 13
1. All Federal, State, and Navajo County permits required for each lot must be obtained and adhered to.
2. This Master Development Site Plan shall allow for a maximum of two-hundred ninety (290) residential units.  Of these two-hundred ninety (290) residential units,
there shall be a maximum of twenty-four (24) single-family residential lots, one-hundred thirty-three (133) manufactured home residential lots, and one-hundred
thirty-three (133) multiple-family residential units.
3. Any commercial development within this Master Development Plan Amendment shall require Site Plan Review approval from the Navajo County Planning and
Zoning Commission, prior to development.
4. A Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA), Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report
for the development, prepared by a Professional Engineer, licensed in the State of Arizona, shall be submitted to and approved by the County Engineer’s office before
the Tentative Plat and/or Site Plan Review is submitted to the Planning and Zoning Commission.
5. All required offsite improvements identified in the TIA, Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection System Design Report, and Water
Distribution Design Report shall be constructed or financially assured before the stage of development is constructed that requires the improvement.
6. Sufficient off-road drainage easements shall be made available to accommodate major drainage as required.
7. Drainage structures, including detention or retention ponds, shall be proposed with the Final Plat and/or Site Plan Review, as required.
8. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations shall be met before approval of the Tentative Plat and/or Site Plan Review. Variances shall be requested
in accordance with Section 4.12.
9. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations and Requirements, Flood Control Ordinance, Building Safety Ordinance, and applicable codes shall be
adhered to and approved at the proper Tentative Plat, Final, or Building Permit and construction phase (to include, without limitation, the Traffic Impact Analysis,
Drainage Study, Floodplain Study, Construction Improvement Plans, and Grading Plans).
10. Approval of the Master Development Site Plan is conditioned upon the submittal for a request for either a Tentative Plat or for a Site Plan Review to the Planning
and Zoning Commission, along with proof of compliance with the above conditions, within 24 months of the date of Board of Supervisors Resolution. If this condition
is not met, approval shall be revoked, and the Master Development Site Plan shall become null and void. This condition shall be conclusively deemed to have been
satisfied unless the Board of Supervisors causes a notice of revocation to be recorded in the Office of the Navajo County Recorder within 30 days after the expiration
of the 24-month period (or any extension thereof).
