<!-- page 575 -->
INTRODUCTION 
The Rock Creek development, located in the White Mountain Lakes Estate area of Navajo 
County, Arizona, is nestled in the scenic White Mountains. Known for its forested landscapes, 
cool climate, and abundant outdoor recreational opportunities, the area is a bout 10 miles (16 
kilometers) north of Show Low and accessible via Arizona State Route 77 (AZ -77). Surrounded 
by natural attractions such as White Mountain Lake and the Apache -Sitgreaves National Forest, 
this location is ideal for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers. 
 
The project, which encompasses parcel 304-21-371Q, aims to elevate property values by 
transforming underutilized land. It will feature the construction of quality, attainable, and 
aesthetically pleasing manufactured homes, rentals, self -storage facilities, a convenience style 
store, RV and camping areas, as well as storage for RVs and boats —all within a Special 
Development Zone. The new homes are designed to enhance the neighborhood's aesthetic and 
potentially increase property values. Additi onally, the development will offer amenities such as 
camping areas, short -term rentals with creek views, and walking trails, catering to community 
interests. 
 
The developers are exploring eco -friendly practices, including planting numerous trees to 
promote a greener community. Throughout the development process, updates and information 
will be shared via the project's website, social media channels, and email communications, 
ensuring that the community remains informed and engaged. 
 
TENTATIVE PLAT 
The Tentative Plat outlines the subdivision of the property into various components, including: 
 
 
● Up to 24 single-family lots (yellow). 
● Up to 133 multifamily units situated over 5 acres (orange) 
● Up to 133 manufactured homes (green) 
● 1 convenience-style store near the storage and parking areas (gray) 
● Self-storage units and parking, including RV and boat storage (gray)

<!-- page 576 -->
The property is zoned as a Special Development Zone, accommodating diverse dwelling types, 
parking areas, recreational open spaces, and other community facilities while preserving a rural 
atmosphere. 
 
The development will comprise 290 units, spanning a total project site area of 67.2 acres. 
 
 
SETBACKS 
Setbacks will be defined as part of the Master Development Plan. Each lot will feature on lot 
parking, with additional garage spaces available, eliminating the need for on street parking. The 
lots are designed with ample depth to accommodate sufficient parking within each lot. 
 
CONCLUSION 
The Rock Creek development represents a thoughtfully planned project that seeks to enhance the 
White Mountain Lakes Vista neighborhood by providing quality housing, recre ational 
opportunities, and essential amenities. With a focus on improving property values, promoting 
eco-friendly practices, and fostering community engagement, Rock Creek aims to create a 
harmonious and vibrant living environment. As the project progresse s, continuous updates and 
open communication will ensure that the community remains informed and involved in shaping 
its future. Through careful planning and a commitment to excellence, Rock Creek is poised to 
become a cornerstone of the area's growth and development.

Dear Mr. cooper,  
Please accept this document as a “Will Serve Letter” in regard to the proposed development and 
expansion of the Juniper Ridge development APN 304-21-371Q.  The property in question is 
located within the legal boundaries of the Timber Mesa Fire and Medical District (District).  
Subsequently, the development will be required to meet the minimum requirements of the 2018 
International Fire Code as adopted by the district.  District officials will have to meet with the 
members of the development team should rezoning be approved by the county and this 
requirement is understood by all parties involved, discussion on infrastructure, access, water 
systems etc. will need to be discussed. The district will issue notice of final approval upon 
completion of the proposed development.  Any changes to the proposed development must be 
approved by the district prior to construction. 
If there are any questions, please feel free to contact me for further information.

Citizen Review Plan Report  
Proposed Subdivision 
‘Rock Creek’ 
APN 304-21-371Q 
August 22, 2024 
Allen Land Development, LLC 
10356 E. Thornton Ave, Mesa, AZ 85212 
In compliance with Section 2907 - Citizen Review, we make this notice to meet compliance with 
the requirements of Section 2907 and respectfully submit the following summary;  
Attachments include: 
•Address Lists used for invitations 
•Sign-In Sheet from the meeting held 
•Copies of the invitations sent out 
•Copy of the Tentative Plat 
An invitation to a community meeting was sent to all listed Owners and Agencies on August 
6, 2024, providing relevant information and directions to the meeting site planned for 
August 22, 2024. Allen Land Development, LLC members drafted a ‘letter of notice’ with 
relevant information, inviting all property owners and agents of record, representing all 
properties within three hundred feet of our location to attend an on-site meeting where we held 
open discussions regarding our intentions.  
Here are several additional items that were presented: 
•Priority Access to New Storage Units: Community members will have the first opportunity to 
reserve new storage units. 
•New Recreational Opportunities: We are planning to add new recreational facilities and 
amenities. 
•Community Feedback Welcome: We value your input and will be seeking feedback through 
planned community meetings and a dedicated website. 
•Improving Local Infrastructure: The project will explore improvements to roadways and 
infrastructure to enhance accessibility and convenience for residents in the area. 
•Enhanced Safety Measures: New security features will be implemented to ensure a safe 
environment for everyone. 
•Better Access to Amenities: The project will improve access to local amenities, such as the 
nearby golf course, resort, and White Mountain Lake, making everyday life more enjoyable. 
•Staying Informed: Updates and information will be available through our website, social 
media channels, and email communications to keep the community informed.

<!-- page 605 -->
The Letter of Notice was drafted and submitted to Cody Cooper. Mr. Cooper replied the same 
day with approval of the drafted invitation and further supplied us with a mailing list for 
comparison to ensure full compliance. We mailed out the invitations on August 6, 2024. The 
invitations were sent in advance as required, 16 days before the August 22 Neighborhood 
Community Meeting. (See attached copies of the invitation postcard sent). 
Approximately 60 people participation. The meeting was held own-site where all interested 
parties were free to exchange information and discuss our intentions, along with opportunities for 
attended to voice concerns or questions. We presented copies of our proposed plat and gathered 
the names, phone numbers and email addresses of those in attendance. The meeting duration was 
approximately 1.5 hours. The list of attendees is attached. Each participant was provided with a 
pen, pad, and the Allen Land Development, LLC contact information including website, email 
and phone number. Complimentary water and snacks were provided. We also contacted the 
Home Owners Association of Juniper Ridge and White Mountain Lakes and encouraged staff to 
inform the entire community of the Neighborhood Community Meeting. 
A list of people in attendance is attached. Some had accompanying spouses in attendance 
who did not list their names. Summaries of the questions and concerns with answers below;  
Q1: Discussion on which local boards Rock Creek Development has been in contact with. 
A: HOA Presidents of Juniper Ridge Resort and White Mountain Lakes Vistas. 
Q2: Discussion on water, fire, sewer, medical and police concerns. 
A: We are working directly with Voyager at White Mountain Lake Water Company, Inc, White 
Mountain Sanitation, Inc and Timber Mesa Fire & Medical District and will we comply with all 
International fire codes and municipality codes required. 
Q3: Concerns were expressed related to the overall finished construction and aesthetics of the 
development. 
A: We have onboarded Vida Architects to work in alignment with Navajo County and the 
development team to enhance the overall aesthetics of the property. The goal of the development 
will be to improve and enhance what is currently existing and to bring amenities. Housing will 
be equal to or better than the current housing quality. All housing will meet or exceed current 
housing requirements and comply with current building and energy codes. 
Q4: Concerns were expressed related to wildlife.

<!-- page 606 -->
A: The development team will prioritize minimizing environmental disruption. Rock Creek 
development is committed to preserving the natural environment and are exploring options to 
mitigate any potential impacts. 
Q5: Homeowners presented concerns about maintaining an age restricted 55+ community. 
A: We will be working with Juniper Ridge Resort and White Mountain Lakes Vistas along with 
Navajo county on providing more of what is already existing in the above sub divisions.  
Q6: Discussed road way concerns and impact.  
A: A traffic impact study will be conducted to determine the necessary upgrades to ensure safe 
traffic flow. 
Q7: (Question directed to Chris Pasters from Real AZ) Does your funding come from the 
government entities or the people that you represent? 
A: Real AZ has members that pay dues. Our members pay dues, so all of the counties, the 
municipalities, the nonprofits, for profits, and the academic institutions, all pay dues, that goes to 
RealAZ. My salary is also supplemented by Navajo County. So Navajo County says we want 
economic development. As a region, we want this guy to be serving RealAZ's board. 
Q8: Discussed the groundbreaking date.  
A: We don't know when, but we will keep you all informed of our schedule. 
Q9: Discussion on deviation from original master plan. 
A: Due to updated feasibility studies and reports. 
Q10: Discussion regarding the density.  
A: We are currently working on a master plan with Navajo County that will designate the 
approved by public works. 
Q11: Homeowners expressed concern about light pollution. 
A: We would be open to communicating with the neighborhood facilitation with night sky rules 
that relate to lighting.  
Q12: Homeowners expressed concern about water retention and down flow impact to the lake, 
pollution, grading and drainage.

<!-- page 607 -->
A: We are working with our civil engineer to assist us in grading, drainage and hydrology.  
Q13: Homeowners expressed concern about the overall use of the proposed development.  
A: The goal of Rock Creek Development is to increase much needed housing with different living 
options and to promote lifestyle and healthy living. Rock Creek development will bring 
additional amenities to the local area.  
Q14: Were any of the county representatives invited to this meeting besides an independent, 
hired by the group? 
A: Multiple representatives were invited. 
We recognize the importance of keeping the community informed. We will provide timely 
updates as we gather more detailed information. A follow-up community meeting will be 
scheduled soon to discuss the results of our ongoing studies. In the interim, significant 
developments will be communicated through the contact information provided by attendees and 
on our website. 
Allen Land Development, LLC intends to work with Navajo County’s needs, continue to 
carefully consider the community preferences, and concerns, and develop based on feasibility 
reports for all good concerned while adhering to Navajo County’s requirements. 
Please note that we are considering the impact on lake views and will keep our plans adaptable to 
meet any necessary guidelines. We’re currently working on the best approach to ensure 
compliance and maintain flexibility. 
This concludes our Citizen Review Plan Report.  
Thank you for your consideration and direction. 
Bryant Aplass, Member Representative 
Allen Land Development, LLC

Dear Sirs: 
 
I am writing regarding your proposal to develop your property on Silver Creek Dr. in the White Mountain Lake area. I am 
a resident and owner at Juniper Ridge Resort. When I moved here, I understood that while the White Mountain Lake 
Vistas no longer controlled the property south of their development that it was deeded to be an over-55 community with a 
master plan indicating homes similar to the homes at the Vistas. 
 
I strongly object to the proposed changes to that Master Plan. The reasons for my objections are as follows: 
 
1. There is a Declaration of Aﬃrmative Land Use and Restrictive Covenants attached to the deed for the property which 
clearly states that “(ii) any Residential, Recreational Vehicle Lot, Vacation Rental, Common Area Recreational or 
Commercial Development that abuts or is within 100 feet of the Beneﬁciaries’ homeowner lots shall be operated as or for 
an Age-Restricted Housing Community or Resort.” 
 
2. The lots that are designated as single-family lots (20) and manufactured homes along the western boundary of the 
property on your proposed development are adjacent to or within 100 feet of homeowner lots at White Mountain Vistas. 
This must be addressed. 
 
3. Adding 300 housing units that are not age limited will radically change the atmosphere of Juniper Ridge Resort and the 
Vistas which are both over-55 communities. It will make it very diﬃcult for us to maintain the quiet and privacy that the 
communities currently provide. 
 
4. Both communities are gated to provide security for the homeowners. Adding non-over-55 housing units that are not 
gated will compromise our security because much of your development lies adjacent to our golf course. 
 
5. Adding 300 housing units to the community instead of the number in the Master Plan raises the density of the 
community to too high a level. Your plan provides no greenspace of any size (aside from our golf holes) to mitigate the 
density of the housing and instead allocates a great deal of the parcel to the storage, parking and camping areas. 
 
6. The plan for 150 manufactured homes is also problematic. It is becoming increasingly diﬃcult in this area to obtain 
homeowners insurance for park models and manufactured homes. Adding stick-
built houses as per the Master Plan makes 
more sense in this insurance environment. 
 
7. I do not believe that the addition of 150 multifamily apartments is either desirable or needed. The White Mountain 
Lake area is predominantly a summer recreation area. We have little or no infrastructure for full-time residents with no 
schools and little shopping. We are located over 10 miles from Show Low proper where most of the employment is 
located. People renting apartments are also a concern to our residents because of security concerns. 
 
8. Juniper Ridge Resort has its own RV and vehicle storage lots that can be easily expanded. They are rented to our 
residents at a very reasonable rate. Thus, they are not an asset to the community. Their location along Silver Creek Rd will 
produce a potential eyesore. And there is the potential for pollution of Silver Creek from vehicles parked in storage. 
 
9. There is no indication of how anyone will access the camping you are proposing along the Silver Creek drainage or how 
many and what kind of campsites you are proposing. Camping will further reduce the quiet, privacy and security of our 
over-55 gated communities.

<!-- page 637 -->
2
10. The addition of both the camping area and 300 more housing units raises a serious concern regarding our roads. Both 
White Mountain Lake Rd and Silver Creek Dr. are two-lane country roads with no verges. Adding 3 more egresses for 
your parcel will not increase safety. The 300 proposed housing units will increase the number of trips per day on these 
roads considerably. Camping will also increase the usage of these roads in the summer. 
 
11. There is great concern regarding the strain this proposed development will place on our water and sewer companies. 
The sewer company is especially problematic since it has been out of compliance for so long and has no approved plan for 
expansion. 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Rick and Jane Johnson 
Lot # 267 
Juniper Ridge Resort 
775-720-3480
